root.title: Convex QP Structural Taxonomy
root.top_down_role: Structural organization of convex quadratic programs with affine constraints, including representations, geometry, certificates, computational regimes, and solver-facing interfaces.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Problem statement, solver, infeasibility, polishing, and interfaces

children.title: Convex QP Model Forms
children.top_down_role: Canonical and solver-oriented representations of affine-constrained convex quadratic models.

children.title: Canonical Affine-Constraint Forms
children.top_down_role: Model organizations distinguished by equality, inequality, and variable-domain conventions.

children.title: Mixed Equality–Inequality QP
children.top_down_role: General representation with separate affine equality and inequality blocks.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}\{\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x:Ax=b,\ Gx\le h\}\) is the solution set of the mixed-form convex QP.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex QP with distinct affine equality and inequality blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(b\in\mathbb R^{m_e}\), and \(h\in\mathbb R^{m_i}\), a mixed equality–inequality convex quadratic program has the form \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\ \tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax=b,\qquad Gx\le h.\] The inequalities are interpreted componentwise. Positive semidefiniteness of \(Q\) makes the objective convex, while both constraint blocks define affine or polyhedral convex sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mixed-form convex QP minimizes a convex quadratic over separate affine equality and componentwise affine inequality blocks.
knowledge_statements.title: Mixed Equality–Inequality QP

children.title: Equality-Nonnegativity Standard-Form Interface
children.top_down_role: Standard-form organization using equalities and nonnegative variables.

children.title: Equality Constraint Block
children.top_down_role: Organization of the affine equality portion of the standard form.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The equality block defines the affine feasible set \(E=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b\}\).

notation.meaning: Affine set defined by the equality block.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality block in an equality–nonnegativity standard-form QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An equality constraint block is a system \(Ax=b\), meaning \(a_i^\top x=b_i\) for every row \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\). Its feasible set is \[E:=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b\}.\] The set \(E\) is affine when nonempty; it may be empty if the system is inconsistent. In equality–nonnegativity standard form, this block is imposed together with the separate domain restriction \(x\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The equality block is the affine system Ax=b, possibly inconsistent, imposed separately from variable-domain restrictions.
knowledge_statements.title: Equality Constraint Block

children.title: Nonnegative Variable Domain
children.top_down_role: Sign-domain structure imposed on standard-form variables.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in\mathbb R_+^n\) if and only if \(x_j\ge0\) for every \(j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\).

notation.meaning: Nonnegative orthant in n-dimensional real space.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise nonnegativity convention for standard-form decision variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The nonnegative variable domain is the closed convex cone \[\mathbb R_+^n:=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:x_j\ge0\ \text{for every}\ j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\}.\] Thus the standard-form restriction \(x\ge0\) is componentwise and includes zero. It constrains the variable domain rather than adding an equality to the equality block.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The nonnegative domain is the closed orthant consisting of vectors whose components are all at least zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonnegative Variable Domain

children.title: Equality–Nonnegativity Conversion
children.top_down_role: Structural correspondence between general affine constraints and the standard-form organization.

assumptions_latex: The original constraints are \(Ax=b\) and \(Gx\le h\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The lifted equality–nonnegativity QP has the same feasible \(x\) and the same objective values as the original QP.

notation.meaning: Positive and negative parts of the original free variable.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion using nonnegative slacks and positive–negative splitting of free variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Set \(x=x^+-x^-\), introduce \(s=h-Gx\), and require \(x^+\ge0\), \(x^-\ge0\), and \(s\ge0\). Then the mixed QP is represented as \[\min\ \tfrac12(x^+-x^-)^\top Q(x^+-x^-)+c^\top(x^+-x^-)\] subject to \[A(x^+-x^-)=b,\qquad G(x^+-x^-)+s=h.\] Projection by \(x=x^+-x^-\) maps the lifted feasible set onto the original feasible set, and the displayed objectives agree under that map.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Slack variables convert inequalities to equalities, while positive–negative splitting makes every lifted variable nonnegative without changing feasible original points or objective values.
knowledge_statements.title: Equality–Nonnegativity Conversion

children.title: Standard-Form Size Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Dimension growth and sparsity effects associated with the conversion.

knowledge_statements.title: Standard-Form Size Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact dimension and coefficient-matrix nonzero counts for the direct slack-and-split conversion, before presolve or structural sharing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the direct conversion \(x=x^+-x^-\) and \(Gx+s=h\), an original model with \(n\) free variables, \(m_e\) equality rows, and \(m_i\) inequality rows becomes a model with \(2n+m_i\) nonnegative variables and \(m_e+m_i\) equality rows. Its equality matrix is \[\begin{bmatrix}A&-A&0\\G&-G&I_{m_i}\end{bmatrix}.\] Before presolve or structural sharing, this matrix has exactly \(2\operatorname{nnz}(A)+2\operatorname{nnz}(G)+m_i\) nonzero entries, which is an increase of \(\operatorname{nnz}(A)+\operatorname{nnz}(G)+m_i\) over the original stacked matrix \(\begin{bmatrix}A\\G\end{bmatrix}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Direct standardization doubles the free-variable coefficient columns and adds one slack column per inequality, yielding 2n+m_i variables, m_e+m_i equality rows, and an exactly quantifiable increase in matrix nonzeros.
assumptions_latex: Every original variable is free and is split, and every inequality receives one slack variable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The conversion yields \(2n+m_i\) nonnegative variables, \(m_e+m_i\) equality rows, and \(2\operatorname{nnz}(A)+2\operatorname{nnz}(G)+m_i\) equality-matrix nonzeros before presolve or structural sharing.

notation.meaning: Numbers of original equality and inequality rows.
Number of nonzero entries of a matrix.

children.title: Inequality-Only QP Form
children.top_down_role: Representation in which affine equalities and variable domains are encoded through inequalities.

assumptions_latex: All affine restrictions admit a finite system of scalar inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasible set is \(\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\widetilde Gx\le\widetilde h\}\), with all comparisons componentwise.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional encoding of equalities and coordinate bounds by affine inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An inequality-only convex QP has the form \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\ \tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x\quad\text{subject to}\quad \widetilde Gx\le\widetilde h.\] A row \(a^\top x=b\) is encoded by \(a^\top x\le b\) and \(-a^\top x\le-b\). Coordinate bounds \(\ell\le x\le u\) are encoded by \(-I_nx\le-\ell\) and \(I_nx\le u\), omitting any side whose bound is infinite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inequality-only QP aggregates all affine restrictions; each equality becomes two opposite inequalities and finite variable bounds become identity rows.
knowledge_statements.title: Inequality-Only QP Form

children.title: Free-Split Variable Representation Pair
children.top_down_role: Equivalent forms produced by reorganizing unrestricted and sign-constrained variables.

children.title: Unrestricted Variable Forms
children.top_down_role: Representations that retain variables without sign restrictions.

assumptions_latex: \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) has no sign or coordinate-bound restrictions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The unrestricted domain is \(\mathbb R^n\), and every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) admits a nonnegative split representation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Free real variables before conversion to a nonnegative-variable interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An unrestricted, or free, variable vector has domain \(x\in\mathbb R^n\); no condition \(x_j\ge0\), \(x_j\le0\), or finite coordinate bound is intrinsic to that domain. It can be represented through nonnegative vectors by \[x=x^+-x^-,\qquad x^+\in\mathbb R_+^n,\qquad x^-\in\mathbb R_+^n.\] This representation is surjective onto \(\mathbb R^n\) but is generally not unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A free variable ranges over all real vectors and can be represented, nonuniquely, as the difference of two nonnegative vectors.
knowledge_statements.title: Unrestricted Variable Forms

children.title: Split-Variable Forms
children.top_down_role: Representations replacing unrestricted variables with sign-constrained components.

knowledge_statements.title: Split-Variable Forms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnegative lifted coordinates representing an unrestricted real vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A split-variable form replaces each unrestricted vector \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) by a pair \((x^+,x^-)\in\mathbb R_+^n\times\mathbb R_+^n\) and uses the reconstruction map \[T(x^+,x^-):=x^+-x^-.\] Any occurrence of \(x\) in the objective and constraints is replaced by \(T(x^+,x^-)\). The lifted representation has a nonnegative domain and is redundant because adding the same nonnegative vector to both parts leaves \(T(x^+,x^-)\) unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Split-variable form replaces one free vector by two nonnegative vectors and reconstructs the original as their difference.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The map \(T:\mathbb R_+^n\times\mathbb R_+^n\to\mathbb R^n\), defined by \(T(x^+,x^-)=x^+-x^-\), is surjective and generally noninjective.

children.title: Positive–Negative Variable Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Structural correspondence between an unrestricted variable and its signed components.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The canonical parts satisfy \(x=x^+-x^-\), \(x^+,x^-\ge0\), and \((x^+)_j(x^-)_j=0\) for every \(j\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical complementary choice among all positive–negative split representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), define componentwise \[(x^+)_j:=\max\{x_j,0\},\qquad (x^-)_j:=\max\{-x_j,0\}.\] Then \(x^+,x^-\in\mathbb R_+^n\), \(x=x^+-x^-\), and \((x^+)_j(x^-)_j=0\) for every \(j\). These complementarity relations select the unique canonical positive–negative decomposition of \(x\); an unconstrained split-variable QP representation need not impose them.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The canonical positive and negative parts reconstruct x, are componentwise nonnegative, and never have both parts positive in the same coordinate.
knowledge_statements.title: Positive–Negative Variable Decomposition

children.title: Split-Representation Size Effects
children.top_down_role: Dimension, sparsity, and degeneracy consequences of variable splitting.

assumptions_latex: Exactly \(k\) scalar variables of the original model are unrestricted.
Each unrestricted variable is replaced by one positive and one negative part.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The split model has \(k\) additional scalar variables, while each affected matrix column is replaced by a column and its negative.

notation.meaning: Number of unrestricted scalar variables being split.
Original coefficient matrix for the split variables.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact variable and column counts caused by positive–negative splitting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Replacing \(k\) unrestricted scalar variables by positive and negative parts changes those \(k\) coordinates into \(2k\) nonnegative coordinates, hence adds exactly \(k\) scalar variables. If their original linear coefficient block is \(M\), the split block is \([M\ -M]\). For a quadratic term with Hessian block \(Q\), substitution produces \[\begin{bmatrix}Q&-Q\\-Q&Q\end{bmatrix}.\] Thus the representation can duplicate nonzeros and introduces a \(k\)-dimensional null direction corresponding to equal changes in both parts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Splitting k free variables adds k coordinates, duplicates signed matrix structure, and creates redundant directions in the lifted representation.
knowledge_statements.title: Split-Representation Size Effects

children.title: OSQP Bound-Form QP
children.top_down_role: Two-sided affine-image bound representation used by OSQP and related splitting interfaces.

children.title: Row-Bound Regimes
children.top_down_role: Finite, one-sided, equality, and inactive affine-row bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Row-Bound Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: OSQP-style classification of each affine row by finite or infinite endpoints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the row-bound system \(\ell\le Ax\le u\), row \(i\) is an equality when \(\ell_i=u_i\in\mathbb R\); two-sided when \(-\infty<\ell_i<u_i<+\infty\); lower-only when \(\ell_i\in\mathbb R\) and \(u_i=+\infty\); upper-only when \(\ell_i=-\infty\) and \(u_i\in\mathbb R\); and inactive when \(\ell_i=-\infty\) and \(u_i=+\infty\). Under the admissible endpoint domains and the condition \(\ell_i\le u_i\), these regimes exhaust the possible bounds on \(a_i^\top x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each affine row is classified exhaustively as an equality, finite interval, lower-only bound, upper-only bound, or inactive row according to its admissible endpoints.
assumptions_latex: \(m,n\) are nonnegative integers and \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every row belongs to exactly one of the equality, two-sided, lower-only, upper-only, or inactive regimes according to \((\ell_i,u_i)\).

children.title: Variable Bounds as Constraint Rows
children.top_down_role: Embedding simple variable domains in the affine-row interface.

assumptions_latex: The QP row interface is \(\ell\le Ax\le u\).
Variable bounds are \(\ell^x\le x\le u^x\), with possibly infinite endpoints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Appending \(I_n\) and the bounds \((\ell^x,u^x)\) represents variable bounds exactly as affine constraint rows.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identity-row embedding of coordinate bounds in an OSQP-style bound form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given row constraints \(\ell\le Ax\le u\) and coordinate bounds \(\ell^x\le x\le u^x\), define \[\bar A:=\begin{bmatrix}A\\I_n\end{bmatrix},\qquad \bar\ell:=\begin{bmatrix}\ell\\\ell^x\end{bmatrix},\qquad \bar u:=\begin{bmatrix}u\\u^x\end{bmatrix}.\] Then \(\bar\ell\le\bar Ax\le\bar u\) holds exactly when both original systems hold. Infinite coordinate endpoints encode absent bound sides, and a fixed variable is represented by \(\ell_j^x=u_j^x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Appending identity rows embeds lower, upper, interval, and fixed-variable bounds exactly in the same affine row-bound interface.
knowledge_statements.title: Variable Bounds as Constraint Rows

children.title: Bound-Form Splitting Lift
children.top_down_role: Lifted separation of the affine image from its interval domain.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(l\le Ax\le u\) is represented exactly by \(Ax-z=0\) and \(z\in[l,u]\).

notation.meaning: Closed coordinatewise interval, allowing infinite endpoints.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex QP lift with possibly infinite row bounds.

source_refs.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The bound-form quadratic program
\[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\ \tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Px+q^{\mathsf T}x\quad\text{subject to}\quad l\le Ax\le u\]
is equivalent to
\[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n,\ z\in\mathbb R^m}\ \tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Px+q^{\mathsf T}x+\delta_{[l,u]}(z)\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax-z=0.\]
Projection of the lifted feasible set onto the \(x\)-coordinates gives exactly the original feasible set, and corresponding feasible points have identical objective values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Introduce the affine image as a new variable, constrain it to the row-bound interval, and enforce equality with the original affine map.
knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Form Splitting Lift

source_witnesses.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

children.title: Dimension-Expanding QP Lift Family
children.top_down_role: Dimension-expanding transformations exposing simple domains, separability, or alternative solver interfaces.

children.title: Inequality Slack Forms
children.top_down_role: Equality-plus-domain representations of affine inequalities.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Gx\le h\) holds if and only if some \(s\in\mathbb R_+^m\) satisfies \(Gx+s=h\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-sided affine inequalities in finite-dimensional QPs.

source_refs.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\),
\[Gx\le h\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \exists s\in\mathbb R_+^m:\ Gx+s=h.\]
The correspondence is unique for fixed \(x\), namely \(s=h-Gx\). Hence replacing \(Gx\le h\) by the equality \(Gx+s=h\) together with the domain restriction \(s\in\mathbb R_+^m\) preserves the feasible \(x\)-set and any objective depending only on \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine inequality is equivalent to an affine equality after adding its uniquely determined nonnegative slack vector.
knowledge_statements.title: Inequality Slack Forms

source_witnesses.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

children.title: Consensus Copy-Variable Lift Family
children.top_down_role: Lifted forms exposing block separability or distributed coupling.

children.title: Copy-Variable Lifts
children.top_down_role: Lifted organizations using replicated decision variables.

assumptions_latex: For \(i=1,\ldots,k\), let \(E_i\in\mathbb R^{n_i\times n}\) and let \(f_i:\mathbb R^{n_i}\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Introducing \(z_i=E_i x\) preserves the objective and the projected feasible set.

notation.meaning: Linear extraction or transformation for block i.
Local copy of the affine image.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: variable substitution by exact linear equalities
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-dimensional copies of linear images used by separable formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The composite problem
\[\min_{x\in X}\ \sum_{i=1}^k f_i(E_i x)\]
has the exact lifted representation
\[\min_{x\in X,\ z_i\in\mathbb R^{n_i}}\ \sum_{i=1}^k f_i(z_i)\quad\text{subject to}\quad z_i-E_i x=0,\quad i=1,\ldots,k.\]
For each feasible \(x\), the equalities determine a unique tuple \((z_1,\ldots,z_k)\); conversely, projecting any lifted feasible point onto \(x\) recovers an original feasible point with the same objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace repeated linear images of a shared variable by local copy variables tied to the original variable through exact equalities.
knowledge_statements.title: Copy-Variable Lifts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The copy-variable lift is mathematically precise and fits the leaf, but no inspectable source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Consensus Coupling Constraints
children.top_down_role: Equality couplings that reconcile replicated variable blocks.

assumptions_latex: Let \(\mathcal G=(V,E)\) be a connected undirected graph with oriented incidence matrix \(B\in\mathbb R^{|E|\times |V|}\).
Each node \(i\in V\) carries a copy \(z_i\in\mathbb R^n\), stacked as \(z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((B\otimes I_n)z=0\) holds exactly when \(z_1=\cdots=z_{|V|}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: nullspace characterization of a connected graph incidence matrix
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Graph-structured equality coupling among full-dimensional local copies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consensus of the local copies is imposed by
\[(B\otimes I_n)z=0.\]
Because \(\mathcal G\) is connected, \(\ker B=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf 1\}\), and therefore
\[\ker(B\otimes I_n)=\{\mathbf 1\otimes x:x\in\mathbb R^n\}.\]
Thus the coupling constraint is satisfied if and only if there exists \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) such that \(z_i=x\) for every node \(i\). Connectivity is essential; with multiple connected components, equality is enforced only within each component.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Incidence-matrix equalities force all local copies to agree exactly when the coupling graph is connected.
knowledge_statements.title: Consensus Coupling Constraints

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The connected-graph incidence characterization and connectivity boundary are correct and fit a condition record, but the claim lacks an inspectable cited source.

children.title: Block-Separability Exposure
children.top_down_role: Separable objective or constraint structure revealed by replication.

assumptions_latex: For \(i=1,\ldots,k\), let \(f_i:\mathbb R^{n_i}\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper convex functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The lifted objective and uncoupled domain are block-separable; all cross-block dependence is confined to \(Cz=d\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: separability follows directly from Cartesian products and additive objectives
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive convex blocks with linear coupling isolated by lifting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[F(z)=\sum_{i=1}^k f_i(z_i),\qquad Z=\prod_{i=1}^k\operatorname{dom}f_i.\]
Then the lifted formulation \(\min\{F(z):z\in Z,\ Cz=d\}\) exposes block separability: evaluation and subdifferentiation satisfy
\[\partial F(z)=\partial f_1(z_1)\times\cdots\times\partial f_k(z_k),\]
and minimization of \(F(z)+\sum_i g_i^{\mathsf T}z_i\) over \(Z\) decomposes into \(k\) independent block problems. Any dependence between distinct blocks occurs solely through the displayed coupling equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After lifting, the objective and domains separate by block, while a linear equality contains all interactions among blocks.
knowledge_statements.title: Block-Separability Exposure

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The separability property fits the leaf and is mathematically sound, but no source is cited. The assumptions also contain the malformed fragment \\(z=(z_1,\\\\ldots,z_k)\\), which should use \\ldots.

children.title: Lifted-Dimension Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Storage, sparsity, and system-size consequences of consensus lifting.

assumptions_latex: Consensus equalities are placed on a connected graph with incidence matrix \(B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The lift has \(kn\) scalar variables, consensus rank \((k-1)n\), and feasible consensus dimension \(n\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: rank-nullity applied to connected-graph consensus constraints
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimension accounting for full-copy consensus lifts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Stacking \(k\) copies produces \(kn\) scalar variables. Since a connected graph incidence matrix satisfies \(\operatorname{rank}B=k-1\),
\[\operatorname{rank}(B\otimes I_n)=(k-1)n,\qquad \dim\ker(B\otimes I_n)=n.\]
Thus the lift adds \((k-1)n\) variable degrees before coupling and requires the same number of independent scalar equalities to recover an \(n\)-dimensional consensus subspace. Extra graph edges add redundant equality rows but may change sparsity, conditioning, and decomposition structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full-copy consensus multiplies the variable count by the number of blocks and removes the added degrees of freedom through independent coupling equalities.
knowledge_statements.title: Lifted-Dimension Tradeoffs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The variable count, consensus rank, and nullity are correct for full copies coupled over a connected graph, but no inspectable source is supplied.

children.title: Quadratic Epigraph Lifts
children.top_down_role: Lifted objective representations used in cone-based canonicalization.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t\ge\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Px\) is equivalent to \((t,1,Rx)\in\mathcal Q_r\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct substitution into the rotated-cone definition
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rotated-cone epigraph of a positive-semidefinite quadratic form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[\mathcal Q_r=\{(a,b,y):a\ge0,\ b\ge0,\ 2ab\ge\lVert y\rVert_2^2\}.\]
For every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(t\in\mathbb R\),
\[t\ge\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Px\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad (t,1,Rx)\in\mathcal Q_r.\]
Consequently, minimizing a convex quadratic objective \(\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Px+q^{\mathsf T}x\) over any affine-conic feasible set is equivalent to minimizing \(t+q^{\mathsf T}x\) after adjoining this cone constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-semidefinite quadratic epigraph becomes one rotated second-order-cone constraint after factoring the Hessian.
knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Epigraph Lifts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The rotated-cone epigraph equivalence is correctly normalized and appropriately classified as a representation, but it has no cited source or locator.

children.title: Quadratic Curvature Representations
children.top_down_role: Storage and modeling organizations for positive-semidefinite quadratic curvature.

children.title: Explicit Symmetric-Hessian Form
children.top_down_role: Direct matrix representation of quadratic curvature.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The quadratic uses \(H=(P+P^{\mathsf T})/2\), and it is convex exactly when \(H\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional real quadratic functions represented by a symmetric Hessian.

source_refs.locator: 3.8 The GOP for Quadratic Problems with Linear Constraints p. 95

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For
\[f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Px+q^{\mathsf T}x+r,\]
set \(H=(P+P^{\mathsf T})/2\). Since \(x^{\mathsf T}(P-P^{\mathsf T})x=0\), the same function has the explicit symmetric-Hessian form
\[f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+q^{\mathsf T}x+r.\]
Moreover, \(\nabla f(x)=Hx+q\), \(\nabla^2f(x)=H\), and \(f\) is convex on \(\mathbb R^n\) if and only if \(H\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every real quadratic depends only on the symmetric part of its matrix, which is its Hessian and determines convexity.
knowledge_statements.title: Explicit Symmetric-Hessian Form

source_witnesses.locator: 3.8 The GOP for Quadratic Problems with Linear Constraints p. 95

children.title: Gram-Factor Form
children.top_down_role: Factor-based representation exposing semidefiniteness and rank structure.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\succeq0\) exactly when \(P=R^{\mathsf T}R\) for some real matrix \(R\).

notation.meaning: A real Gram factor, possibly rectangular.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: spectral factorization of a positive-semidefinite matrix
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Real finite-dimensional factorization of positive-semidefinite quadratic curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The matrix \(P\) is positive semidefinite if and only if there exist an integer \(r\ge0\) and a matrix \(R\in\mathbb R^{r\times n}\) such that
\[P=R^{\mathsf T}R.\]
Under this representation,
\[x^{\mathsf T}Px=\lVert Rx\rVert_2^2\quad\text{for every }x\in\mathbb R^n.\]
The factor can be chosen with \(r=\operatorname{rank}P\); any factor satisfying the equality obeys \(\operatorname{rank}R=\operatorname{rank}P\). Thus rectangular factors expose low-rank curvature directly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetric matrix is positive semidefinite exactly when it is a Gram matrix; the factor converts the quadratic form into a squared norm.
knowledge_statements.title: Gram-Factor Form

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Gram-factor characterization and rank statements are correct and fit the representation leaf, but no inspectable source is cited.

children.title: Least-Squares QP Form
children.top_down_role: Residual-based quadratic models and quadratic regularization.

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(L\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(\lambda\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The model is a convex QP with \(P=A^{\mathsf T}A+\lambda L^{\mathsf T}L\) and \(q=c-A^{\mathsf T}b\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear least squares with quadratic regularization and a linear term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The residual model
\[f(x)=\tfrac12\lVert Ax-b\rVert_2^2+\tfrac\lambda2\lVert Lx\rVert_2^2+c^{\mathsf T}x\]
has the QP expansion
\[f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Px+q^{\mathsf T}x+\tfrac12\lVert b\rVert_2^2,\qquad P=A^{\mathsf T}A+\lambda L^{\mathsf T}L,\quad q=c-A^{\mathsf T}b.\]
Because \(\lambda\ge0\), \(P\succeq0\), so the model is convex. The additive constant may be omitted without changing minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expanding squared residuals and quadratic regularization yields a convex QP whose Hessian is a sum of Gram matrices.
knowledge_statements.title: Least-Squares QP Form

children.title: Matrix-Free Quadratic Operator
children.top_down_role: Operator access to curvature for large structured problems.

assumptions_latex: \(P:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) is a linear self-adjoint positive-semidefinite operator.
An oracle returns \(Pv\) for any requested \(v\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The oracle suffices to evaluate \(x^{\mathsf T}Px\), compute \(Px+q\), and apply Krylov methods without storing \(P\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: quadratic evaluation and gradient follow from exact operator products
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact product-oracle representation of large positive-semidefinite curvature operators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A matrix-free representation supplies the oracle
\[\mathcal O_P(v)=Pv\]
without requiring entries or a stored factor of \(P\). For \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Px+q^{\mathsf T}x+r\), one oracle call at \(x\) gives
\[f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}\mathcal O_P(x)+q^{\mathsf T}x+r,\qquad \nabla f(x)=\mathcal O_P(x)+q.\]
Algorithms whose curvature access consists solely of products \(Pv\), including conjugate-gradient and Lanczos subroutines, can therefore operate on the exact quadratic model without explicitly materializing \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A product oracle represents the Hessian implicitly and supports exact objective, gradient, and Krylov computations without storing the matrix.
knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Free Quadratic Operator

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The product-oracle representation and its objective, gradient, and Krylov-access consequences fit the leaf, but no inspectable source is supplied.

children.title: Conic Representations of Convex QP
children.top_down_role: Cone-based reformulations of convex quadratic objectives and epigraphs.

children.title: Rotated Second-Order-Cone QP Lift
children.top_down_role: Cone lift derived from a positive-semidefinite curvature factor.

assumptions_latex: The remaining feasible set \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is representable by affine and conic constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The convex QP equals a conic linear problem with the single added constraint \((t,1,Rx)\in\mathcal Q_r\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: equivalence follows directly from the rotated-cone inequality
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full convex-QP objective canonicalization through a rotated second-order cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[\mathcal Q_r=\{(a,b,y):a\ge0,\ b\ge0,\ 2ab\ge\lVert y\rVert_2^2\}.\]
Then
\[\min_{x\in X}\ \tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Px+q^{\mathsf T}x\]
is equivalent to the conic problem
\[\min_{x\in X,\ t\in\mathbb R}\ t+q^{\mathsf T}x\quad\text{subject to}\quad (t,1,Rx)\in\mathcal Q_r.\]
For every feasible \(x\), the least feasible \(t\) is \(\tfrac12\lVert Rx\rVert_2^2=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Px\); hence both formulations have the same optimal value and the same optimal \(x\)-coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Factoring the positive-semidefinite Hessian converts a convex quadratic objective into a linear objective plus one rotated-cone constraint.
knowledge_statements.title: Rotated Second-Order-Cone QP Lift

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The full convex-QP rotated-cone lift is mathematically correct and distinct from the epigraph-only leaf, but it lacks a cited authoritative source with a locator.

children.title: Low-Rank Conic QP Lifts
children.top_down_role: Reduced-dimensional lifts derived from thin curvature factors.

assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\) has a factorization \(Q=R^\top R\) with \(R\in\mathbb R^{r\times n}\) and \(r\ll n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{epi}(q)=\{(x,t):(t,1,Rx)\in\mathcal Q_{r+2}^{\mathrm{rot}}\}\).

notation.meaning: Quadratic function whose epigraph is lifted.
Thin square-root factor of the Hessian.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact rotated-cone epigraph lift using a rank-revealing curvature factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(\mathcal Q_{r+2}^{\mathrm{rot}}=\{(u,v,w)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^r:u\ge 0,\ v\ge 0,\ 2uv\ge\lVert w\rVert_2^2\}\). For \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx=\tfrac12\lVert Rx\rVert_2^2\), its epigraph has the exact lifted representation \[ (x,t)\in\operatorname{epi}(q)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad (t,1,Rx)\in\mathcal Q_{r+2}^{\mathrm{rot}}. \] Thus the nonlinear part of the conic model has dimension \(r+2\), determined by the factor rank rather than the ambient dimension \(n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank-r Hessian factor converts the quadratic epigraph into one rotated second-order-cone constraint of dimension r+2.
knowledge_statements.title: Low-Rank Conic QP Lifts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The rotated-cone representation is mathematically correct, but no inspectable source is supplied. The assumptions also do not explicitly state that r=rank(Q) or that R has full row rank, although the dimensionality claim describes r as the factor rank.

children.title: Semidefinite QP Embeddings
children.top_down_role: Matrix-cone representations linking QP structure to semidefinite models.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: QP as a special case of semidefinite programming

assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\) and \(Q=R^\top R\) for some \(R\in\mathbb R^{r\times n}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t\ge\tfrac12x^\top Qx\) if and only if \(\begin{bmatrix}2t&(Rx)^\top\\Rx&I_r\end{bmatrix}\succeq0\).

notation.meaning: A square-root factor satisfying the displayed Gram identity.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Schur-complement embedding of a convex quadratic epigraph into a positive-semidefinite cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(t\in\mathbb R\), the convex quadratic epigraph inequality admits the exact semidefinite representation \[ t\ge\tfrac12x^\top Qx\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \begin{bmatrix}2t&(Rx)^\top\\Rx&I_r\end{bmatrix}\succeq0. \] The equivalence follows under the stated factorization because the lower-right block \(I_r\) is positive definite and its Schur complement is \(2t-\lVert Rx\rVert_2^2=2t-x^\top Qx\). Consequently, affine constraints on \(x\) may be retained unchanged while the quadratic objective or constraint is represented by a linear matrix inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A PSD quadratic epigraph is exactly an LMI obtained from any square-root factor of its Hessian.
knowledge_statements.title: Semidefinite QP Embeddings

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Schur-complement LMI is correct and the representation kind fits the container, but the record has no citation and includes proof-style Schur-complement derivation that should be removed from a knowledge statement.

children.title: Conic Dual Recovery for QP
children.top_down_role: Correspondence between QP certificates and lifted conic primal-dual solutions.

assumptions_latex: \(Q=R^\top R\succeq0\), and the displayed primal and conic-dual solutions satisfy primal feasibility, dual feasibility, stationarity, and complementarity.
The QP constraints are \(Ax=b\) and \(Gx\le h\), with inequality multiplier \(\lambda\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z=-\tfrac12Rx\) and \(Qx+c+A^\top y+G^\top\lambda=0\), together with \(\lambda_i(Gx-h)_i=0\).

notation.meaning: PSD matrix used in the lifted epigraph constraint.
Dual PSD matrix partitioned conformably with M.
Off-diagonal block of the conic dual matrix.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery through the semidefinite epigraph lift with a fixed sign convention for conic multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimizing \(t+c^\top x\) subject to \(Ax=b\), \(Gx\le h\), and \(M(x,t)=\begin{bmatrix}2t&(Rx)^\top\\Rx&I_r\end{bmatrix}\succeq0\). Write its PSD dual variable as \(S=\begin{bmatrix}\alpha&z^\top\\z&W\end{bmatrix}\succeq0\), using the Lagrangian term \(-\langle S,M(x,t)\rangle\). Conic stationarity gives \(\alpha=\tfrac12\) and \(c+A^\top y+G^\top\lambda-2R^\top z=0\). Matrix complementarity \(SM(x,t)=0\) gives \(z=-\tfrac12Rx\). Substitution recovers the QP stationarity equation \(Qx+c+A^\top y+G^\top\lambda=0\); scalar complementarity recovers \(\lambda_i(Gx-h)_i=0\) for every inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The lifted PSD dual blocks recover the original QP stationarity and complementary-slackness certificate by eliminating the off-diagonal dual block.
knowledge_statements.title: Conic Dual Recovery for QP

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated sign convention consistently recovers the original QP stationarity equation, but this specialized dual-block recovery has no source. The statement also contains derivational proof text rather than only the duality correspondence.

children.title: Convex QP Curvature Regime Family
children.top_down_role: Ambient, feasible-direction, and reduced-space curvature regimes for QPs.

children.title: Positive-Semidefinite Hessian Condition
children.top_down_role: Organizer for global convexity, equivalent curvature representations, degeneracy, and validation.

children.title: Symmetric-Part Reduction
children.top_down_role: Canonical symmetric representation of quadratic curvature.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\top Mx=x^\top Sx\) for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\); moreover, \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Mx+c^\top x+\gamma\) is convex on \(\mathbb R^n\) if and only if \(S\succeq0\), and strongly convex if and only if \(S\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional real quadratic forms; the skew-symmetric coefficient component is immaterial.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M=S+K\), where \(S=(M+M^\top)/2\) is symmetric and \(K=(M-M^\top)/2\) is skew-symmetric. For every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), \[x^\top Kx=0\quad\text{and}\quad x^\top Mx=x^\top Sx.\] Thus \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Mx+c^\top x+\gamma\) has the canonical symmetric Hessian \(S\). The function \(f\) is convex on \(\mathbb R^n\) exactly when \(S\succeq0\), and it is strongly convex on \(\mathbb R^n\) exactly when \(S\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every real quadratic form depends only on the symmetric part of its coefficient matrix, which is the canonical Hessian used for convexity and strong-convexity tests.
knowledge_statements.title: Symmetric-Part Reduction

children.title: Spectral PSD Structure
children.top_down_role: Eigenstructure-based organization of nonnegative curvature.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q\succeq0\) if and only if every eigenvalue of \(Q\) is nonnegative.

notation.meaning: Rank of Q, equal to the number of positive eigenvalues when Q is PSD.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orthogonal spectral characterization of real positive-semidefinite quadratic curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: There exist an orthogonal matrix \(U\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) and real eigenvalues \(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n\) such that \[ Q=U\Lambda U^\top,\qquad \Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n). \] The matrix satisfies \(Q\succeq0\) if and only if \(\lambda_i\ge0\) for every \(i\). In that case, writing \(u_i\) for the columns of \(U\), \(x^\top Qx=\sum_{i=1}^n\lambda_i(u_i^\top x)^2\). Its rank is the number of strictly positive eigenvalues, and its nullspace is the span of eigenvectors associated with zero eigenvalues.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetric Hessian is PSD exactly when all eigenvalues are nonnegative; positive and zero eigenmodes identify curved and flat directions.
knowledge_statements.title: Spectral PSD Structure

children.title: Factorization-Based PSD Structure
children.top_down_role: Recognition and storage of curvature through square-root and Gram factors.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q\succeq0\) if and only if \(Q=R^\top R\) for some real matrix \(R\).

notation.meaning: Gram or square-root factor of Q.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent Gram, spectral square-root, and thin-factor representations of PSD curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A real symmetric matrix \(Q\) is positive semidefinite if and only if there exists a real matrix \(R\) such that \(Q=R^\top R\). Under a spectral decomposition \(Q=U\Lambda U^\top\) with \(\Lambda\succeq0\), the symmetric square root is \(Q^{1/2}=U\Lambda^{1/2}U^\top\). If \(r=\operatorname{rank}(Q)\), retaining only positive eigenvalues yields a thin factor \(R\in\mathbb R^{r\times n}\). For every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), \[ x^\top Qx=\lVert Rx\rVert_2^2, \] so the factor stores and evaluates curvature without retaining a dense \(n\)-row square root.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: PSD curvature is equivalent to a Gram factorization, and a rank-r Hessian admits a thin r-by-n square-root factor.
knowledge_statements.title: Factorization-Based PSD Structure

children.title: Null-Curvature Structure
children.top_down_role: Flat objective directions and their interaction with affine feasibility.

assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x+\gamma\), and the nonempty feasible affine set is \(F=x_0+L\) for a linear subspace \(L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every nonzero \(d\in L\cap\ker Q\), \(f(x+td)=f(x)+t c^\top d\) for all \(x\in F\) and \(t\in\mathbb R\); if \(c^\top d=0\), the objective is constant on the feasible line, while if \(c^\top d\ne0\), the problem is unbounded below.

notation.meaning: Direction subspace of the feasible affine set.
Nonzero feasible direction with zero quadratic curvature.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonzero flat Hessian directions within an affine feasible set and their effect on existence and uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), a direction \(d\in\mathbb R^n\) has zero curvature exactly when \(d^\top Qd=0\), equivalently when \(Qd=0\). For every nonzero \(d\in L\cap\ker Q\), every \(x\in F\), and every \(t\in\mathbb R\), \[f(x+td)=f(x)+t c^\top d.\] If \(c^\top d=0\), the objective is constant along a nontrivial feasible line, so an attained minimizer cannot be unique. If \(c^\top d\ne0\), one orientation of the feasible line drives the objective to \(-\infty\), so the affine-feasible QP has no finite minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero feasible nullspace direction either creates a line of equal objective values or makes the QP unbounded below, depending on its linear slope.
knowledge_statements.title: Null-Curvature Structure

children.title: Near-PSD Validation Boundary
children.top_down_role: Numerical ambiguity near the convexity boundary.

assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\), and perturbations are measured in the spectral norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The spectral-norm ball \(\{Q+E:E\in\mathbb S^n,\ \lVert E\rVert_2<\varepsilon\}\) contains both a PSD matrix and an indefinite matrix.

notation.meaning: Bound on symmetric data or backward error.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral-norm ambiguity of exact convexity when the smallest eigenvalue lies inside the error radius.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\lambda=\lambda_{\min}(Q)\) and let \(u\) be a corresponding unit eigenvector. If \(|\lambda|<\varepsilon\), a perturbation of norm below \(\varepsilon\) can produce a positive-semidefinite matrix: when \(\lambda<0\), take \(E_+=-\lambda I\), and when \(\lambda\ge0\), take \(E_+=0\). A perturbation of norm below \(\varepsilon\) can also produce an indefinite matrix: choose \(\delta>0\) with \(|\lambda|+\delta<\varepsilon\) and, when \(\lambda\ge0\), take \(E_-=-(\lambda+\delta)uu^\top\); when \(\lambda<0\), take \(E_-=0\). Therefore a computed eigenvalue inside the error radius cannot alone certify exact positive semidefiniteness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the smallest eigenvalue is smaller in magnitude than the error bound, nearby admissible Hessians include both PSD and indefinite matrices.
knowledge_statements.title: Near-PSD Validation Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The intended ambiguity between PSD and non-PSD matrices is standard, but the record instead claims an indefinite matrix. A negative-definite Q with E=0 is non-PSD but not indefinite, and in dimension one no symmetric matrix is indefinite. The mathematical boundary must be reformulated or supplemented with dimensional and spectral hypotheses, and an inspectable perturbation source is required.

children.title: Strict-Strong Convexity Hierarchy
children.top_down_role: Distinctions among full-space, feasible-set, and quantitative curvature.

children.title: Ambient Positive Definiteness
children.top_down_role: Full-space strictly positive curvature.

assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S^n\) is the Hessian of \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x+\gamma\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q\succ0\) if and only if \(f\) is strongly convex on \(\mathbb R^n\), with maximal modulus \(\lambda_{\min}(Q)>0\).

notation.meaning: Symmetric Hessian of the quadratic objective.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full-space positive definiteness and strong convexity of a finite-dimensional quadratic function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Ambient positive definiteness means \[ d^\top Qd>0\qquad\text{for every }d\in\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}. \] For symmetric \(Q\), this is equivalent to \(\lambda_{\min}(Q)>0\) and to the existence of \(\mu>0\) such that \(Q\succeq\mu I\). Under these conditions, for all \(x,y\in\mathbb R^n\), \[ f(y)\ge f(x)+\nabla f(x)^\top(y-x)+\tfrac\mu2\lVert y-x\rVert_2^2. \] The largest admissible modulus is \(\mu=\lambda_{\min}(Q)\); hence the quadratic is strongly, and therefore strictly, convex throughout the ambient space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic has full-space strictly positive curvature exactly when its symmetric Hessian is positive definite, equivalently when its smallest eigenvalue is positive.
knowledge_statements.title: Ambient Positive Definiteness

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Positive Definiteness from Nullspace Positivity and PSD Penalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional symmetric quadratic-form criterion under which a positive-semidefinite penalty supplies curvature outside the nullspace and yields ambient positive definiteness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let P and Q be symmetric matrices of the same size. If Q\succeq 0 and x^{\mathsf T}Px>0 for every nonzero x satisfying x^{\mathsf T}Qx=0, then there exists \bar c\in\mathbb{R} such that P+cQ\succ 0 for every c>\bar c.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If P is positive definite on the nullspace of a positive-semidefinite matrix Q, then adding every sufficiently large scalar multiple of Q makes the resulting quadratic form positive definite on the entire space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\bar c\in\mathbb{R}\ \forall c>\bar c,\quad P+cQ\succ 0

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A symmetric matrix \(A\) is positive definite if and only if \(y^TAy>0\) for every nonzero vector \(y\). In particular, when \(
abla^2f(x^*)\) is symmetric, \(y^T
abla^2f(x^*)y>0\) for every \(y
eq0\) is equivalent to \(
abla^2f(x^*)\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetric matrix is positive definite exactly when its quadratic form is strictly positive in every nonzero direction. The same criterion characterizes a symmetric positive-definite Hessian.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A\succ0\iff \bigl(y^TAy>0\ \forall y\neq0\bigr).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Leading-principal-minor characterization of positive definiteness for a real symmetric matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) satisfy \(Q=Q^\top\), and define \(\Delta_k=\det Q[1{:}k,1{:}k]\) for \(k=1,\ldots,n\). Then \(Q\) is positive definite if and only if \(\Delta_k>0\) for every \(k=1,\ldots,n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A real symmetric matrix is positive definite if and only if all of its leading principal minors are positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Q\succ0\iff \Delta_k>0\quad\text{for every }k=1,\ldots,n.
knowledge_statements.title: Sylvester's criterion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent full-space strict-curvature criteria for a real symmetric matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For A\in\mathcal S^n, the following are equivalent: (i) A\succ0; (ii) x^TAx>0 for every nonzero x\in\mathbb R^n; (iii) every eigenvalue of A is strictly positive; (iv) all n leading principal minors are strictly positive; (v) if p_A(\lambda)=\lambda^n+\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}p_k\lambda^k, then (-1)^{n-k}p_k>0 for k=0,\ldots,n-1; and (vi) A=BB^T for a square nonsingular matrix B.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A real symmetric matrix is positive definite exactly when its quadratic form is positive away from the origin, its eigenvalues are positive, its leading principal minors are positive, its characteristic-polynomial coefficients strictly alternate in sign, or it has a nonsingular square Gram factor.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A\succ0\iff(\forall x\neq0)\ x^TAx>0\iff(\forall i)\ \lambda_i(A)>0\iff(\forall k=1,\ldots,n)\det A_{\{1,\ldots,k\}}>0\iff(\forall k=0,\ldots,n-1)\ (-1)^{n-k}p_k>0\iff(\exists B\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\text{ nonsingular})\ A=BB^T.

children.title: Strict Convexity on the Feasible Affine Hull
children.top_down_role: Strict curvature restricted to the effective feasible geometry.

assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty and convex, with \(\operatorname{aff}(F)=\bar x+L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The restriction \(f|_F\) is strictly convex if and only if \(d^\top Qd>0\) for every nonzero \(d\in L\).

notation.meaning: Direction space of the feasible affine hull.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict convexity relative to the affine hull of a nonempty convex feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The quadratic objective is strictly convex on \(F\) exactly when its Hessian is positive definite on the direction space of the feasible affine hull: \[ d^\top Qd>0\qquad\text{for every }d\in L\setminus\{0\}. \] Equivalently, for all distinct \(x,y\in F\) and every \(\theta\in(0,1)\), \[ f(\theta x+(1-\theta)y)<\theta f(x)+(1-\theta)f(y). \] Ambient positive definiteness is sufficient but unnecessary: \(Q\) may be singular on \(\mathbb R^n\) provided \(L\cap\ker Q=\{0\}\). Under this condition, a minimizer over \(F\), if attained, is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex quadratic is strictly convex on its feasible geometry exactly when its Hessian is positive definite on every nonzero affine-hull direction.
knowledge_statements.title: Strict Convexity on the Feasible Affine Hull

children.title: Strong-Convexity Conditioning Regimes
children.top_down_role: Quantitative curvature regimes relevant to stability and complexity.

children.title: Strong Convexity Modulus
children.top_down_role: Quantitative lower-curvature strength relevant to stability and complexity.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The maximal strong-convexity modulus of \(f\) on \(\mathbb R^n\) is \(\mu_*=\lambda_{\min}(Q)\), provided \(\lambda_{\min}(Q)>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean strong-convexity modulus for an unconstrained finite-dimensional quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A number \(\mu>0\) is a strong-convexity modulus of \(f\) on \(\mathbb R^n\) when, for every \(x,y\in\mathbb R^n\), \[ f(y)\ge f(x)+\nabla f(x)^\top(y-x)+\tfrac\mu2\lVert y-x\rVert_2^2. \] For the quadratic Hessian \(Q\), this condition is equivalent to \(Q\succeq\mu I\). Consequently, a positive modulus exists exactly when \(Q\succ0\), and the maximal modulus is \[ \mu_* = \sup\{\mu:Q\succeq\mu I\}=\lambda_{\min}(Q). \] Any \(0<\mu\le\mu_*\) is also a valid modulus.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The strong-convexity modulus is any positive lower spectral bound on the Hessian; the largest such modulus is its smallest eigenvalue.
knowledge_statements.title: Strong Convexity Modulus

children.title: Hessian Spectral Conditioning
children.top_down_role: Full-space spectral disparity in the quadratic curvature.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Euclidean spectral condition number is \(\kappa_2(Q)=\lambda_{\max}(Q)/\lambda_{\min}(Q)\ge1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean spectral conditioning of a positive-definite quadratic Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the quadratic \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x+\gamma\), the gradient \(\nabla f(x)=Qx+c\) is Lipschitz continuous in the Euclidean norm with smallest Lipschitz constant \(L=\lambda_{\max}(Q)\). Its maximal strong-convexity modulus is \(\mu=\lambda_{\min}(Q)\). The Hessian spectral condition number is therefore \[ \kappa_2(Q)=\lVert Q\rVert_2\lVert Q^{-1}\rVert_2=\frac{L}{\mu}=\frac{\lambda_{\max}(Q)}{\lambda_{\min}(Q)}. \] It equals one precisely when all eigenvalues coincide, and it diverges as the smallest eigenvalue approaches zero while the largest remains bounded away from zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a positive-definite quadratic, spectral conditioning is the ratio of gradient smoothness to strong curvature, equivalently largest to smallest Hessian eigenvalue.
knowledge_statements.title: Hessian Spectral Conditioning

children.title: Feasible-Subspace Conditioning
children.top_down_role: Conditioning restricted to directions permitted by the affine geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasible-Subspace Conditioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral conditioning of a convex quadratic restricted to the affine hull of its feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and convex, let \(L=\operatorname{span}(C-C)\) have positive dimension, and let \(Q=Q^\top\). Define the feasible-subspace curvature bounds by \[\mu_C=\min_{d\in L,\ \|d\|_2=1}d^\top Qd,\qquad L_C=\max_{d\in L,\ \|d\|_2=1}d^\top Qd.\] If \(\mu_C>0\), the feasible-subspace condition number is \(\kappa_C=L_C/\mu_C\). It measures curvature anisotropy only along directions parallel to \(\operatorname{aff}(C)\), so curvature orthogonal to that affine hull is irrelevant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The feasible-subspace condition number is the ratio of largest to smallest positive quadratic curvature along directions parallel to the feasible set.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty and convex with \(\dim\operatorname{span}(C-C)>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa_C=L_C/\mu_C\).

notation.meaning: Linear space parallel to the affine hull of the feasible set.
Smallest and largest Rayleigh quotients of Q on the feasible-direction space.

children.title: Ill-Conditioned Curvature Boundary
children.top_down_role: Near-singular quantitative-curvature regimes affecting solution sensitivity.

knowledge_statements.title: Ill-Conditioned Curvature Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of uniform positive curvature at the boundary of strongly convex quadratic models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(0<\varepsilon\leq1\), consider \(q_\varepsilon(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Q_\varepsilon x\) on \(\mathbb R^2\), where \(Q_\varepsilon=\operatorname{diag}(\varepsilon,1)\). Then \(q_\varepsilon\) is strongly convex with modulus \(\varepsilon\) and spectral condition number \(\kappa(Q_\varepsilon)=1/\varepsilon\). Hence \(\kappa(Q_\varepsilon)\to\infty\) as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\). At the boundary \(Q_0=\operatorname{diag}(0,1)\), convexity remains but strong convexity and uniqueness under arbitrary linear perturbations can fail because the first coordinate is a flat direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: As the smallest curvature approaches zero, the condition number diverges; at zero, a flat direction remains and strong convexity is lost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa(Q_\varepsilon)=\varepsilon^{-1}\to\infty\), while \(Q_0\succeq0\) but \(Q_0\not\succ0\).

notation.meaning: Ratio of largest to smallest eigenvalue.

children.title: Positive-Definite Reduced Hessian Condition
children.top_down_role: Organizer for curvature after equality elimination or active-face restriction.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Active-Set QP Step under Positive-Definite Reduced Curvature
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active-set quadratic-programming iterations for which the Hessian projected onto the current working-set null space is positive definite.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\operatorname{range}(Z_k)=\ker(\widehat A_k)\) and suppose \(Z_k^TGZ_k\succ0\); in particular, \(G\succ0\) is sufficient for this condition. Then
\[
(Z_k^TGZ_k)p_z=-Z_k^Tg_k,\qquad p_k=Z_kp_z
\]
has a unique solution, and the quadratic objective has a unique minimizer on the affine subspace defined by the working equalities. If the unit step along \(p_k\) is feasible, it reaches that restricted minimizer and a stationary point for the working equalities. Otherwise, the maximal feasible step is less than one and reaches a blocking constraint, which is then admitted to the working set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-definite projected Hessian makes the reduced Newton direction and the minimizer on the current working-set subspace unique. A feasible unit step reaches that minimizer; otherwise the step stops at the nearest blocking constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p_z=-(Z_k^TGZ_k)^{-1}Z_k^Tg_k\text{ is unique};\quad \alpha=1\text{ reaches the restricted minimizer if feasible, otherwise the maximal feasible }\alpha<1\text{ reaches a blocking constraint.}

children.title: Equality Null-Space Curvature
children.top_down_role: Curvature restricted to feasible directions of an equality system.

knowledge_statements.title: Equality Null-Space Curvature
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-definite reduced-Hessian condition for a linear equality-constrained quadratic program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x\) subject to \(Ax=b\), where \(Q=Q^\top\), and let the columns of \(Z\) form a basis of \(\ker A\). The equality null-space curvature condition is \[Z^\top QZ\succ0.\] Equivalently, \(d^\top Qd>0\) for every nonzero feasible direction \(d\in\ker A\). This condition is independent of the chosen null-space basis and makes the objective strictly convex on every nonempty affine feasible set \(\{x:Ax=b\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equality null-space curvature is positive when the quadratic form is positive on every nonzero direction preserving the equalities.
assumptions_latex: \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A\) and \(Z\) has full column rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Z^\top QZ\succ0\iff d^\top Qd>0\) for every \(d\in\ker A\setminus\{0\}\).

notation.meaning: A basis matrix for the null space of A.

children.title: Active-Face Reduced Curvature
children.top_down_role: Curvature restricted to a candidate active face.

knowledge_statements.title: Active-Face Reduced Curvature
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced-Hessian condition on directions parallel to the affine hull of a specified nonempty polyhedral face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b,\ Gx\leq h\}\), where \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(G\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(h\in\mathbb R^p\). For an index set \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,p\}\), suppose \(F_I=\{x\in P:G_Ix=h_I\}\) is a nonempty face, and define \(L_I=\operatorname{span}(F_I-F_I)\). Let \(Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be symmetric, and let the full-column-rank matrix \(Z_I\) satisfy \(\operatorname{range}(Z_I)=L_I\). The reduced curvature of \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x\), with \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), on the face is \(R_I=Z_I^\top QZ_I\). Then \(R_I\succ0\) if and only if \(d^\top Qd>0\) for every \(d\in L_I\setminus\{0\}\); this condition gives strict convexity relative to \(\operatorname{aff}(F_I)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Curvature on an active face is obtained by restricting the Hessian to the linear space parallel to that face's affine hull; positive definiteness of this restriction gives relative strict convexity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_I\succ0\iff d^\top Qd>0\) for every \(d\in L_I\setminus\{0\}\).

notation.meaning: The nonempty face selected by the active index set I.
Linear space parallel to the affine hull of the face.
Hessian reduced to the face-direction space.

children.title: Reduced-System Definiteness
children.top_down_role: Reduced curvature as the basis for definite equality-subproblem linear algebra.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-System Definiteness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive reduced curvature guarantees nonsingularity of equality-constrained KKT linear algebra.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, let \(Q=Q^\top\), and let \(Z\) span \(\ker A\). If \(Z^\top QZ\succ0\), then the saddle-point matrix \[K=\begin{pmatrix}Q&A^\top\\A&0\end{pmatrix}\] is nonsingular. Consequently, for every right-hand side \((r,s)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\), the system \(K(p,\lambda)^\top=(r,s)^\top\) has a unique solution. In null-space coordinates, its primal component is determined through the positive-definite reduced system with coefficient matrix \(Z^\top QZ\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full-row-rank equalities and a positive-definite reduced Hessian make the KKT matrix nonsingular and the equality subproblem uniquely solvable.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\det K\neq0\), so \(K(p,\lambda)^\top=(r,s)^\top\) has exactly one solution.

source_refs.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

source_witnesses.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

children.title: Reduced-Hessian Singularity Boundary
children.top_down_role: Flat feasible directions, nonuniqueness, and singular reduced systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Hessian Singularity Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Flat equality-feasible directions at the boundary of positive-definite reduced curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x+\alpha\), where \(x,c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(\alpha\in\mathbb R\), and \(Q=Q^\top\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\). Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, and let the full-column-rank matrix \(Z\) satisfy \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A\). Suppose \(R=Z^\top QZ\succeq0\) is singular. Then there is a nonzero \(d\in\ker A\) such that \(d^\top Qd=0\), and the KKT matrix \(K=\begin{pmatrix}Q&A^\top\\A&0\end{pmatrix}\) is singular. If \(x_*\) is a KKT point for minimizing \(q(x)\) subject to \(Ax=b\), with \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), then \(q(x_*+td)=q(x_*)\) for every \(t\in\mathbb R\), so the equality-constrained minimizer is not unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singular positive-semidefinite reduced Hessian produces a nonzero flat feasible direction, makes the KKT matrix singular, and yields nonunique minimizers whenever a KKT point exists.
assumptions_latex: \(Q=Q^\top\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) and \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
\(Z\) has full column rank and \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K\) is singular and \(\exists d\in\ker A\setminus\{0\}:q(x_*+td)=q(x_*)\) for every \(t\in\mathbb R\).

notation.meaning: Reduced Hessian on the equality null space.

children.title: Convex-QP Curvature Boundary
children.top_down_role: Curvature regimes that leave or only conditionally enter the convex-QP class.

children.title: Indefinite Quadratic Models
children.top_down_role: Models containing negative-curvature directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Indefinite Quadratic Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic models possessing at least one direction of strictly negative curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A quadratic model \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x+\alpha\) on \(\mathbb R^n\), with \(Q=Q^\top\), is indefinite when \(Q\) has both a negative and a positive eigenvalue. In particular, there exists \(d\neq0\) with \(d^\top Qd<0\), so \(q\) is not convex on \(\mathbb R^n\). Along that direction, \(q(x+td)=\tfrac12t^2d^\top Qd+O(t)\), and hence an unconstrained indefinite quadratic has infimum \(-\infty\). Constraints may remove or bound the negative-curvature directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An indefinite quadratic has positive and negative curvature directions; without constraints, every negative-curvature direction drives its value to negative infinity.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) has at least one negative and at least one positive eigenvalue.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q\) is nonconvex on \(\mathbb R^n\) and \(\inf_{x\in\mathbb R^n}q(x)=-\infty\).

notation.meaning: Symmetric Hessian of the quadratic model.
A direction satisfying negative quadratic curvature.

children.title: Domain-Restricted Quadratic Convexity
children.top_down_role: Curvature that is nonnegative only on restricted feasible directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Domain-Restricted Quadratic Convexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convexity characterized only on directions generated by a convex feasible domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and convex, let \(L=\operatorname{span}(C-C)\), and let \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x+\alpha\) with \(Q=Q^\top\). Then \(q\) is convex on \(C\) if and only if \[d^\top Qd\geq0\qquad\text{for every }d\in L.\] Thus \(Q\) may be indefinite on \(\mathbb R^n\) while the restricted problem remains convex, provided every negative-curvature eigendirection is excluded from the linear space parallel to \(\operatorname{aff}(C)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic is convex on a convex domain exactly when its Hessian is nonnegative on directions parallel to that domain's affine hull.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q|_C\text{ is convex}\iff d^\top Qd\geq0\) for all \(d\in\operatorname{span}(C-C)\).

notation.meaning: Linear space parallel to the affine hull of C.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The characterization is mathematically plausible and correctly scoped, but the cited locator concerns convex sets and does not specifically support the quadratic-function convexity equivalence. A locator covering convex quadratic functions or Hessian restriction to an affine hull is required.

children.title: Hidden-Convex Quadratic Models
children.top_down_role: Apparently nonconvex quadratic models recoverable through specialized reformulations.

knowledge_statements.title: Hidden-Convex Quadratic Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical hidden-convex representation of the possibly indefinite trust-region subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Q=Q^\top\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(\Delta>0\), the possibly nonconvex trust-region problem \[\min_{\|x\|_2\leq\Delta}\ \tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x\] has the same optimal value as the convex semidefinite program \[\min_{x,X}\ \tfrac12\langle Q,X\rangle+c^\top x\quad\text{subject to}\quad \operatorname{tr}(X)\leq\Delta^2,\quad \begin{pmatrix}X&x\\x^\top&1\end{pmatrix}\succeq0.\] The semidefinite program admits an optimal rank-one lift \(X=xx^\top\), so this relaxation is exact despite indefinite \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A trust-region quadratic with an indefinite Hessian has an exact convex semidefinite lifting and an optimal rank-one representative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{val}(\mathrm{TRS})=\operatorname{val}(\mathrm{SDP})\), and the SDP has an optimum satisfying \(X=xx^\top\).

notation.meaning: Lifted matrix representing the quadratic products of x.
Trace inner product between Q and X.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Exactness of the trust-region SDP relaxation and existence of an optimal rank-one lift are nontrivial claims. No source or inspectable locator is supplied.

children.title: Convex QP Problem Classes
children.top_down_role: Canonical subclasses distinguished by constraint geometry, curvature structure, and changing data.

children.title: Constraint-Geometry QP Classes
children.top_down_role: QP families organized by the geometry of their feasible sets.

children.title: Unconstrained Convex QP
children.top_down_role: Quadratic minimization without explicit constraints, including singular-curvature cases.

knowledge_statements.title: Unconstrained Convex QP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete solvability classification for an unconstrained positive-semidefinite quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x+\alpha\), where \(Q=Q^\top\succeq0\). The problem \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}q(x)\) has a minimizer if and only if \(c\in\operatorname{range}(Q)\). In that case its solution set is \[-Q^\dagger c+\ker Q,\] and its optimal value is \(\alpha-\tfrac12c^\top Q^\dagger c\). The minimizer is unique exactly when \(Q\succ0\). If \(c\notin\operatorname{range}(Q)\), then a null-space direction exposes a nonzero linear term and \(\inf q=-\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex unconstrained quadratic is solvable exactly when its linear coefficient lies in the Hessian range; singular curvature then permits multiple minimizers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{argmin}q=-Q^\dagger c+\ker Q\) when \(c\in\operatorname{range}(Q)\); otherwise \(\inf q=-\infty\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The solvability classification and pseudoinverse formulas are correct, but “Part I Convex Analysis” is not a section, theorem, definition, or page-level locator as required.

children.title: Equality-Constrained QP
children.top_down_role: Affine-subspace quadratic optimization and its reduced-space structure.

children.title: Independent-Equality QP
children.top_down_role: Equality-constrained models with an independent constraint system.

knowledge_statements.title: Independent-Equality QP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained quadratic program whose constraint rows are linearly independent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An independent-equality quadratic program has the form \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\ \tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax=b,\] where \(Q=Q^\top\) and \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) satisfies \(\operatorname{rank}(A)=m\). Thus the equality gradients are linearly independent, \(AA^\top\) is positive definite, and \(A\) maps \(\mathbb R^n\) onto \(\mathbb R^m\); consequently \(Ax=b\) is feasible for every \(b\in\mathbb R^m\). Its feasible-direction space is \(\ker A\), of dimension \(n-m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An independent-equality QP has a full-row-rank equality matrix, so every right-hand side is feasible and the feasible-direction dimension is n minus m.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(AA^\top\succ0\), \(\operatorname{range}(A)=\mathbb R^m\), and \(\dim\ker A=n-m\).

children.title: Rank-Deficient Equality QP
children.top_down_role: Models with redundant or inconsistent equality descriptions.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Deficient Equality QP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility and multiplier degeneracy when equality rows are linearly dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimizing \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x\) subject to \(Ax=b\), where \(x,c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(Q=Q^\top\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(\operatorname{rank}(A)<m\). The equalities are feasible if and only if \(b\in\operatorname{range}(A)\). When feasible, redundant equality rows can be removed without changing the feasible set. Furthermore, \(\ker A^\top\neq\{0\}\). Hence, if \((x,\lambda)\) satisfies \(Qx+c+A^\top\lambda=0\) and \(Ax=b\), then \((x,\lambda+w)\) satisfies the same KKT equations for every \(w\in\ker A^\top\). Thus equality multipliers are nonunique whenever they exist, even when the primal minimizer is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank-deficient equalities are feasible exactly when the right-hand side belongs to the constraint-matrix range; when feasible, redundant rows cause nonunique equality multipliers whenever KKT multipliers exist.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ax=b\) is feasible iff \(b\in\operatorname{range}(A)\); if a KKT multiplier \(\lambda\) exists, then \(\lambda+w\) is also a multiplier for every \(w\in\ker A^\top\).

notation.meaning: Nonzero space of multiplier perturbations invisible to stationarity.

children.title: Null-Space-Parameterized QP
children.top_down_role: Equality-constrained models represented in feasible affine coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Null-Space-Parameterized QP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact null-space reduction of a feasible equality-constrained convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\). Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\tfrac12x^TQx+c^Tx\) subject to \(Ax=b\), where \(Q=Q^T\succeq0\) and the equations are consistent. Choose \(x_p\in\mathbb R^n\) with \(Ax_p=b\), set \(k=n-\operatorname{rank}(A)\), and let the columns of \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times k}\) form a basis of \(\ker A\). Every feasible point has a unique representation \(x=x_p+Zz\) with \(z\in\mathbb R^k\). Substitution gives the equivalent unconstrained problem \[\min_{z\in\mathbb R^k}\;\tfrac12z^T(Z^TQZ)z+(Qx_p+c)^TZz,\] up to the constant \(\tfrac12x_p^TQx_p+c^Tx_p\). If \(z^*\) solves the reduced problem, then \(x^*=x_p+Zz^*\) solves the original problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible equality-constrained convex QP is represented exactly as an unconstrained QP in coordinates spanning the null space of its equality matrix.
assumptions_latex: \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A\) and \(Z\) has full column rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^*=x_p+Zz^*\), where \(z^*\) solves the reduced QP.

notation.meaning: A particular solution of the equality constraints.
Dimension of the null space of A.

children.title: Box QP
children.top_down_role: QP over a finite or partially finite Cartesian box.

knowledge_statements.title: Box QP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex quadratic optimization over coordinatewise lower and upper bounds, including infinite endpoints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A box QP is a problem \\[\\min_{x\\in\\mathbb R^n}\\;q(x):=\\tfrac12x^TQx+c^Tx \\quad\\text{subject to}\\quad \\ell_i\\le x_i\\le u_i,\\ i=1,\\ldots,n,\\] where \\(Q=Q^T\\succeq0\\), \\(\\ell_i\\in\\mathbb R\\cup\\{-\\infty\\}\\), \\(u_i\\in\\mathbb R\\cup\\{+\\infty\\}\\), and \\(\\ell_i\\le u_i\\). The feasible set is the Cartesian product \\(B=\\prod_{i=1}^n[\\ell_i,u_i]\\), with the usual interpretation for infinite endpoints; it is a finite box when every endpoint is finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A box QP minimizes a convex quadratic over independent coordinate intervals, whose endpoints may be finite or infinite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \\(B=\\prod_{i=1}^n[\\ell_i,u_i]\\) is the feasible box.

children.title: One-Sided Bound QP
children.top_down_role: Nonnegative-variable and individually one-sided bound variants.

knowledge_statements.title: One-Sided Bound QP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex QPs in which each constrained coordinate has only a lower or only an upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A one-sided bound QP minimizes \\(q(x)=\\tfrac12x^TQx+c^Tx\\), with \\(Q=Q^T\\succeq0\\), over constraints chosen coordinatewise from \\(x_i\\ge\\ell_i\\), \\(x_i\\le u_i\\), or no bound. Its feasible set can be written \\(C=\\{x:Lx\\ge L\\ell,\\ Ux\\le Uu\\}\\), where \\(L\\) and \\(U\\) select disjoint coordinate sets. The nonnegative-variable QP is the special case \\(C=\\mathbb R_+^n\\), obtained by imposing \\(x_i\\ge0\\) on every coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each constrained variable has a lower bound or an upper bound, but not both; nonnegative QPs are the canonical special case.
assumptions_latex: The coordinate sets selected by \\(L\\) and \\(U\\) are disjoint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasible region is a Cartesian product of rays and free lines.

notation.meaning: Coordinate-selection matrices for lower- and upper-bounded variables.
