children.title: Free–Active Variable Geometry
children.top_down_role: Face structure induced by free variables and active bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Free–Active Variable Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Face representation of a nondegenerate box using active lower, active upper, and free coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \\(B=\\{x\\in\\mathbb R^n:\\ell\\le x\\le u\\}\\) with \\(\\ell_i<u_i\\). For \\(x\\in B\\), define \\(I_L(x)=\\{i:x_i=\\ell_i\\}\\), \\(I_U(x)=\\{i:x_i=u_i\\}\\), and \\(F(x)=\\{1,\\ldots,n\\}\\setminus(I_L(x)\\cup I_U(x))\\). The relative interior of the unique minimal face containing \\(x\\) consists of points \\(y\\) satisfying \\(y_i=\\ell_i\\) on \\(I_L(x)\\), \\(y_i=u_i\\) on \\(I_U(x)\\), and \\(\\ell_i<y_i<u_i\\) on \\(F(x)\\). Its tangent space is \\(\\{d:d_i=0\\text{ on }I_L(x)\\cup I_U(x)\\}\\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Active bounds fix coordinates on a box face, while free coordinates parameterize its relative interior and tangent space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Free coordinates span the tangent space of the minimal face containing \\(x\\).

notation.meaning: Indices active at lower and upper bounds.

children.title: Bound-QP Stationarity Certificates
children.top_down_role: Projected, normal-cone, and complementarity certificate views for bound constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-QP Stationarity Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent first-order certificates for a differentiable convex quadratic over a finite box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \\(q(x)=\\tfrac12x^TQx+c^Tx\\), \\(Q\\succeq0\\), and \\(B=\\{x:\\ell\\le x\\le u\\}\\), a feasible point \\(x^*\\) is optimal exactly when any—and hence all—of the following hold: \\(0\\in Qx^*+c+N_B(x^*)\\); \\(x^*=\\Pi_B(x^*-\\alpha(Qx^*+c))\\) for any \\(\\alpha>0\\); or there exist \\(\\lambda^L,\\lambda^U\\ge0\\) such that \\(Qx^*+c-\\lambda^L+\\lambda^U=0\\), \\(\\lambda_i^L(x_i^*-\\ell_i)=0\\), and \\(\\lambda_i^U(u_i-x_i^*)=0\\). Each displayed condition is a verifiable stationarity certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normal-cone inclusion, a zero projected-gradient residual, and complementary bound multipliers are equivalent optimality certificates for a convex box QP.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each displayed stationarity condition is necessary and sufficient for global optimality of \\(x^*\\).

notation.meaning: Convex-analysis normal cone of the box at x.

children.title: General Polyhedral QP
children.top_down_role: Convex quadratic optimization over an arbitrary polyhedron.

knowledge_statements.title: General Polyhedral QP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex quadratic minimization over a nonempty polyhedron given by linear equalities and inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A general polyhedral convex QP has the form \\[\\min_{x\\in\\mathbb R^n}\\;\\tfrac12x^TQx+c^Tx \\quad\\text{subject to}\\quad Ax=b,\\;Gx\\le h,\\] where \\(Q=Q^T\\succeq0\\) and the polyhedron \\(P=\\{x:Ax=b,\\ Gx\\le h\\}\\) is nonempty. The representation permits redundant constraints, rank-deficient equality matrices, unbounded polyhedra, and the absence of either equality or inequality rows. Convexity ensures that every local minimizer is global, although existence requires the objective to attain its infimum on \\(P\\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A general polyhedral QP minimizes a convex quadratic over any nonempty set described by finitely many linear equalities and inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The problem is convex, and every local minimizer is globally optimal.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Positive-Definite Quadratic Program with Linear Inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The strictly convex specialization of a polyhedral quadratic program and its interior-minimizer characterization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Cx\le d\}\) and \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^TAx+b^Tx+c\), where \(A=A^T\succ0\), \(b\in\mathbb R^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R\), \(C\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(d\in\mathbb R^m\). The problem \(\min_{x\in F}q(x)\) is a positive-definite quadratic program with linear inequalities. If a minimizer \(x^*\) lies in \(\operatorname{int}F\), no inequality is active and \(Ax^*+b=0\), so \(x^*=-A^{-1}b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-definite quadratic objective minimized subject to linear inequalities is a polyhedral quadratic program. If its minimizer is an interior feasible point, no constraint is active and the minimizer equals the unconstrained minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^*\in\operatorname{int}F\;\Longrightarrow\;Ax^*+b=0,\quad x^*=-A^{-1}b,\quad\text{and no inequality is active at }x^*.

children.title: Structured Polyhedral QP

knowledge_statements.title: Structured Polyhedral QP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedral QPs whose constraint representation has exploitable simplex, network, product, or block structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A structured polyhedral QP is \\(\\min_{x\\in P}\\tfrac12x^TQx+c^Tx\\), with \\(Q\\succeq0\\), where the polyhedron \\(P\\) has an explicit structure enabling specialized projection or linear algebra. Representative forms include the simplex \\(P=\\{x\\ge0:\\mathbf1^Tx=\\tau\\}\\), a network-flow polyhedron \\(P=\\{x:B x=d,\\ell\\le x\\le u\\}\\) with node-arc incidence matrix \\(B\\), and a Cartesian product \\(P=P_1\\times\\cdots\\times P_k\\). The designation concerns the algebraic representation of \\(P\\), not a different convexity condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This class retains identifiable simplex, network, product, or block structure that supports specialized projections or linear-system operations.
assumptions_latex: \\(P\\) is a nonempty polyhedron with an explicitly specified structural representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The model is a general polyhedral QP with additional exploitable constraint structure.

notation.meaning: Node-arc incidence matrix in the network-flow example.

children.title: Curvature-Structure QP Classes
children.top_down_role: QP families organized by algebraic structure in the quadratic term.

children.title: Strictly Convex QP
children.top_down_role: QP with uniqueness-supporting curvature on the relevant feasible geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Strictly Convex QP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict curvature is imposed along every nonzero chord of the convex feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \\(C\\subseteq\\mathbb R^n\\) be nonempty and convex, and let \\(q(x)=\\tfrac12x^TQx+c^Tx\\) with \\(Q=Q^T\\succeq0\\). The QP \\(\\min_{x\\in C}q(x)\\) is strictly convex on its feasible geometry precisely when \\[(x-y)^TQ(x-y)>0\\quad\\text{for every distinct }x,y\\in C.\\] Under this condition, \\(q\\) is strictly convex on \\(C\\), so the QP has at most one minimizer. The stronger condition \\(Q\\succ0\\) guarantees this property for every convex feasible set containing more than one point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex QP is strictly convex on its feasible set when every nonzero feasible chord has positive quadratic curvature, implying at most one minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Positive curvature on every nonzero feasible chord implies uniqueness whenever a minimizer exists.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The feasible-chord curvature condition is precise, the uniqueness conclusion is appropriately conditional on existence, and condition fits the stated role. No source is supplied for this nontrivial characterization.

children.title: Singular Semidefinite QP
children.top_down_role: Convex QP with flat directions and potentially nonunique solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Singular Semidefinite QP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex quadratic optimization with a positive-semidefinite but singular curvature matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A singular semidefinite QP is \\(\\min_{x\\in C}q(x)\\), where \\(q(x)=\\tfrac12x^TQx+c^Tx\\), \\(C\\subseteq\\mathbb R^n\\) is convex, and \\(Q=Q^T\\succeq0\\) is singular. Every nonzero \\(d\\in\\ker Q\\) is a flat-curvature direction, since \\(d^TQd=0\\). If two minimizers differ by such a feasible direction, convexity makes their connecting segment optimal; hence solutions may be nonunique. Singularity alone neither guarantees nonuniqueness nor guarantees attainment, because constraints and the linear term can remove or expose flat directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singular semidefinite QP has zero-curvature directions; these can create nonunique optima or affect attainment, depending on constraints and the linear term.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The objective is convex but not globally strictly convex on \\(\\mathbb R^n\\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition correctly distinguishes singular positive-semidefinite curvature from nonuniqueness and attainment, and it fits the terminal class. No inspectable source is supplied.

children.title: Separable Diagonal-Curvature QP Class
children.top_down_role: Coordinate-separable curvature with coupling determined by constraints.

children.title: Diagonal Curvature QP
children.top_down_role: QP instances whose quadratic curvature is diagonal in the chosen coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Diagonal Curvature QP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex QP whose Hessian is diagonal in the stated coordinate system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A diagonal-curvature QP has objective \\[q(x)=\\tfrac12x^TDx+c^Tx=\\sum_{i=1}^n\\left(\\tfrac12d_i x_i^2+c_i x_i\\right),\\] where \\(D=\\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\\ldots,d_n)\\) and \\(d_i\\ge0\\). It minimizes \\(q\\) over a specified convex feasible set \\(C\\). Diagonality eliminates quadratic cross-terms from the objective, but it does not by itself make the optimization problem coordinatewise separable: constraints defining \\(C\\) may still couple several variables. Positive diagonal entries make the objective strictly convex on \\(\\mathbb R^n\\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Hessian is diagonal and the objective is a sum of one-variable quadratics, although constraints may still couple coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The objective contains no quadratic cross-terms and is convex.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition correctly identifies diagonal curvature, absence of quadratic cross-terms, and possible constraint coupling. No inspectable authoritative source is supplied.

children.title: Objective Separability
children.top_down_role: Coordinate-wise decomposition of the quadratic objective.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective Separability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive separability induced by diagonal quadratic curvature and a coordinatewise linear term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \\(D=\\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\\ldots,d_n)\\), the quadratic objective \\(q(x)=\\tfrac12x^TDx+c^Tx\\) is additively separable: \\[q(x)=\\sum_{i=1}^n q_i(x_i),\\qquad q_i(t)=\\tfrac12d_i t^2+c_i t.\\] Consequently, its gradient is coordinatewise, \\(\\nabla_iq(x)=d_i x_i+c_i\\), and its Hessian has no off-diagonal interactions. This property concerns only the objective; independent minimization of the functions \\(q_i\\) is valid when the feasible set also factors into coordinate sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Diagonal curvature makes the objective a sum of scalar quadratics, but independent optimization additionally requires a product-form feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \\(q(x)=\\sum_{i=1}^n q_i(x_i)\\) with \\(q_i(t)=\\tfrac12d_i t^2+c_i t\\).

notation.meaning: Scalar objective component for coordinate i.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The additive decomposition and coordinatewise gradient are correct, and property is the appropriate content kind. The distinction between objective separability and problem decomposition is also appropriate, but no source is supplied.

children.title: Constraint-Induced Coordinate Coupling
children.top_down_role: Loss of full separability through shared affine constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Induced Coordinate Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of coordinatewise decomposition caused by a nonproduct feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \\(\\min_{x\\in C}\\sum_{i=1}^n q_i(x_i)\\). The constraints induce coordinate coupling when \\(C\\) is not representable as a Cartesian product \\(C_1\\times\\cdots\\times C_n\\) of coordinate sets. For example, a row \\(a^Tx=b\\) with at least two nonzero entries links the corresponding coordinates even when every \\(q_i\\) is scalar. In that case, independently minimizing each \\(q_i\\) over its coordinate projection need not produce a feasible or optimal point. If \\(C=\\prod_iC_i\\), then the problem decomposes exactly into the scalar problems \\(\\min_{t\\in C_i}q_i(t)\\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A separable objective remains coupled when feasibility is not a Cartesian product; product constraints are exactly the coordinate-decoupled regime.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Coordinatewise minimization is generally invalid when \\(C\\neq\\prod_iC_i\\), and exact when \\(C=\\prod_iC_i\\).

notation.meaning: Feasible set for coordinate i in a product representation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The product-feasible-set sufficiency claim is standard, while the use of every nonproduct feasible set as an exact definition of coordinate coupling requires careful qualification for degenerate objectives or redundant representations. No authoritative source is supplied to settle the intended scope.

children.title: Coordinate-Decoupled Regime
children.top_down_role: Instances retaining coordinate separation across both objective and feasible geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate-Decoupled Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact coordinate decomposition of a convex QP, including both objective and feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A convex quadratic program is in the coordinate-decoupled regime when it can be written as 
\[\min_{x\in X}\ \sum_{i=1}^{n}\left(\tfrac12 d_i x_i^2+c_i x_i\right),\qquad X=\prod_{i=1}^{n}X_i,\]
where each \(d_i\ge 0\) and each \(X_i\subseteq\mathbb R\) is a nonempty polyhedron. Its optimal set equals 
\[\prod_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname*{argmin}_{t\in X_i}\left(\tfrac12 d_i t^2+c_i t\right),\]
provided every scalar subproblem attains its minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A diagonal-curvature QP is coordinate-decoupled when its feasible set is Cartesian; it then reduces exactly to independent scalar convex quadratic problems.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\sum_i(\tfrac12d_ix_i^2+c_ix_i)=\prod_i\operatorname*{argmin}_{t\in X_i}(\tfrac12d_it^2+c_it)\)

notation.meaning: Diagonal curvature coefficient of coordinate i.
One-dimensional feasible set for coordinate i.

children.title: Block-Structured QP
children.top_down_role: Block-diagonal, bordered, or loosely coupled curvature and constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Structured QP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural definition based on a fixed partition and sparse block interactions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a partition \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_p)\), a convex QP 
\[\min_x\ \tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+c^{\mathsf T}x\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax\le b\]
is block-structured when \(H\succeq0\) and the conformal block matrices \(H_{ij}\) and column blocks \(A_i\) admit a specified sparse interaction pattern. The block-interaction graph has vertices \(1,\ldots,p\) and an edge \(i\!-\!j\) whenever \(H_{ij}\ne0\) or some constraint row contains nonzero coefficients in both \(A_i\) and \(A_j\). Block-diagonal, bordered, and loosely coupled QPs correspond to particular forms of this graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block-structured QP has variables partitioned into blocks whose curvature and constraint interactions follow a specified sparse graph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The nonzero cross-block curvature and shared constraint rows determine the block-interaction graph.

notation.meaning: Curvature block coupling variable blocks i and j.
Constraint-matrix columns belonging to block i.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: block sparsity is conventionally represented by a variable-interaction graph
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The graph-based definition fits the block-structured QP container, but the terminology and treatment of bordered or loosely coupled structures require an authoritative source.

children.title: Low-Rank Curvature Update Family
children.top_down_role: Curvature structure supporting compact storage and update formulas.

children.title: Low-Rank Curvature QP
children.top_down_role: QP instances with compact low-rank quadratic curvature.

knowledge_statements.title: Low-Rank Curvature QP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex QP whose Hessian has rank much smaller than the variable dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A low-rank curvature QP is a convex quadratic program of the form 
\[\min_{x\in P}\ \tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+c^{\mathsf T}x,\qquad H=UU^{\mathsf T},\]
where \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is polyhedral, \(U\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\), and \(r\ll n\). Thus \(H\succeq0\), \(\operatorname{rank}(H)\le r\), and the quadratic term satisfies \(x^{\mathsf T}Hx=\lVert U^{\mathsf T}x\rVert_2^2\). Curvature is therefore confined to \(\operatorname{range}(U)\), while directions in \(\ker(U^{\mathsf T})\) have zero quadratic curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Hessian factors through a much smaller matrix, so quadratic curvature acts only on a low-dimensional subspace.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H=UU^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\), \(\operatorname{rank}(H)\le r\), and \(x^{\mathsf T}Hx=\lVert U^{\mathsf T}x\rVert_2^2\).

notation.meaning: Factor width and upper bound on Hessian rank.

children.title: Low-Rank-Updated Curvature
children.top_down_role: QP sequences whose curvature changes through compact-rank modifications.

knowledge_statements.title: Low-Rank-Updated Curvature
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A base convex curvature matrix modified through a compact symmetric update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A curvature matrix has a rank-\(r\) symmetric update representation when 
\[H=H_0+USU^{\mathsf T},\]
where \(H_0=H_0^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(U\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\), and \(S=S^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^{r\times r}\). The update has rank at most \(r\). It defines convex QP curvature precisely when \(H\succeq0\); the sufficient conditions \(H_0\succeq0\) and \(S\succeq0\) guarantee this, although they are not necessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Low-rank-updated curvature is a symmetric base Hessian plus a compact symmetric correction whose rank is at most the factor width.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}(H-H_0)\le r\), and \(H_0\succeq0,\ S\succeq0\) imply \(H\succeq0\).

notation.meaning: Compact factors defining the symmetric update.

children.title: Compact Curvature Storage
children.top_down_role: Storage structures enabled by low-rank representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Compact Curvature Storage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Storage representation for a symmetric low-rank update of a structured base matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For 
\[H=H_0+USU^{\mathsf T},\qquad U\in\mathbb R^{n\times r},\quad S=S^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^{r\times r},\]
the update is stored by \(U\) and the upper triangle of \(S\), requiring \(nr+r(r+1)/2\) scalars in addition to the representation of \(H_0\). A matrix-vector product can be evaluated without forming \(H\) by 
\[Hv=H_0v+U\bigl(S(U^{\mathsf T}v)\bigr).\]
When multiplication by \(H_0\) costs \(T_0(n)\), this evaluation costs \(T_0(n)+O(nr+r^2)\) arithmetic operations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Store the low-rank factors instead of a dense Hessian; matrix-vector products then use the base operator and compact factors.
assumptions_latex: A representation or operator for \(H_0\) is available
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The additional storage is \(nr+r(r+1)/2\), and \(Hv\) costs \(T_0(n)+O(nr+r^2)\).

notation.meaning: Arithmetic cost of multiplying a vector by the base matrix.

children.title: Update-Sensitive Linear Algebra
children.top_down_role: Factorization reuse and system-structure consequences of compact updates.

knowledge_statements.title: Update-Sensitive Linear Algebra
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inverse action under a low-rank update via the Sherman–Morrison–Woodbury identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H=H_0+USU^{\mathsf T}\), where \(H_0\) and \(S\) are nonsingular. If \(S^{-1}+U^{\mathsf T}H_0^{-1}U\) is nonsingular, then \(H\) is nonsingular and 
\[H^{-1}=H_0^{-1}-H_0^{-1}U\left(S^{-1}+U^{\mathsf T}H_0^{-1}U\right)^{-1}U^{\mathsf T}H_0^{-1}.\]
Consequently, solving with the updated matrix can reuse solves with \(H_0\) and requires an additional dense solve of dimension \(r\), without forming or refactorizing a dense \(n\times n\) matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The inverse of a low-rank-updated matrix is computed from base-matrix solves and one small dense system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed Sherman–Morrison–Woodbury representation of \(H^{-1}\) holds.

notation.meaning: Base matrix whose solves are reusable.
Factors of the low-rank symmetric update.

children.title: Parametric QP Sequence Family

children.title: Parametric Convex QP
children.top_down_role: QP with parameter-dependent objective, bounds, or right-hand sides.

knowledge_statements.title: Parametric Convex QP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex QP with affine parameter dependence in objective and constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A parametric convex QP is a family indexed by \(\theta\in\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^q\) of the form 
\[V(\theta)=\inf_x\left\{\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+(c+C\theta)^{\mathsf T}x: Ax\le b+B\theta,\ Ex=e+F\theta\right\},\]
where \(H=H^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\) is independent of \(\theta\). The feasible-set mapping is \(P(\theta)=\{x:Ax\le b+B\theta,\ Ex=e+F\theta\}\), and the solution mapping is \(X^*(\theta)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in P(\theta)}\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+(c+C\theta)^{\mathsf T}x\), possibly empty or set-valued.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A parametric convex QP is a convex quadratic optimization family whose linear objective and constraint data depend affinely on parameters.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The family is described by the value mapping \(V\), feasible-set mapping \(P\), and solution mapping \(X^*\).

notation.meaning: Optimal value, with extended-real value when infeasible or unbounded.
Set of minimizers at the specified parameter.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: affine-data parametric QP is a standard finite-dimensional model
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Multiparametric QP Regions
children.top_down_role: Parameter-space regions associated with stable optimal active sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiparametric QP Regions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Critical regions defined by stability of an optimal active-set description.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a parametric QP with inequality index set \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\), the critical region associated with \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\) is 
\[\mathcal R_I=\left\{\theta\in\Theta:\text{there exist }x\in X^*(\theta),\ \lambda\ge0\text{ satisfying the KKT conditions, with }I=\{i:a_i^{\mathsf T}x=b_i+B_i\theta\}\right\}.\]
A full-dimensional subset on which a nondegenerate optimizer has the same active set is a stable active-set region. Under positive-definite curvature and linear independence with strict complementarity, its optimizer and multipliers are affine functions of \(\theta\), and the region is polyhedral.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A critical region collects parameters sharing an optimal active set; under nondegeneracy, the optimizer is affine there and the region is polyhedral.
assumptions_latex: The QP data depend affinely on \(\theta\)
For the final claim, \(H\succ0\), LICQ, and strict complementarity hold on the region
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: On each nondegenerate stable region, \(x^*(\theta)\) and the active multipliers are affine in \(\theta\), and the region is polyhedral.

notation.meaning: Parameter region associated with active set I.
Optimal solution set at parameter theta.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The critical-region and piecewise-affine claims are plausible, but their exact regularity hypotheses require authoritative support. The rows denoted by a_i and B_i should also be introduced explicitly.

children.title: Repeated-Solve QP Sequences
children.top_down_role: Slowly changing models supporting warm starts and cached linear algebra.

knowledge_statements.title: Repeated-Solve QP Sequences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequence model for related QPs with reusable structure or numerical state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A repeated-solve QP sequence is a family 
\[\mathcal Q_k:\quad\min_{x\in P_k}\ \tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}H_kx+c_k^{\mathsf T}x,\qquad H_k\succeq0,\quad k=0,1,\ldots,\]
whose successive instances retain identified reusable structure, such as a fixed sparsity pattern, unchanged constraint matrix, low-rank curvature modification, or small changes in vectors and bounds. A warm start for \(\mathcal Q_{k+1}\) consists of a primal-dual iterate or working set produced for \(\mathcal Q_k\); cached linear algebra consists of symbolic factorizations or numerical factors that remain valid under the specified data changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A repeated-solve sequence contains related convex QPs whose prior iterates, active sets, or matrix factorizations can initialize subsequent solves.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Successive instances expose explicitly identified solver state or matrix structure for reuse.

notation.meaning: Polyhedral feasible set of the kth instance.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: warm starts and factorization reuse define the repeated-solve computational regime
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The sequence model fits the leaf and makes no unsupported performance guarantee, but its defining reuse criteria and terminology lack an inspectable source.

children.title: Feasible-to-Solution Geometry Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Polyhedral feasibility, active faces, recession behavior, and solution-set structure.

children.title: Polyhedral Feasible Geometry
children.top_down_role: Geometric structures governing feasible motion and active constraints.

children.title: Effective Affine Hull
children.top_down_role: Affine geometry determining the effective dimension of the QP.

knowledge_statements.title: Effective Affine Hull
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine hull and effective dimension of a nonempty polyhedral feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b\}\ne\varnothing\), and define the index set of inequalities tight throughout \(P\) by 
\[I_P=\{i:a_i^{\mathsf T}x=b_i\text{ for every }x\in P\}.\]
Then 
\[\operatorname{aff}(P)=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:A_{I_P}x=b_{I_P}\}.\]
For any \(\bar x\in P\), equivalently \(\operatorname{aff}(P)=\bar x+\ker(A_{I_P})\). Hence the effective dimension of the QP feasible geometry is \(\dim(P)=n-\operatorname{rank}(A_{I_P})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The affine hull is determined by inequalities that are equalities everywhere on the feasible polyhedron; their rank gives its effective dimension.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{aff}(P)=\bar x+\ker(A_{I_P})\) and \(\dim(P)=n-\operatorname{rank}(A_{I_P})\).

notation.meaning: Indices of inequalities tight at every feasible point.

children.title: Face-Active-Set Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Correspondence between active constraint patterns and polyhedral faces.

children.title: Polyhedral Faces
children.top_down_role: Face structure within the affine feasible polyhedron.

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Faces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exposed-face definition specialized to a nonempty convex polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty polyhedron. A nonempty subset \(F\subseteq P\) is a face of \(P\) when there exist \(a\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(\beta\in\mathbb R\) such that 
\[a^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta\quad\text{for every }x\in P,\qquad F=\{x\in P:a^{\mathsf T}x=\beta\}.\]
Equivalently, \(F\) is the maximizer set of a linear functional over \(P\), provided that maximum is finite and attained. The choice \(a=0\), \(\beta=0\) gives the improper face \(F=P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polyhedral face is the intersection of the polyhedron with one of its supporting hyperplanes, including the whole polyhedron as an improper face.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F=P\cap\{x:a^{\mathsf T}x=\beta\}\) for a valid inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le\beta\) of \(P\).

notation.meaning: A valid supporting inequality for P.

children.title: Active-Constraint Patterns
children.top_down_role: Constraint-index patterns active at feasible points.

knowledge_statements.title: Active-Constraint Patterns
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise pattern of tight inequalities in a fixed polyhedral representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a represented polyhedron \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b\}\) and a point \(x\in P\), the active-constraint pattern is 
\[I(x)=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}:a_i^{\mathsf T}x=b_i\}.\]
The inactive pattern is its complement, for which \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x<b_i\). This pattern depends on the chosen inequality representation: redundant or duplicated inequalities can alter \(I(x)\) without changing \(P\). Points in the relative interior of the same face have the same active pattern after constraints active everywhere on \(P\) are retained consistently.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The active pattern lists inequalities tight at a feasible point; it is representation-dependent and constant on the relative interior of each face.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I(x)=\{i:a_i^{\mathsf T}x=b_i\}\), with all remaining represented inequalities strict at \(x\).

notation.meaning: Indices of inequalities active at x.

children.title: Face–Active-Set Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Navigation between geometric faces and their active-constraint representations.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F=\{y\in P:A_i y=b_i\ \forall i\in I(F)\}\) and, for every \(x\in P\), \(x\in\operatorname{relint}F\iff I(x)=I(F)\).

notation.meaning: Indices of inequalities active at x.
Indices active at every point of the face F.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed active patterns represent faces of a finite-dimensional polyhedron, including redundant inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b,\ Ex=f\}\), and let \(I(x)=\{i:A_i x=b_i\}\) for \(x\in P\). For every nonempty face \(F\) of \(P\), define \(I(F)=\{i:A_i y=b_i\text{ for every }y\in F\}\). Then \[F=\{y\in P:A_i y=b_i\text{ for all }i\in I(F)\}.\] Moreover, for every \(x\in P\), \(x\in\operatorname{relint}F\) if and only if \(I(x)=I(F)\). Consequently, each face has a unique maximal active pattern, although smaller inequality subsets may define the same face when the representation is redundant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each polyhedral face is determined by the inequalities active throughout it. Its relative-interior points, and only those feasible points, share its unique maximal active pattern, though redundant constraint subsets may represent the same face.
knowledge_statements.title: Face–Active-Set Correspondence

children.title: Degenerate Active Representations
children.top_down_role: Redundant or nonunique active patterns representing the same face.

knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Active Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Degeneracy here means nonuniqueness of constraint subsets representing one polyhedral face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b,\ Ex=f\}\) and let \(F\) be a nonempty face. A subset \(J\subseteq I(F)\) represents \(F\) when \[F=\{x\in P:A_jx=b_j\text{ for every }j\in J\}.\] The active representation of \(F\) is called degenerate when two distinct subsets \(J_1,J_2\subseteq I(F)\) both represent \(F\). This occurs through redundant active equalities; nevertheless, \(I(F)\), the set of all inequalities active throughout \(F\), remains the unique maximal representing pattern.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An active representation is degenerate when distinct subsets of active inequalities define the same face. The full set of inequalities active throughout that face remains uniquely maximal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\) is degenerately represented iff \(\exists J_1\ne J_2\subseteq I(F)\) with \(F=\{x\in P:A_jx=b_j\ \forall j\in J_k\}\) for \(k\in\{1,2\}\).

notation.meaning: A subset of active inequalities used to represent F.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the intended leaf if degeneracy is expressly being used for nonunique constraint-subset representations. However, that terminology is not standard enough to attribute to the cited generic polyhedral-sets section without inspecting support for this exact sense, including the assertion about redundant active equalities. A source specifically establishing or defining this usage is required.

children.title: Tangent-Normal Cone Duality
children.top_down_role: Feasible-direction and supporting-normal geometry used by QP certificates.

children.title: Tangent Cones
children.top_down_role: Local feasible-direction geometry at points or faces.

knowledge_statements.title: Tangent Cones
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bouligand tangent cone specialized to a polyhedron described by equalities and inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a closed set \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and \(x\in C\), its tangent cone is \[T_C(x)=\left\{d:\exists x_k\in C,\ t_k\downarrow0,\ \frac{x_k-x}{t_k}\to d\right\}.\] If \(P=\{z:Az\le b,\ Ez=f\}\) is polyhedral and \(I(x)=\{i:A_ix=b_i\}\), then the cone is closed and has the exact linearized representation \[T_P(x)=\{d\in\mathbb R^n:A_i d\le0\ \forall i\in I(x),\ Ed=0\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The tangent cone contains all limiting first-order feasible displacements. For a polyhedron it is exactly described by homogeneous equalities and the inequalities active at the base point.
assumptions_latex: For the explicit formula, \(C=P\) is polyhedral.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_P(x)=\{d:A_i d\le0\ \forall i\in I(x),\ Ed=0\}\).

notation.meaning: Bouligand tangent cone of C at x.

children.title: Normal Cones
children.top_down_role: Supporting-normal geometry associated with feasible points or faces.

assumptions_latex: For the explicit polyhedral formula, \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(E\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), and \(f\in\mathbb R^p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_C(x)=T_C(x)^\circ\), with \(N_P(x)=\{A_{I(x)}^{\mathsf T}\lambda+E^{\mathsf T}\mu:\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^{|I(x)|},\ \mu\in\mathbb R^p\}\) when \(C=P\).

notation.meaning: Convex normal cone of C at x.
Negative polar of the cone K.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex-analytic normal cone and its polar relationship with the tangent cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a closed convex set \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) and \(x\in C\), define \[N_C(x)=\{v\in\mathbb R^n:\langle v,y-x\rangle\le0\ \forall y\in C\}.\] Then \(N_C(x)=T_C(x)^\circ\), where \(K^\circ=\{v\in\mathbb R^n:\langle v,d\rangle\le0\ \forall d\in K\}\). If \(C=P=\{y\in\mathbb R^n:Ay\le b,\ Ey=f\}\), with \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(E\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), \(f\in\mathbb R^p\), and \(I(x)=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}:A_i x=b_i\}\), then \[N_P(x)=\{A_{I(x)}^{\mathsf T}\lambda+E^{\mathsf T}\mu:\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^{|I(x)|},\ \mu\in\mathbb R^p\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The normal cone consists of supporting normals at a point and is the negative polar of the tangent cone. For a polyhedron it is generated by nonnegative combinations of active inequality normals together with arbitrary combinations of equality normals.
knowledge_statements.title: Normal Cones

children.title: Feasible-Direction Geometry
children.top_down_role: Directional structure available for local movement within the feasible set.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasible-Direction Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact feasible-direction and tangent-cone representations for a polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in P\), define the feasible-direction cone by \[D_P(x)=\{d:\exists\varepsilon>0\text{ such that }x+td\in P\ \forall t\in[0,\varepsilon]\}.\] If \(P=\{z\in\mathbb R^n:Az\le b,\ Ez=f\}\), then \[D_P(x)=T_P(x)=\{d:A_i d\le0\ \forall i\in I(x),\ Ed=0\}.\] Thus every tangent direction to a polyhedron is realized by a sufficiently short feasible line segment, a property that need not hold for arbitrary closed sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a polyhedral point, feasible directions equal tangent directions and satisfy the homogeneous linearization of precisely the active constraints and all equality constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_P(x)=T_P(x)=\{d:A_i d\le0\ \forall i\in I(x),\ Ed=0\}\).

notation.meaning: Cone of directions feasible for a short segment from x.
Tangent cone of P at x.

children.title: Supporting-Normal Certificates
children.top_down_role: Use of normal geometry in convex-QP optimality certification.

knowledge_statements.title: Supporting-Normal Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order global optimality certificate for a differentiable convex quadratic over a polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\) with \(Q\succeq0\), and let \(P=\{x:Ax\le b,\ Ex=f\}\). A feasible point \(x^*\) minimizes \(q\) over \(P\) if and only if \[-\nabla q(x^*)\in N_P(x^*).\] Equivalently, there exist \(\lambda\ge0\) and \(\mu\) such that \[Qx^*+c+A^{\mathsf T}\lambda+E^{\mathsf T}\mu=0,\qquad \lambda_i(A_ix^*-b_i)=0\ \forall i.\] These finite equalities and inequalities constitute a directly checkable supporting-normal certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point solves the convex QP exactly when the negative gradient is a supporting normal. Active nonnegative multipliers provide a finite certificate through stationarity and complementarity.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a nonempty polyhedron and \(x^*\in P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in P}q(x)\iff-\nabla q(x^*)\in N_P(x^*)\).

notation.meaning: Normal cone of P at the candidate point.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate is mathematically correct and the certificate content kind fits the terminal container. However, the only citation is to a section on polars and does not specifically locate the convex optimality condition or its KKT multiplier form. Source uncertainty therefore concerns support for the exact certificate, not its formulation.

children.title: Recession Structure
children.top_down_role: Unbounded feasible directions and their interaction with quadratic curvature.

knowledge_statements.title: Recession Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedral recession directions and the quadratic objective restricted to their rays.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b,\ Ex=f\}\) be nonempty. Its recession cone is \[P^\infty=\{d:x+td\in P\ \forall x\in P,\ \forall t\ge0\}=\{d:Ad\le0,\ Ed=0\}.\] For \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\) and any \(x\in P\), \[q(x+td)=q(x)+t(Qx+c)^{\mathsf T}d+\tfrac12t^2d^{\mathsf T}Qd.\] If \(Q\succeq0\), then \(d^{\mathsf T}Qd=0\) implies \(Qd=0\); hence a direction satisfying \(Qd=0\) and \(c^{\mathsf T}d<0\) makes the objective tend to \(-\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The recession cone is obtained by homogenizing the polyhedral constraints. Along its rays, quadratic curvature dominates unless it vanishes; a negative remaining linear slope then certifies unboundedness below.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P^\infty=\{d:Ad\le0,\ Ed=0\}\), and \(d\in P^\infty,\ Qd=0,\ c^{\mathsf T}d<0\Rightarrow\inf_{x\in P}q(x)=-\infty\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The recession-cone formula, ray expansion, and stated sufficient unboundedness certificate are correct and fit the topic. The cited polyhedral-sets section may support the recession cone, but no source locator supports the quadratic-curvature interaction or the unbounded-objective conclusion. A specific QP recession result is required.

children.title: Solution-Set Structure
children.top_down_role: Existence, uniqueness, multiplicity, and optimal-face geometry.

children.title: Attained-Optimum Regimes
children.top_down_role: Geometric regimes supporting existence of an optimal solution.

knowledge_statements.title: Attained-Optimum Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Frank–Wolfe attainment criterion for a convex quadratic on a polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty polyhedron and let \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\) with \(Q\succeq0\). The following are equivalent: \[(i)\quad \inf_{x\in P}q(x)>-\infty;\qquad (ii)\quad \nexists d\in P^\infty\text{ with }Qd=0\text{ and }c^{\mathsf T}d<0.\] Whenever these conditions hold, there exists \(x^*\in P\) satisfying \(q(x^*)=\inf_{x\in P}q(x)\). Thus boundedness below already implies attainment for a convex quadratic over a nonempty polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex quadratic over a nonempty polyhedron attains its infimum whenever it is bounded below. Boundedness fails exactly when a recession direction has zero curvature and negative linear slope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x\in P}q(x)>-\infty\iff\nexists d\in P^\infty:\ Qd=0,\ c^{\mathsf T}d<0\), and finiteness implies attainment.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem content kind is appropriate, and the finite-dimensional convex-QP attainment and recession characterization are stated precisely. Because no source is cited for the nontrivial Frank–Wolfe attainment theorem or the claimed equivalence, the record requires an authoritative theorem or section locator.

children.title: Unique-Solution Regimes
children.top_down_role: Curvature and feasible-geometry combinations that isolate the minimizer.

knowledge_statements.title: Unique-Solution Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact displacement criterion and a curvature-based sufficient regime for uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^*\) minimize \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\) over a convex polyhedron \(P\), where \(Q\succeq0\). Then \(x^*\) is the unique minimizer if and only if every nonzero \(d\) with \(x^*+d\in P\) satisfies \[(Qx^*+c)^{\mathsf T}d+\tfrac12d^{\mathsf T}Qd>0.\] In particular, uniqueness holds for every linear term \(c\) whenever \[d^{\mathsf T}Qd>0\quad\forall d\in\operatorname{lin}(P-P)\setminus\{0\},\] because the objective is then strictly convex on the affine hull of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A minimizer is unique exactly when every other feasible displacement strictly increases the quadratic. Positive-definite curvature on the feasible affine hull guarantees this regime for every linear term.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a nonempty convex polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^*\text{ is unique}\iff (Qx^*+c)^{\mathsf T}d+\tfrac12d^{\mathsf T}Qd>0\) for every \(0\ne d\) with \(x^*+d\in P\).

notation.meaning: Direction space parallel to the affine hull of P.
A displacement from the candidate minimizer.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact feasible-displacement criterion is correct, and positive definiteness on the direction space parallel to the affine hull is a valid sufficient regime for uniqueness. The condition content kind fits the leaf, but the record has no source for either characterization.

children.title: Optimal-Face Multiplicity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Flat feasible directions and faces supporting nonunique minimizers.

children.title: Optimal Face Geometry
children.top_down_role: Faces or face subsets supporting attained optimal values.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimal Face Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation of the minimizer set through a supporting face and the quadratic nullspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^*\) minimize \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\) over a polyhedron \(P\), with \(Q\succeq0\), and set \(g=Qx^*+c\). The set \[H=\{y\in P:g^{\mathsf T}(y-x^*)=0\}\] is the exposed face of \(P\) supported by \(g\). The complete minimizer set is \[M=\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in P}q(y)=H\cap(x^*+\ker Q).\] Thus \(M\) is a polyhedron contained in an exposed face, but it need not itself be a face of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The minimizers are precisely the points in the gradient-supported face whose displacement lies in the quadratic nullspace. Their set is polyhedral but need not be a face of the feasible polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in P}q(y)=\{y\in P:g^{\mathsf T}(y-x^*)=0\}\cap(x^*+\ker Q)\).

notation.meaning: Gradient of the quadratic at x-star.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The supporting-face and nullspace representation is mathematically consistent and appropriately classified as a representation. In particular, optimality gives a nonnegative gradient slope on P, while positive semidefiniteness identifies zero quadratic displacement with the kernel. No source is supplied for this nontrivial complete minimizer-set formula.

children.title: Nonunique Minimizer Sets
children.top_down_role: Solution sets containing multiple primal minimizers.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonunique Minimizer Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact null-curvature characterization of multiple minimizers in a convex quadratic program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^*\) minimize \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\) over a convex polyhedron \(P\), where \(Q\succeq0\), and let \(g=Qx^*+c\). A distinct point \(y=x^*+d\in P\) is also optimal if and only if \[Qd=0\qquad\text{and}\qquad g^{\mathsf T}d=0.\] Hence the minimizer is nonunique exactly when such a nonzero feasible displacement exists. In that case every point \(x^*+td\) with \(t\in[0,1]\) is optimal, and the entire minimizer set is convex and polyhedral.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiple minimizers exist exactly when a nonzero feasible displacement has zero quadratic curvature and zero first-order slope. The segment joining any two minimizers is entirely optimal.
assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a nonempty convex polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^*+d\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in P}q(x)\iff x^*+d\in P,\ Qd=0,\ g^{\mathsf T}d=0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property correctly characterizes another minimizer by zero gradient slope and a displacement in the kernel of the positive-semidefinite Hessian. Its plain and LaTeX statements agree and the content kind fits the leaf, but no supporting source or locator is provided.

children.title: Flat Optimal Directions
children.top_down_role: Feasible directions along which the objective remains optimal.

knowledge_statements.title: Flat Optimal Directions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local flat directions at a convex-QP minimizer and their relation to other minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^*\) minimize \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\) over a polyhedron \(P\), with \(Q\succeq0\), and let \(g=Qx^*+c\). Define \[K^*(x^*)=T_P(x^*)\cap\ker Q\cap\{d:g^{\mathsf T}d=0\}.\] For every \(d\in K^*(x^*)\), there exists \(\varepsilon>0\) such that \(x^*+td\in P\) and \(q(x^*+td)=q(x^*)\) for all \(t\in[0,\varepsilon]\). Conversely, if \(y\) is any minimizer, then \(y-x^*\in K^*(x^*)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Flat optimal directions are tangent directions with zero curvature and zero gradient slope. They generate short optimal segments, and every displacement between minimizers is such a direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K^*(x^*)=T_P(x^*)\cap\ker Q\cap g^\perp\), and every \(d\in K^*(x^*)\) generates a locally optimal segment.

notation.meaning: Cone of flat optimal directions at x-star.
Tangent cone of P at x-star.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The flat-direction cone and both directional claims are correct for a polyhedron, since every tangent direction is realized by a short feasible segment. The property content kind fits the leaf, but the full local characterization and converse have no cited source.

children.title: Unique-to-Multiple Solution Boundary
children.top_down_role: Structural transition between isolated and nonisolated minimizers.

knowledge_statements.title: Unique-to-Multiple Solution Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes loss of uniqueness at a minimizer of a convex quadratic over a polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty polyhedron, let \(Q\succeq0\), and define \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\). If \(x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x)\), then \(x^\star\) is the unique minimizer exactly when no nonzero \(d\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfies \(x^\star+d\in C\), \(Qd=0\), and \((Qx^\star+c)^{\mathsf T}d=0\). Thus the transition to multiple solutions occurs precisely when a feasible displacement enters both the null space of the quadratic curvature and the zero directional-derivative subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniqueness is lost exactly when a nonzero feasible displacement has zero quadratic curvature and zero first-order change at an optimal point.
assumptions_latex: C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ is a nonempty polyhedron}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^\star\text{ is nonunique}\iff\exists d\ne0:\ x^\star+d\in C,\ Qd=0,\ (Qx^\star+c)^{\mathsf T}d=0

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role and mathematical statement are appropriate, but the cited geometric-structure section does not specifically establish the stated convex-QP uniqueness criterion. An authoritative locator for uniqueness of minimizers of a positive-semidefinite quadratic over a polyhedron is required.

children.title: Unbounded-Objective Regimes
children.top_down_role: Recession structures preventing a finite optimum.

knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded-Objective Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact recession-direction criterion for a convex quadratic objective on a nonempty polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty polyhedron and \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\) with \(Q\succeq0\). The value \(\inf_{x\in C}f(x)\) equals \(-\infty\) if and only if there exists \(d\in\operatorname{rec}(C)\) such that \(Qd=0\) and \(c^{\mathsf T}d<0\). For every \(x\in C\), such a direction gives \(x+td\in C\) and \(f(x+td)=f(x)+t c^{\mathsf T}d\) for all \(t\ge0\), producing unbounded descent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex polyhedral QP is unbounded below exactly when a recession direction has zero quadratic curvature and a strictly negative linear cost.
assumptions_latex: C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ is a nonempty polyhedron}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf_{x\in C}f(x)=-\infty\iff\exists d\in\operatorname{rec}(C):Qd=0,\ c^{\mathsf T}d<0

notation.meaning: recession cone of the feasible polyhedron

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The recession-direction characterization is mathematically standard and fits the unbounded-objective terminal, but no source is supplied. A specific theorem, section, or page supporting both directions of the equivalence is required.

children.title: Convex QP Certificate System
children.top_down_role: Certificate structures for optimality, infeasibility, unboundedness, and perturbation behavior.

children.title: KKT Certificate Families for Convex QP
children.top_down_role: Optimality certificates organized by constraint representation and geometric interpretation.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Section 16.4: Optimality Conditions for Inequality-Constrained Problems

children.title: Equality-QP KKT Certificates
children.top_down_role: Primal-dual certificates for affine-subspace QPs.

knowledge_statements.title: Equality-QP KKT Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient certificate for a convex QP over an affine subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_x\{\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b\}\), where \(Q\succeq0\) and the affine constraints are feasible. A vector \(x^\star\) is globally optimal if and only if there exists \(y^\star\) satisfying \(Ax^\star=b\) and \(Qx^\star+c+A^{\mathsf T}y^\star=0\). Hence the pair \((x^\star,y^\star)\) is a finite, directly verifiable certificate: feasibility checks the affine constraint, while stationarity certifies that no feasible direction decreases the convex quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal feasibility and Lagrangian stationarity form a necessary and sufficient optimality certificate for an equality-constrained convex QP.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{Ax=b}f(x)\iff\exists y^\star:\ Ax^\star=b,\ Qx^\star+c+A^{\mathsf T}y^\star=0

children.title: Polyhedral-QP KKT Certificates
children.top_down_role: Multiplier and complementarity certificates for general affine inequalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral-QP KKT Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier certificate for a convex QP with affine inequality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_x\{\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\le b\}\) with \(Q\succeq0\) and a nonempty feasible set. A vector \(x^\star\) is globally optimal if and only if there exists \(\lambda^\star\ge0\) such that \(Ax^\star\le b\), \(Qx^\star+c+A^{\mathsf T}\lambda^\star=0\), and \(\lambda_i^\star(a_i^{\mathsf T}x^\star-b_i)=0\) for every row \(i\). These primal feasibility, dual feasibility, stationarity, and complementarity relations constitute a verifiable KKT certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a polyhedral convex QP, feasibility, nonnegative multipliers, stationarity, and complementary slackness exactly certify global optimality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^\star\text{ is optimal}\iff\exists\lambda^\star\ge0\text{ satisfying primal feasibility, stationarity, and complementarity}

notation.meaning: row i of the constraint matrix

children.title: Bound-QP KKT Certificates
children.top_down_role: Sign-partitioned certificates specialized to variable bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-QP KKT Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sign-partitioned optimality certificate for a convex QP with finite componentwise bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_x\{\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x:\ell\le x\le u\}\), where \(Q\succeq0\) and \(\ell\le u\) are finite. A feasible \(x^\star\) is globally optimal if and only if there exist \(\alpha^\star,\beta^\star\ge0\) such that \(Qx^\star+c-\alpha^\star+\beta^\star=0\), \(\alpha_i^\star(x_i^\star-\ell_i)=0\), and \(\beta_i^\star(u_i-x_i^\star)=0\) for every \(i\). The lower- and upper-bound multipliers therefore give a directly checkable certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lower- and upper-bound multipliers certify a bound-constrained convex QP through feasibility, signed stationarity, and complementary slackness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^\star\text{ is optimal}\iff\exists\alpha^\star,\beta^\star\ge0\text{ satisfying the displayed bound KKT system}

children.title: Normal-Cone QP Certificates
children.top_down_role: Geometric consolidation of stationarity and polyhedral constraint effects.

knowledge_statements.title: Normal-Cone QP Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate-free first-order certificate for convex quadratic minimization over a closed convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let \(Q\succeq0\), and define \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\). For \(x^\star\in C\), global optimality is equivalent to \(0\in Qx^\star+c+N_C(x^\star)\), or equivalently \(-(Qx^\star+c)\in N_C(x^\star)\), where \(N_C(x^\star)=\{v:v^{\mathsf T}(z-x^\star)\le0\text{ for all }z\in C\}\). Membership in this normal cone consolidates stationarity and all active constraint effects into one geometric certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point solves a convex QP exactly when the negative objective gradient belongs to the feasible set's normal cone.
assumptions_latex: C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ is nonempty, closed, and convex}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x)\iff0\in Qx^\star+c+N_C(x^\star)

notation.meaning: convex-analytic normal cone to C at x

children.title: Equality-Constrained QP Dual
children.top_down_role: Dual organization for affine-subspace quadratic models.

knowledge_statements.title: Equality-Constrained QP Dual
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pseudoinverse form of the Lagrange dual for a positive-semidefinite equality-constrained QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the primal problem \(\inf\{\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b\}\) with \(Q\succeq0\), define \(v(y)=c+A^{\mathsf T}y\). Its Lagrange dual is \[\sup_y\left\{-\tfrac12v(y)^{\mathsf T}Q^\dagger v(y)-b^{\mathsf T}y:v(y)\in\operatorname{range}(Q)\right\}.\] If the primal feasible set is nonempty and its optimal value is finite, primal and dual optima are attained and their values agree. The range constraint is exactly the condition under which minimizing the Lagrangian over \(x\) has a finite value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The equality-QP dual maximizes a pseudoinverse quadratic subject to a range condition; feasibility and finite primal value yield attainment and zero gap.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p^\star=d^\star,\quad d^\star=\max_{v(y)\in\operatorname{range}(Q)}\{-\tfrac12v(y)^{\mathsf T}Q^\dagger v(y)-b^{\mathsf T}y\}

knowledge_statements.title: Inequality-Constrained QP Dual
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier dual for a convex quadratic program with affine inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\inf\{\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\le b\}\) with \(Q\succeq0\), put \(v(\lambda)=c+A^{\mathsf T}\lambda\). The Lagrange dual is \[\sup_{\lambda\ge0}\left\{-\tfrac12v(\lambda)^{\mathsf T}Q^\dagger v(\lambda)-b^{\mathsf T}\lambda:v(\lambda)\in\operatorname{range}(Q)\right\}.\] If the polyhedral feasible set is nonempty and the primal value is finite, the primal and dual optima are attained and equal. Optimal pairs satisfy the polyhedral-QP KKT certificate, including complementarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The inequality-QP dual is a concave pseudoinverse quadratic over nonnegative multipliers with a range constraint, and finite feasible convex QPs have zero gap.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p^\star=d^\star,\quad d^\star=\max_{\lambda\ge0,\ v(\lambda)\in\operatorname{range}(Q)}\{-\tfrac12v(\lambda)^{\mathsf T}Q^\dagger v(\lambda)-b^{\mathsf T}\lambda\}

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Form QP Dual
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual representation for convex QPs with finite two-sided affine row bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\inf\{\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x:\ell\le Ax\le u\}\), where \(Q\succeq0\) and \(\ell,u\) are finite, assign multipliers \(\alpha,\beta\ge0\) to \(\ell-Ax\le0\) and \(Ax-u\le0\). With \(v(\alpha,\beta)=c+A^{\mathsf T}(\beta-\alpha)\), the dual is \[\sup_{\alpha,\beta\ge0}\left\{-\tfrac12v^{\mathsf T}Q^\dagger v+\ell^{\mathsf T}\alpha-u^{\mathsf T}\beta:v\in\operatorname{range}(Q)\right\}.\] A nonempty feasible set and finite primal value imply attainment and equality of primal and dual values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two-sided row bounds yield separate nonnegative lower and upper multipliers in a concave pseudoinverse-quadratic dual with a range condition.
assumptions_latex: \{x:\ell\le Ax\le u\}\ne\varnothing\text{ and the primal value is finite}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p^\star=\max_{\alpha,\beta\ge0,\ v\in\operatorname{range}(Q)}\{-\tfrac12v^{\mathsf T}Q^\dagger v+\ell^{\mathsf T}\alpha-u^{\mathsf T}\beta\}

notation.meaning: c+A-transpose times the signed multiplier difference

children.title: Conic-Lifted QP Dual

knowledge_statements.title: Conic-Lifted QP Dual
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard cone duality applied to a rotated-second-order-cone lift of convex quadratic curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Factor \(Q=R^{\mathsf T}R\) and encode \(t\ge\tfrac12\lVert Rx\rVert_2^2\) by \((t,1,Rx)\in\mathcal Q_r\), where \(\mathcal Q_r=\{(u,v,w):u,v\ge0,\ 2uv\ge\lVert w\rVert_2^2\}\). After collecting this relation and all affine constraints as \(Mz=h\) with \(z\in K\), the lifted QP has form \(\inf\{g^{\mathsf T}z:Mz=h,\ z\in K\}\). Its conic dual is \[\sup_y\{h^{\mathsf T}y:g-M^{\mathsf T}y\in K^*\}.\] If either side is strictly feasible and has finite value, the optimal values agree; under standard closedness conditions the opposite optimum is attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rotated-cone epigraph converts a convex QP into conic form, whose dual uses an affine equation in the dual cone.
assumptions_latex: K\text{ is the closed product cone induced by the lift}
\text{one conic side is strictly feasible with finite value}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf\{g^{\mathsf T}z:Mz=h,\ z\in K\}=\sup\{h^{\mathsf T}y:g-M^{\mathsf T}y\in K^*\}

notation.meaning: dual cone of the lifted product cone

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Regularity Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedral constraints admit exact normal-cone multipliers without a separate constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b\}\) be nonempty and let \(I(x)=\{i:a_i^{\mathsf T}x=b_i\}\). For every \(x\in C\), \[N_C(x)=\{A^{\mathsf T}\lambda:\lambda\ge0,\ \lambda_i(a_i^{\mathsf T}x-b_i)=0\text{ for all }i\}.\] Consequently, for any differentiable convex objective, and in particular any convex quadratic, the normal-cone optimality condition is equivalent to a KKT multiplier system at every minimizer. No Slater point or linear-independence assumption is required solely to obtain multiplier existence for affine inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polyhedron's normal cone is generated by active constraint normals, so convex-QP minimizers possess KKT multipliers without Slater or independence assumptions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_C(x)=\{A^{\mathsf T}\lambda:\lambda\ge0,\ \lambda_i(a_i^{\mathsf T}x-b_i)=0\ \forall i\}

notation.meaning: active inequality index set at x

children.title: Saddle-Point Structure
children.top_down_role: Primal-dual optimality viewed through the quadratic Lagrangian.

knowledge_statements.title: Saddle-Point Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between convex-QP KKT pairs and saddle points of the quadratic Lagrangian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\) with \(Q\succeq0\) and constraints \(Ax\le b\), define \(L(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}(Ax-b)\) for \(\lambda\ge0\). A pair \((x^\star,\lambda^\star)\) satisfies the polyhedral-QP KKT system if and only if it is a Lagrangian saddle point: \[L(x^\star,\lambda)\le L(x^\star,\lambda^\star)\le L(x,\lambda^\star)\quad\text{for all }x\in\mathbb R^n,\ \lambda\ge0.\] Every such pair is primal-dual optimal and has zero duality gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex-QP primal-multiplier pair satisfies KKT exactly when it is a saddle point of the Lagrangian, implying primal-dual optimality and zero gap.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (x^\star,\lambda^\star)\text{ is KKT}\iff L(x^\star,\lambda)\le L(x^\star,\lambda^\star)\le L(x,\lambda^\star)\ \forall x,\lambda\ge0

children.title: Zero-Duality-Gap Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Duality-Gap Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Slater regime for a convex QP with affine equalities and inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(G\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), and \(h\in\mathbb R^p\). Define \(p^\star=\inf\{\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x:Ax=b,\ Gx\le h\}\), \(L(x,y,\lambda)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x+y^\top(Ax-b)+\lambda^\top(Gx-h)\), and \(d^\star=\sup_{y\in\mathbb R^m,\,\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^p}\inf_{x\in\mathbb R^n}L(x,y,\lambda)\). If \(p^\star\in\mathbb R\) and there exists \(\bar x\in\mathbb R^n\) with \(A\bar x=b\) and \(G\bar x<h\), then \(p^\star=d^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite-dimensional convex QP with finite primal value, strict feasibility of all affine inequalities relative to the affine equalities guarantees equality of the primal and Lagrange-dual values.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(G\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), and \(h\in\mathbb R^p\).
There exists \(\bar x\in\mathbb R^n\) such that \(A\bar x=b\) and \(G\bar x<h\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p^\star=d^\star\).

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier Existence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Slater-sufficient existence of KKT multipliers at an attained convex-QP optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(G\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), and \(h\in\mathbb R^p\). If \(x^\star\in\mathbb R^n\) minimizes \(\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x\) subject to \(Ax=b\) and \(Gx\le h\), and there exists \(\bar x\in\mathbb R^n\) with \(A\bar x=b\) and \(G\bar x<h\), then there exist \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^p\) such that \(Qx^\star+c+A^\top y+G^\top\lambda=0\) and \(\lambda_i(G_i x^\star-h_i)=0\) for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,p\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At every attained optimum of the stated convex QP, strict inequality feasibility relative to the equalities guarantees at least one equality-and-inequality multiplier pair satisfying the KKT conditions.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(G\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), and \(h\in\mathbb R^p\).
There exists \(\bar x\in\mathbb R^n\) with \(A\bar x=b\) and \(G\bar x<h\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal M(x^\star)\ne\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Set of KKT multiplier pairs at the minimizer.

knowledge_statements.title: Unique Multiplier Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LICQ-based uniqueness at a fixed convex-QP minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(G\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), and let \(x^\star\in\mathbb R^n\) be a minimizer admitting a KKT multiplier. Define \(I(x^\star)=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,p\}:G_i x^\star=h_i\}\). If the rows of \(A\), together with the rows \(G_i\) for \(i\in I(x^\star)\), are linearly independent, then the KKT multiplier pair at \(x^\star\) is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An existing KKT multiplier pair is unique when the equality gradients and active inequality gradients are linearly independent.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(G\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\).
\(x^\star\in\mathbb R^n\) is a primal minimizer and \(\mathcal M(x^\star)\ne\varnothing\).
The rows of \(A\), together with \(G_i\) for \(i\in I(x^\star)\), are linearly independent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|\mathcal M(x^\star)|=1\).

notation.meaning: KKT multiplier set at the minimizer.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedral representation of all multipliers associated with one fixed optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(G\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), and let \(x^\star\in\mathbb R^n\) be a minimizer. With \(I=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,p\}:G_i x^\star=h_i\}\), the complete multiplier family is \[\mathcal M(x^\star)=\{(y,\lambda)\in\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R_+^p:Qx^\star+c+A^\top y+G^\top\lambda=0,\ \lambda_i=0\text{ for every }i\notin I\}.\] If nonempty, \(\mathcal M(x^\star)\) is a closed convex polyhedron; it may be a singleton, a bounded positive-dimensional polytope, or an unbounded polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a fixed optimum, the complete multiplier family is the closed convex polyhedron defined by stationarity, nonnegativity, and zero multipliers on inactive inequalities.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(G\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal M(x^\star)\) is a nonempty closed convex polyhedron.

notation.meaning: All KKT multiplier pairs associated with the fixed minimizer.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier Regularity Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete boundary showing that loss of active-gradient independence permits multiplier nonuniqueness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The one-dimensional convex QP \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R}x\) subject to \(-x\le0\) and \(-2x\le0\) has the unique minimizer \(x^\star=0\), linearly dependent active gradients, and multiplier set \[\mathcal M(0)=\{(\lambda_1,\lambda_2)\in\mathbb R_+^2:\lambda_1+2\lambda_2=1\}.\] Thus a unique primal minimizer need not have a unique multiplier when active-gradient independence fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Duplicated binding inequalities can preserve a unique primal minimizer while producing a continuum of KKT multipliers.
assumptions_latex: The QP is \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R}x\) subject to \(-x\le0\) and \(-2x\le0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal M(0)=\{(\lambda_1,\lambda_2)\in\mathbb R_+^2:\lambda_1+2\lambda_2=1\}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Infeasibility Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Farkas-type certificate for incompatibility of affine equalities and inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(G\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), and \(h\in\mathbb R^p\). If there exist \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(z\in\mathbb R_+^p\) satisfying \(A^\top y+G^\top z=0\) and \(b^\top y+h^\top z<0\), then \(\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b,\ Gx\le h\}=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative separating multiplier whose combined left side vanishes and whose combined right side is negative certifies that the affine equality-and-inequality system is infeasible.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(G\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), and \(h\in\mathbb R^p\).
There exist \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(z\in\mathbb R_+^p\) such that \(A^\top y+G^\top z=0\) and \(b^\top y+h^\top z<0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b,\ Gx\le h\}=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Unrestricted equality multiplier and nonnegative inequality multiplier.

children.title: Dual-Infeasibility Certificates

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Infeasibility Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact recession witness for a feasible convex QP under the standard Lagrange dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(G\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), and \(h\in\mathbb R^p\), and suppose \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b,\ Gx\le h\}\ne\varnothing\). A vector \(d\in\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}\) satisfying \(Ad=0\), \(Gd\le0\), \(Qd=0\), and \(c^\top d<0\) certifies that \(\inf_{x\in P}(\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x)=-\infty\) and that the standard Lagrange dual is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero feasible recession direction annihilated by the quadratic term and having negative linear cost certifies primal unboundedness and infeasibility of the standard Lagrange dual.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(G\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), and \(h\in\mathbb R^p\).
There exists \(d\in\mathbb R^n\setminus\{0\}\) with \(Ad=0\), \(Gd\le0\), \(Qd=0\), and \(c^\top d<0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p^\star=-\infty\), and the standard Lagrange dual is infeasible.

children.title: Primal Recession Rays
children.top_down_role: Feasible rays governing the large-scale behavior of the primal model.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Recession Rays
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recession-cone characterization for a nonempty affine-equality and inequality feasible region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(G\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), \(h\in\mathbb R^p\), and \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b,\ Gx\le h\}\ne\varnothing\). A vector \(d\in\mathbb R^n\) is a recession direction of \(P\) if \(x+td\in P\) for every \(x\in P\) and every \(t\ge0\). For this polyhedron, \[\operatorname{rec}(P)=\{d\in\mathbb R^n:Ad=0,\ Gd\le0\}.\] Every nonzero \(d\in\operatorname{rec}(P)\) generates an unbounded feasible ray from each \(x\in P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonempty affine polyhedron, a direction is a feasible recession direction exactly when it preserves every equality and does not increase any inequality left side.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(G\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), and \(h\in\mathbb R^p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d\in\operatorname{rec}(P)\iff Ad=0\text{ and }Gd\le0\).

children.title: Objective-Descent Rays
children.top_down_role: Recession directions associated with continuing objective improvement.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Descent Rays
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact linear-descent condition along a feasible ray of a convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty feasible polyhedron. Define \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+c^\top x\). If \(d\in\operatorname{rec}(P)\) satisfies \(Qd=0\) and \(c^\top d<0\), then, for every \(x\in P\) and every \(t\ge0\), \(f(x+td)=f(x)+t c^\top d\). In particular, \(f(x+td)<f(x)\) for every \(t>0\), and \(f(x+td)\to-\infty\) as \(t\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible recession direction annihilated by the quadratic term and having negative linear cost is a strict objective-descent ray along which the objective tends to negative infinity.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a nonempty feasible polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(x\in P\) and \(t>0\), \(f(x+td)=f(x)+t c^\top d<f(x)\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between finite value and unbounded descent for a feasible convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty polyhedron \(P\) and \(Q\succeq0\), the convex quadratic objective \(f\) has a finite infimum on \(P\) exactly when no direction \(d\in\operatorname{rec}(P)\) satisfies both \(Qd=0\) and \(c^\top d<0\). Existence of such a direction yields \(f(x+td)\to-\infty\); absence of every such direction excludes recession-driven loss of a finite optimum.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-based status witnesses; numerical thresholds depend on scaling and the chosen norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An approximate optimality witness \((x,y,\lambda)\) satisfies \(\lambda\ge0\) and bounds primal feasibility, stationarity, and complementarity residuals by \(\varepsilon\). An approximate primal-infeasibility witness is normalized \((y,z)\), with \(z\ge0\), \(\|A^\top y+G^\top z\|\le\varepsilon\), and \(b^\top y+h^\top z<0\). An approximate unboundedness witness is normalized \(d\), with \(\|Ad\|\le\varepsilon\), \(\|(Gd)_+\|\le\varepsilon\), \(\|Qd\|\le\varepsilon\), and \(c^\top d<0\).

children.top_down_role: Models close to transitions among feasibility, infeasibility, and unboundedness.

Each exact instance has a status in \(\{\mathrm{optimal},\mathrm{primal\ infeasible},\mathrm{unbounded}\}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A QP instance \(\theta\) lies on the ill-posed status boundary if, for every \(\eta>0\), there exist admissible instances \(\theta_1\) and \(\theta_2\) such that \(\|\theta_j-\theta\|<\eta\) for \(j=1,2\) and \(\operatorname{stat}(\theta_1)\ne\operatorname{stat}(\theta_2)\). Equivalently, arbitrarily small data perturbations can cross between finite optimality, primal infeasibility, and unboundedness, so no neighborhood carries a constant exact status.
