children.title: Optimal-Value Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Value-function dependence on objective, bounds, and right-hand sides.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimal-Value Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local envelope formula for a strongly regular parametric convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(v(\theta)\) be the minimum of \(\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Q(\theta)x+c(\theta)^{\mathsf T}x\) subject to \(Ax=b(\theta)\) and \(Gx\le h(\theta)\). Suppose the data are continuously differentiable near \(\theta_0\), and at \(\theta_0\) the KKT point \((x^*,\lambda^*,\mu^*)\) is unique, satisfies LICQ and strict complementarity, and has positive-definite reduced Hessian. Then \(v\) is differentiable at \(\theta_0\), and for every direction \(d\),
\[Dv(\theta_0)d=\tfrac12(x^*)^{\mathsf T}(DQ(\theta_0)d)x^*+(Dc(\theta_0)d)^{\mathsf T}x^*-(\lambda^*)^{\mathsf T}Db(\theta_0)d-(\mu^*)^{\mathsf T}Dh(\theta_0)d.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under standard strong-regularity conditions, the optimal value is differentiable, and its derivative is obtained by differentiating the Lagrangian data while holding the optimal primal-dual point fixed.
assumptions_latex: d^{\mathsf T}Q(\theta_0)d>0\text{ for every nonzero critical feasible direction }d
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dv(\theta_0)d=D_\theta L(x^*,\lambda^*,\mu^*;\theta_0)d

notation.meaning: Fréchet derivative with respect to the parameter

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The envelope formula is plausible, but no source supports the stated differentiability hypotheses. The parameter space and direction domain are also not introduced, so an authoritative parametric-optimization source is required before fixing the exact theorem.

children.title: Solution-Mapping Stability
children.top_down_role: Continuity and local regularity regimes for primal solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Solution-Mapping Stability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local single-valued stability of the primal solution under strong regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a finite-dimensional convex QP whose objective and affine constraint data depend continuously differentiably on \(\theta\). If at \(\theta_0\) a KKT point satisfies LICQ, strict complementarity, and positive definiteness of the Hessian on the active-constraint null space, then neighborhoods \(U\) of \(\theta_0\) and \(V\) of \(x^*\) exist such that every \(\theta\in U\) has exactly one KKT primal solution in \(V\). The resulting mapping \(x:U\to V\) is continuously differentiable, hence locally Lipschitz: for some \(L<\infty\), \(\|x(\theta_1)-x(\theta_2)\|\le L\|\theta_1-\theta_2\|\) locally.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: LICQ, strict complementarity, and positive reduced curvature make the nearby primal optimizer unique, continuously differentiable, and locally Lipschitz in the QP data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x(\cdot)\text{ is locally single-valued, continuously differentiable, and Lipschitz}

notation.meaning: basis for the null space of the active constraint Jacobian

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The local stability claim is plausible under strong regularity, but the exact single-valued C1 conclusion and its hypotheses need an authoritative sensitivity-analysis source. The domain of the parameter is also unspecified.

children.title: Multiplier Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Stability of dual certificates under perturbations.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Differentiability of active KKT multipliers while the active set remains fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(W\) stack the equality rows and active inequality rows of a parametric convex QP at \(\theta_0\), and let \(y\) stack their multipliers. If LICQ, strict complementarity, and positive-definite reduced curvature hold, then the active set is locally constant and \((x(\theta),y(\theta))\) is continuously differentiable. Its directional derivative is the unique solution of the differentiated KKT equations
\[\begin{pmatrix}Q&W^{\mathsf T}\\W&0\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}Dx(\theta_0)d\\Dy(\theta_0)d\end{pmatrix}=-D_\theta\begin{pmatrix}Q(\theta)x^*+c(\theta)+W(\theta)^{\mathsf T}y^*\\W(\theta)x^*-r(\theta)\end{pmatrix}_{\theta=\theta_0}d.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With strong regularity and a fixed active set, equality and active-inequality multipliers vary differentiably; their derivative follows from one differentiated KKT solve.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dy(\theta_0)d\text{ exists uniquely and is obtained from the differentiated KKT system}

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the active-set constancy and differentiability theorem. In addition, the matrix on the left should explicitly be evaluated at theta_0, and the parameter and direction domains must be specified.

children.title: Active-Set Transition Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Perturbation boundaries at which the optimal face changes.

knowledge_statements.title: Active-Set Transition Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary characterization for nondegenerate multiparametric convex QPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a convex QP with fixed Hessian and parameter-affine linear terms and right-hand sides, let \(\mathcal R_I\) be a nondegenerate critical region on which the optimal active set is \(I\). Within \(\mathcal R_I\), the primal solution and active multipliers are affine in the parameter. The relative boundary of \(\mathcal R_I\) is contained in
\[\bigcup_{j\notin I}\{\theta:G_jx_I(\theta)-h_j(\theta)=0\}\ \cup\ \bigcup_{i\in I}\{\theta:\mu_{I,i}(\theta)=0\}.\]
Thus an optimal-face transition can occur only when an inactive constraint reaches zero slack or an active multiplier reaches zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nondegenerate critical region ends only when an inactive constraint becomes tight or an active multiplier becomes zero; these affine equalities form its transition boundaries.
assumptions_latex: \text{linear objective and constraint data depend affinely on }\theta
\operatorname{LICQ}\text{ and strict complementarity hold in }\operatorname{relint}(\mathcal R_I)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \partial\mathcal R_I\subseteq\bigcup_{j\notin I}\{s_j=0\}\cup\bigcup_{i\in I}\{\mu_i=0\}

notation.meaning: critical parameter region associated with active set I

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The characterization is standard for nondegenerate multiparametric QPs, but no source establishes the precise critical-region assumptions or whether parameter-domain boundaries must also be included.

children.title: Full KKT Factorization
children.top_down_role: Direct factorization of the coupled saddle-point system.

knowledge_statements.title: Full KKT Factorization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct symmetric-indefinite solution of an equality-constrained convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the equality-constrained QP \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+g^{\mathsf T}x\) subject to \(Ax=b\), where \(H=H^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\). Form \[K=\begin{pmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad r=\begin{pmatrix}-g\\b\end{pmatrix}.\] Compute a symmetric-indefinite factorization \(P^{\mathsf T}KP=LDL^{\mathsf T}\), allowing block pivots in \(D\). Solve \(LDL^{\mathsf T}w=P^{\mathsf T}r\), set \((x,y)=Pw\), and stop when the KKT-system residual meets the prescribed tolerance. If \(A\) has full row rank and \(H\) is positive definite on \(\ker A\), then \(K\) is nonsingular and its exact solution is the unique primal-dual KKT point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Factor the complete symmetric saddle-point matrix and solve by triangular and block-diagonal substitutions; full row rank and positive definiteness on the constraint null space ensure a unique primal-dual solution.
assumptions_latex: z^{\mathsf T}Hz>0\text{ for every }0\ne z\in\ker A
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K\begin{pmatrix}x\\y\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}-g\\b\end{pmatrix}\text{ has a unique solution}

children.title: Range-Space Schur-Complement Method
children.top_down_role: Multiplier-space reduction through primal elimination.

knowledge_statements.title: Range-Space Schur-Complement Method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-QP reduction to a positive-definite system in multiplier space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the equality-constrained QP with KKT equations \(Hx+g+A^{\mathsf T}y=0\) and \(Ax=b\), where \(H=H^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(b,y\in\mathbb R^m\). Assume \(H\succ0\) and \(\operatorname{rank}(A)=m\). Factor \(H\), use linear solves to apply \(H^{-1}\), define \(S=AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\), and solve \[Sy=-b-AH^{-1}g.\] Recover \[x=-H^{-1}(g+A^{\mathsf T}y).\] Return \((x,y)\) when the primal and stationarity residuals meet their prescribed tolerances. The matrix \(S\) is positive definite and may be solved by Cholesky factorization; explicit formation of \(H^{-1}\) is unnecessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminate the primal variables using the positive-definite Hessian, solve the positive-definite multiplier-space Schur complement, and back-substitute for the primal solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S=AH^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\succ0\text{ and the recovered pair satisfies the KKT equations}

source_refs.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

children.title: Null-Space Direct Method
children.top_down_role: Feasible-direction reduction through an explicit null-space basis.

knowledge_statements.title: Null-Space Direct Method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-QP reduction to feasible coordinates in the constraint null space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the equality-constrained QP \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Hx+g^{\mathsf T}x\) subject to \(Ax=b\), where \(H=H^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has rank \(m\), \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\). Compute \(x_p\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying \(Ax_p=b\) and a full-column-rank matrix \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) satisfying \(AZ=0\) and \(\operatorname{range}(Z)=\ker A\). Write \(x=x_p+Zp\), with \(p\in\mathbb R^{n-m}\), and solve \[(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ)p=-Z^{\mathsf T}(Hx_p+g).\] Set \(x=x_p+Zp\), obtain the unique \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) from \(A^{\mathsf T}y=-(Hx+g)\), and return \((x,y)\) after checking feasibility and stationarity. If \(Z^{\mathsf T}HZ\succ0\), the reduced solution and the QP minimizer are unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parameterize all feasible points with a null-space basis, solve the positive-definite reduced Hessian system, and recover the unique equality multiplier from stationarity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x=x_p+Zp\text{ is the unique QP minimizer}

notation.meaning: basis matrix for the null space of A

source_refs.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

source_witnesses.locator: 4.4.2 Projections, Range-, and Null-Space Bases p. 71

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Direct null-space solution of an equality-constrained KKT system
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Null-space direct method for an equality-constrained quadratic KKT system; nonsingularity of the full Hessian matrix is not required.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the KKT system \(-Gp+A^T\lambda=g\), \(Ap=-h\). Suppose \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) has full row rank, the columns of \(Z\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times(n-m)}\) form a basis of \(\ker A\), \(Z^TGZ\succ0\), and \(Y\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times m}\) is such that \([Y\mid Z]\) is nonsingular. Writing \(p=Yp_Y+Zp_Z\), the matrix \(AY\) is nonsingular, and the solution is obtained successively from \((AY)p_Y=-h\), \((Z^TGZ)p_Z=-Z^TGYp_Y-Z^Tg\), \(p=Yp_Y+Zp_Z\), and \((AY)^T\lambda=Y^T(g+Gp)\). The positive-definite reduced system may be solved by Cholesky factorization, and \(G\) itself need not be nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a null-space basis Z and a complementary matrix Y for a full-row-rank equality matrix A, assuming that the reduced Hessian is positive definite. Solve first for the complementary component that restores feasibility, then for the null-space component through the reduced-Hessian system, assemble the primal step, and recover the multiplier from the transposed complementary system. The procedure solves the KKT system without requiring G itself to be nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (AY)p_Y=-h,\quad (Z^TGZ)p_Z=-Z^TGYp_Y-Z^Tg,\quad p=Yp_Y+Zp_Z,\quad (AY)^T\lambda=Y^T(g+Gp),\quad AY\ \text{is nonsingular, and nonsingularity of }G\ \text{is not required}.

children.title: Augmented KKT Systems
children.top_down_role: Saddle-point representations expanded through auxiliary system blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Augmented KKT Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent equality-QP system obtained by an augmented-Lagrangian row modification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\rho>0\), the equality-QP KKT system is equivalent to
\[\begin{pmatrix}H+\rho A^{\mathsf T}A&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}x\\y\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}-g+\rho A^{\mathsf T}b\\b\end{pmatrix}.\]
Indeed, the second block equation enforces \(Ax=b\), after which the first block equation reduces to \(Hx+A^{\mathsf T}y=-g\). Conversely, every solution of the original KKT equations satisfies the augmented system. Hence augmentation changes the coefficient matrix and its numerical spectrum but not the exact primal-dual solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding a positive multiple of the constraint normal matrix to the Hessian yields an equivalent KKT system because the constraint equation cancels the augmentation at every exact solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{sol}(K_\rho,r_\rho)=\operatorname{sol}(K_0,r_0)

source_refs.locator: 4.3 Direct Methods for Solving Linear Systems p. 60

source_witnesses.locator: 4.3 Direct Methods for Solving Linear Systems p. 60

children.title: Regularized KKT Systems
children.top_down_role: KKT representations modified by stabilizing diagonal or block perturbations.

knowledge_statements.title: Regularized KKT Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual diagonal regularization of an equality-QP saddle-point system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For regularization parameters \(\delta>0\) and \(\gamma>0\), replace the equality-QP KKT equations by
\[\begin{pmatrix}H+\delta I&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&-\gamma I\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}x_{\delta,\gamma}\\y_{\delta,\gamma}\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}-g\\b\end{pmatrix}.\]
If \(H\succeq0\), this matrix is nonsingular: its primal diagonal block is positive definite and its dual diagonal block is negative definite. The solution exactly satisfies the perturbed equations \((H+\delta I)x+A^{\mathsf T}y=-g\) and \(Ax-\gamma y=b\); it generally does not exactly satisfy the unregularized KKT system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive primal and negative dual diagonal shifts produce a nonsingular saddle-point system, but its solution solves perturbed rather than exact KKT equations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K_{\delta,\gamma}\text{ is nonsingular and defines a unique regularized primal-dual pair}

children.title: Quasi-Definite System Forms
children.top_down_role: Modified saddle-point structures supporting favorable factorization regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Quasi-Definite System Forms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonsingularity and inertia of symmetric quasi-definite saddle-point matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[K=\begin{pmatrix}P&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&-D\end{pmatrix},\]
where \(P\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) and \(D\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) are symmetric, \(P\succ0\), and \(D\succ0\). Then \(K\) is symmetric quasi-definite and nonsingular for every \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\). Its inertia is
\[\operatorname{inertia}(K)=(n,m,0),\]
meaning that it has exactly \(n\) positive, \(m\) negative, and no zero eigenvalues. Equivalently, the Schur complement \(-D-AP^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\) is negative definite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A saddle-point matrix with a positive-definite primal block and negative-definite dual block is nonsingular and has a fixed positive-negative eigenvalue count, regardless of the coupling matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K\text{ is nonsingular and }\operatorname{inertia}(K)=(n,m,0)

notation.meaning: numbers of positive, negative, and zero eigenvalues
positive-definite primal and dual diagonal blocks

children.title: KKT Stabilization Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Conditioning, sparsity, and perturbation effects of system modification.

knowledge_statements.title: KKT Stabilization Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-bias identity governing diagonal KKT regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((x_{\delta,\gamma},y_{\delta,\gamma})\) solve the diagonally regularized system with matrix \(K_{\delta,\gamma}=K_0+\operatorname{diag}(\delta I,-\gamma I)\) and unmodified right-hand side \(r\). Its residual in the original KKT equations is exactly
\[K_0\begin{pmatrix}x_{\delta,\gamma}\\y_{\delta,\gamma}\end{pmatrix}-r=\begin{pmatrix}-\delta x_{\delta,\gamma}\\\gamma y_{\delta,\gamma}\end{pmatrix}.\]
Thus positive regularization can remove singular or weak diagonal blocks and produce a quasi-definite system, but it introduces primal stationarity and feasibility bias proportional to the parameters and computed variables. Accuracy for the original QP therefore requires controlling these residual terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Diagonal regularization can make a KKT matrix reliably nonsingular, but it introduces exactly quantifiable stationarity and feasibility errors that must be balanced against numerical stability.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K_0z_{\delta,\gamma}-r=(-\delta x_{\delta,\gamma},\gamma y_{\delta,\gamma})^{\mathsf T}

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The residual identity and stated stabilization tradeoff fit the leaf, but the record has no citation. A source addressing diagonal KKT regularization and its residual bias is required.

children.title: Reduced-System Conjugate Gradient
children.top_down_role: Conjugate-gradient treatment of a definite reduced QP system.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-System Conjugate Gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conjugate gradients applied to a positive-definite reduced QP Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(R=R^{\mathsf T}\succ0\) with \(R\in\mathbb R^{q\times q}\), a right-hand side \(q_R\in\mathbb R^q\), a starting point \(p_0\in\mathbb R^q\), and \(\varepsilon>0\), set \(r_0=q_R-Rp_0\). If \(\|r_0\|=0\), return \(p_0\). Otherwise set \(d_0=r_0\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), compute \(\alpha_k=(r_k^{\mathsf T}r_k)/(d_k^{\mathsf T}Rd_k)\), \(p_{k+1}=p_k+\alpha_kd_k\), and \(r_{k+1}=r_k-\alpha_kRd_k\). Return \(p_{k+1}\) when \(\|r_{k+1}\|\le\varepsilon\|r_0\|\). Otherwise set \(\beta_k=(r_{k+1}^{\mathsf T}r_{k+1})/(r_k^{\mathsf T}r_k)\) and \(d_{k+1}=r_{k+1}+\beta_kd_k\). In exact arithmetic, the method reaches the exact solution in at most \(q\) iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply conjugate gradients to a q-dimensional positive-definite reduced system, first returning immediately if the initial residual is zero; otherwise stop at the relative residual tolerance, with exact termination in at most q iterations in exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|q_R-Rp_k\|\le\varepsilon\|r_0\|\text{ at tolerance termination, with exact termination in at most }q\text{ iterations}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\tfrac12x^THx+g^Tx\) subject to \(Ax=b\). Define \(P=I-A^T(AA^T)^{-1}A\), the orthogonal projector onto \(\ker A\), and solve \(PHPp=-P(Hx_0+g)\) on \(\operatorname{range}P\) by CG. Set \(p_0=0\), \(r_0=-P(Hx_0+g)\), and \(d_0=r_0\). At iteration \(k\geq0\), stop if \(r_k\) meets the prescribed tolerance; otherwise set \(\alpha_k=(r_k^Tr_k)/(d_k^THd_k)\), \(p_{k+1}=p_k+\alpha_kd_k\), and \(r_{k+1}=r_k-\alpha_kPHd_k\). If \(r_{k+1}\) does not meet the tolerance, set \(\beta_k=(r_{k+1}^Tr_{k+1})/(r_k^Tr_k)\) and \(d_{k+1}=r_{k+1}+\beta_kd_k\). Define each QP iterate by \(x_k=x_0+p_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projected conjugate gradients solves the positive-definite null-space system. Every displacement lies in the constraint null space, so every QP iterate remains feasible without constructing an explicit null-space basis, and exact-arithmetic termination gives the unique minimizer.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Implicit Full-Space Representation of Projected Conjugate Gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Original-space reformulation of reduced-system PCG that works implicitly with an orthogonal null-space basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_p=Yx_y\) satisfy \(Ax_p=b\), let the columns of \(Z\) form an orthonormal basis of \(\ker A\), and suppose \(W_{zz}=Z^THZ\succ0\) with \(H=H^T\). Reduced-system CG may be rewritten in the original space by maintaining \[x=Zx_z+x_p,\qquad Z^Tr=r_z,\qquad g=Zg_z,\qquad d=Zd_z,\] and introducing the scaled projection matrix \[P=Z(Z^THZ)^{-1}Z^T.\] The resulting projected formulation updates the null-space component implicitly and can be implemented without operating with an explicit null-space basis. In the construction stated by the extract, the implicit use of an orthogonal \(Z\) avoids sensitivity to ill conditioning in \(A\) and to a poor explicit choice of null-space basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projected CG rewrites reduced-system PCG in the original variable space. Starting from a particular feasible component, it maintains full-space counterparts of the reduced point, residual, preconditioned residual, and direction, using a scaled null-space projection matrix. The orthogonal null-space basis is handled implicitly, avoiding the conditioning difficulties of an explicit poor basis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Reduced-system PCG admits an equivalent n-dimensional projected representation that updates }Zx_z\text{ implicitly without explicit operations with }Z.

children.top_down_role: Iterative methods for symmetric indefinite KKT systems.

assumptions_latex: \(H\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is symmetric, \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank, \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The KKT matrix \(K\) is symmetric and nonsingular, and MINRES applies to the symmetric transformed system without requiring \(K\) to be positive definite.

notation.meaning: order-k Krylov subspace generated by the transformed matrix and initial residual

review_flags: MINRES specialization should be confirmed in the cited Krylov material
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetry-preserving MINRES realization for a finite-dimensional nonsingular equality-QP KKT system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the equality-QP KKT equations, define \(K=\begin{pmatrix}H&A^T\\A&0\end{pmatrix}\) and \(q=\begin{pmatrix}-g\\b\end{pmatrix}\). Given \(M=M^T\succ0\), form \(\widehat K=M^{-1/2}KM^{-1/2}\) and \(\widehat q=M^{-1/2}q\). Starting from any \(y_0\in\mathbb R^{n+m}\), let \(\widehat r_0=\widehat q-\widehat Ky_0\) and \(\mathcal K_k(\widehat K,\widehat r_0)=\operatorname{span}\{\widehat r_0,\widehat K\widehat r_0,\ldots,\widehat K^{k-1}\widehat r_0\}\). MINRES uses symmetric Lanczos recurrences and chooses \(y_k\in y_0+\mathcal K_k(\widehat K,\widehat r_0)\) to minimize \(\lVert\widehat q-\widehat Ky\rVert_2\) over that affine space. On termination, recover \(\begin{pmatrix}x\\\lambda\end{pmatrix}=M^{-1/2}y_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Symmetrically preconditioned MINRES solves the nonsingular indefinite KKT system in Lanczos Krylov spaces and minimizes the transformed residual without requiring positive definiteness of the KKT matrix.

knowledge_statements.title: QP Preconditioning Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Three structural preconditioner families for equality-QP linear systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(K=\begin{pmatrix}H&A^T\\A&0\end{pmatrix}\), representative families are the positive-definite block preconditioner \(M_D=\operatorname{diag}(B,S)\), the constraint preconditioner \(M_C=\begin{pmatrix}B&A^T\\A&0\end{pmatrix}\), and the reduced-space preconditioner \(M_R=Z^TBZ\). Here \(B\) approximates \(H\), \(S\) approximates the Schur complement \(AB^{-1}A^T\), and the columns of \(Z\) span \(\ker A\). The block family supports symmetry-preserving MINRES when \(B\succ0\) and \(S\succ0\); the constraint family preserves the saddle-point coupling; the reduced family preconditions the positive-definite null-space equation when \(Z^TBZ\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: QP preconditioners may approximate diagonal blocks, preserve the constraint saddle structure, or act on the reduced null-space Hessian.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
\(B=B^T\succ0\), and \(Z\) has full column rank with \(AZ=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_D\), \(M_C\), and \(M_R\) define block, constraint, and reduced-space preconditioning realizations, respectively.

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetric-Indefinite Sparse Factorization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pivoted sparse direct factorization of an equality-QP KKT matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sparse symmetric-indefinite direct realization selects a symmetric permutation \(P\) and computes \(P^TKP=LDL^T\), where \(L\) is unit lower triangular and \(D\) is block diagonal with nonsingular \(1\times1\) and \(2\times2\) pivot blocks. The KKT solution is obtained by permutation, triangular solution with \(L\), block-diagonal solution with \(D\), solution with \(L^T\), and inverse permutation. Symmetric pivoting may alter a fill-reducing ordering to control small or unstable pivots; consequently, the realized nonzero pattern can differ from the symbolic pattern predicted from the initial permutation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A permuted sparse KKT matrix is factored into triangular and small block-diagonal factors, with pivoting balancing sparsity against numerical stability.
assumptions_latex: \(K=K^T\) is a nonsingular sparse KKT matrix.
The pivoting rule selects only nonsingular accepted pivot blocks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K=P^{-T}LDL^TP^{-1}\), enabling a direct solution by sparse substitutions and block solves.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\tfrac12x^THx+g^Tx\) subject to \(Ax=b\), and write \(x=x_0+Zp\). The reduced stationarity equation is \(Rp=-Z^T(Hx_0+g)\), where \(R=Z^THZ\). Positive definiteness of \(H\) on \(\ker A\) implies \(R\succ0\), so \(R\) admits a Cholesky factorization \(R=LL^T\) with nonsingular lower-triangular \(L\). Solving the two triangular systems determines the unique reduced displacement \(p\), and \(x=x_0+Zp\) is the unique primal minimizer. The sparsity of \(R\) and \(L\) depends on the chosen null-space basis and elimination ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Null-space reduction converts the equality QP into a positive-definite reduced system. Cholesky factorization of that system yields the unique primal minimizer, with sparsity depending on the null-space basis and ordering.

children.title: Sparse Elimination Orderings

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse Elimination Orderings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Permutation-based ordering for symbolic symmetric elimination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a structurally symmetric sparse matrix \(K\) with graph \(G(K)=(V,E)\), a sparse elimination ordering is a bijection \(\pi:\{1,\ldots,n\}\to V\), equivalently a symmetric permutation matrix \(P\). At elimination step \(i\), vertex \(\pi(i)\) is removed and its remaining higher-numbered neighbors are joined pairwise. Applying the ordering to factorization means factoring \(P^TKP\). The ordering determines the symbolic elimination graph, elimination tree, and potential factor nonzeros before numerical pivoting; it is fill-reducing when these symbolic costs are smaller than those produced by a specified comparison ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sparse elimination ordering numbers graph vertices and therefore determines the symbolic fill pattern and dependency tree of a permuted factorization.
assumptions_latex: \(K\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) has a structurally symmetric sparsity pattern.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi\) induces a symmetric permutation and a uniquely determined symbolic elimination process.

notation.meaning: permutation matrix induced by the ordering

children.title: Fill-In Structure
children.top_down_role: Nonzero growth induced by elimination.

knowledge_statements.title: Fill-In Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Graph characterization of symbolic fill under symmetric elimination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix an elimination ordering \(\pi\) of the undirected sparsity graph \(G(K)\). When a vertex is eliminated, every pair of its still-uneliminated neighbors is connected. An edge created by this operation that was absent from \(G(K)\) is a fill edge. The union of original and fill edges is the filled graph \(G_\pi^+(K)\), which is chordal. Structurally, an off-diagonal entry can occur in the triangular factor exactly when its corresponding oriented edge belongs to the filled graph, subject to cancellation-free symbolic analysis. Thus symbolic factor storage is determined by \(G_\pi^+(K)\), while numerical cancellations can only remove predicted entries.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Elimination connects each eliminated vertex's remaining neighbors; the resulting chordal completion predicts the structural nonzeros of the triangular factor.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) has a structurally symmetric pattern and a fixed symmetric elimination ordering \(\pi\).
Symbolic analysis ignores accidental numerical cancellation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The symbolic triangular-factor pattern is encoded by the chordal filled graph \(G_\pi^+(K)\).

notation.meaning: filled graph induced by the ordering

review_flags: authoritative chordal-fill characterization locator is missing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property is a standard graph characterization of symbolic fill and fits the terminal container, but the chordal-completion and exact factor-pattern claims require an authoritative sparse-matrix locator.

children.title: Graph-Based Ordering Heuristics
children.top_down_role: Graph-derived ordering families used to limit factorization growth.

knowledge_statements.title: Graph-Based Ordering Heuristics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum-degree and nested-dissection heuristics for symbolic fill control.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given the undirected sparsity graph \(G=(V,E)\), an approximate minimum-degree ordering repeatedly selects an unnumbered vertex of estimated minimum degree in the current quotient graph, numbers it next, updates the graph after symbolic elimination, and continues until all vertices are numbered. A nested-dissection ordering instead finds a separator \(S\) whose removal partitions \(V\setminus S\) into disconnected subsets, recursively orders those subsets, and numbers \(S\) last. Either procedure returns a permutation \(\pi\); symbolic elimination of \(G\) under \(\pi\) determines the predicted fill and elimination tree. These are heuristics and do not generally guarantee a globally minimum-fill ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimum-degree eliminates locally sparse vertices, while nested dissection recursively postpones graph separators; both produce practical but generally nonoptimal fill-reducing permutations.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is the undirected structural graph used for symmetric symbolic factorization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure returns a complete vertex permutation \(\pi\) for subsequent symbolic or numerical factorization.
review_flags: authoritative locator for minimum-degree and nested-dissection algorithms is missing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind is appropriate, and the descriptions of approximate minimum degree and nested dissection are not overstated. No authoritative section, theorem, algorithm, or page locator is supplied.

children.title: Ordering Quality Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Symbolic cost, numerical behavior, and preprocessing expense across ordering choices.

knowledge_statements.title: Ordering Quality Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiple, potentially conflicting criteria for assessing sparse orderings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an ordering \(\pi\), define symbolic quality by the tuple \(Q(\pi)=(\operatorname{nnz}L_\pi,F_\pi,h_\pi,w_\pi)\), comprising factor nonzeros, predicted arithmetic work, elimination-tree height, and a parallel-front or separator-width measure. No single component determines the others: an ordering may reduce storage while exposing less parallelism or producing larger frontal matrices. For symmetric-indefinite KKT factorization, numerical pivoting introduces an additional stability criterion and may modify \(\pi\), increasing realized fill. Consequently, ordering comparison must specify the cost model and may use Pareto dominance rather than an unqualified assertion that one ordering is best.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sparse orderings trade factor storage, arithmetic, parallel depth, frontal size, and pivot stability; quality is meaningful only relative to a stated cost model.
assumptions_latex: Each candidate ordering is evaluated on the same structural matrix and symbolic-factorization convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Ordering quality is a multi-criterion comparison of \(Q(\pi)\), not a universal scalar ranking.

notation.meaning: symbolic triangular factor under the ordering

children.title: Low-Rank Factor Updates
children.top_down_role: Factor modifications associated with compact additions to a system.

knowledge_statements.title: Low-Rank Factor Updates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Updating a positive-definite factorization after a low-rank positive modification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B=LL^T\succ0\) and let \(U\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\). The modified matrix \(\widetilde B=B+UU^T\) is positive definite and admits \(\widetilde B=\widetilde L\widetilde L^T\). Its factor may be obtained by applying \(r\) successive rank-one Cholesky updates to \(L\), avoiding a factorization from scratch. For linear solves, the same modification satisfies \(\widetilde B^{-1}=B^{-1}-B^{-1}U(I+U^TB^{-1}U)^{-1}U^TB^{-1}\). Thus the modification reduces to triangular solves with \(L\) and a dense system of order \(r\), provided sparsity and stability requirements permit the update path.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive low-rank matrix modification can update an existing Cholesky factor or be handled through a small Woodbury correction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B+UU^T\succ0\) and both its factorization and inverse action can reuse the factor of \(B\).
review_flags: authoritative low-rank factor-update locator is missing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation correctly states positive low-rank Cholesky updating and the Woodbury identity, but no authoritative factor-update or matrix-modification locator is provided.

children.title: Factor Downdates
children.top_down_role: Factor modifications associated with removal or reversal of system contributions.

knowledge_statements.title: Factor Downdates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact feasibility condition for a positive-definite low-rank downdate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B=LL^T\succ0\) and \(U\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\). A real nonsingular Cholesky factor of the downdated matrix \(\widehat B=B-UU^T\) exists if and only if \(I-U^TB^{-1}U\succ0\). Under this condition, successive rank-one downdates can transform \(L\) into \(\widehat L\) satisfying \(\widehat B=\widehat L\widehat L^T\). If the smallest eigenvalue of \(I-U^TB^{-1}U\) approaches zero, the downdate approaches singularity and becomes increasingly sensitive to rounding; if the condition fails, a positive-definite Cholesky downdate is mathematically impossible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subtracting a low-rank term preserves a Cholesky factor exactly when its scaled Gram matrix remains strictly below the identity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B-UU^T\succ0\iff I-U^TB^{-1}U\succ0\).
review_flags: authoritative Cholesky-downdate condition locator is missing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind is exact for this leaf, and the positive-definiteness equivalence is mathematically appropriate. The downdate-existence and rounding-sensitivity claims nevertheless require an authoritative locator.

children.title: Working-Set Factor Reuse
children.top_down_role: Reuse of existing factors across nearby active-set systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Working-Set Factor Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bordered-factor reuse across adjacent active-set QP subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For working set \(W_k\), form \(K_k=\begin{pmatrix}H&A_{W_k}^T\\A_{W_k}&0\end{pmatrix}\) and retain a permutation and factorization of \(K_k\). If one independent constraint with row \(a^T\) is added, form \(K_{k+1}=\begin{pmatrix}K_k&c\\c^T&0\end{pmatrix}\), where \(c=(a^T,0)^T\), and extend the factors using triangular solves and the resulting scalar Schur complement. If a constraint is removed, delete its row and column and apply stable symmetric downdating or refactor the affected part. Solve the new KKT right-hand side with the modified factors; refactor from scratch whenever rank, pivot-quality, or residual tests fail.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An active-set solver reuses KKT factors by bordered updates for added constraints and downdates for removed constraints, refactorizing when stability tests fail.
assumptions_latex: Successive working sets differ by one constraint.
Each accepted working set yields a nonsingular KKT matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The modified factors solve the KKT system for \(W_{k+1}\) without an unconditional full refactorization.

notation.meaning: border column induced by an added constraint

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits working-set factor reuse and appropriately includes refactorization safeguards, but the bordered-update, deletion/downdate, and stability-test claims have no cited source or inspectable locator.

children.title: Update Stability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Numerical regimes where incremental factor modification becomes unreliable.

assumptions_latex: A Cholesky downdate seeks a factor of \(H-uu^{\mathsf T}\) in floating-point arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H-uu^{\mathsf T}\succ0\) holds exactly when \(u^{\mathsf T}H^{-1}u<1\). At equality the downdated matrix is singular, and as \(u^{\mathsf T}H^{-1}u\uparrow1\), its smallest eigenvalue approaches zero and its condition number may diverge. Hence a stable modification scheme must reject or refactor a downdate when the computed margin \(1-u^{\mathsf T}H^{-1}u\) is nonpositive or comparable to accumulated rounding error; no real nonsingular Cholesky factor exists beyond the boundary.

notation.meaning: Symmetric positive-definite matrix represented by a factorization.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp positive-definiteness boundary for a rank-one Cholesky downdate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\) and \(u\in\mathbb R^n\). The rank-one downdate \(H_-=H-uu^{\mathsf T}\) admits a real nonsingular Cholesky factor precisely under
\[
u^{\mathsf T}H^{-1}u<1.
\]
If equality holds, \(H_-\) is singular; if the quantity exceeds one, \(H_-\) is indefinite. Moreover, approaching the boundary can make \(H_-\) arbitrarily ill-conditioned. Consequently, a finite-precision update procedure should monitor the computed definiteness margin and abandon modification in favor of refactorization when that margin cannot be distinguished reliably from zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank-one downdate is valid exactly below its positive-definiteness boundary; near that boundary ill-conditioning makes updating unreliable, so refactorization is required.
knowledge_statements.title: Update Stability Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact positive-definiteness boundary is standard, but the prescribed finite-precision rejection/refactorization rule depends on the downdate algorithm and rounding-error analysis. No inspectable citation supports that stability claim.

children.title: Primal-Feasible Active-Set Methods
children.top_down_role: Working-set methods maintaining primal feasibility across face changes.

assumptions_latex: \(Q\succeq0\), and the current iterate satisfies \(Ax=b\) and \(Gx\le h\).
The working-set rows are linearly independent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted step remains primal feasible. If the computed direction is zero and all working-set inequality multipliers are nonnegative, the current iterate satisfies the convex-QP KKT conditions and is globally optimal.

notation.meaning: Current set of inequalities treated as equalities.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical feasible-start active-set scheme for convex inequality-constrained QPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For
\[
\min_x\ \tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax=b,\ Gx\le h,
\]
start from a feasible \(x^0\) and a working set \(W^0\) of active inequalities. At iteration \(k\), minimize the quadratic model in \(p\) subject to \(Ap=0\) and \(G_{W^k}p=0\). If \(p\ne0\), choose the largest \(\alpha\in(0,1]\) preserving \(G(x^k+\alpha p)\le h\), add a blocking constraint when \(\alpha<1\), and update \(x^{k+1}=x^k+\alpha p\). If \(p=0\), stop when all working-set inequality multipliers are nonnegative; otherwise remove one having a negative multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from a feasible point, solve on the current face, stop at blocking constraints, and delete active constraints whose multipliers violate dual feasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Feasible Active-Set Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The feasible-start active-set outline and multiplier sign are plausible for the stated inequality convention, but no authoritative source with a specific locator supports the algorithm and termination criterion.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal-Feasible Active-Set Algorithm for Convex QP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formal working-set iteration with multiplier-sign release and blocking-constraint admission.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a convex QP, choose a feasible x_0 and \mathcal W_0\subseteq\mathcal A(x_0). At iteration k, solve \min_p\{\tfrac12p^TGp+(Gx_k+c)^Tp:a_i^Tp=0\ \forall i\in\mathcal W_k\} for p_k. If p_k=0, compute multipliers satisfying Gx_k+c=\sum_{i\in\mathcal W_k}a_i\hat\lambda_i. Stop with x^*=x_k when \hat\lambda_i\ge0 for all i\in\mathcal W_k\cap\mathcal I; otherwise choose j\in\arg\min_{i\in\mathcal W_k\cap\mathcal I}\hat\lambda_i, set x_{k+1}=x_k, and set \mathcal W_{k+1}=\mathcal W_k\setminus\{j\}. If p_k\ne0, choose the largest \alpha_k\in[0,1] for which x_k+\alpha_kp_k is feasible, set x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k, and add one blocking constraint when one exists; otherwise retain \mathcal W_k.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Start from a feasible point and a subset of its active constraints. Solve the equality-constrained quadratic step problem for the current working set. A zero step triggers a multiplier test: stop if every working inequality multiplier is nonnegative, or remove an inequality having the smallest multiplier. A nonzero step is shortened only as needed to preserve feasibility, after which one blocking constraint is added if any exists.
assumptions_latex: \text{Each stated working-set subproblem and multiplier system is solvable when invoked}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p_k=0\ \land\ \hat\lambda_i\ge0\ \forall i\in\mathcal W_k\cap\mathcal I\Longrightarrow x^*=x_k;\qquad\text{otherwise }(x_{k+1},\mathcal W_{k+1})\text{ is updated by constraint release or a maximal feasible step and possible blocking admission}.

children.title: Dual Active-Set Methods
children.top_down_role: Working-set methods organized around dual feasibility and constraint addition.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Dual active-set methods for positive-semidefinite quadratic programming

assumptions_latex: \(Q\succeq0\) for the convex QP \(\min \tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\) subject to \(Ax=b\), \(Gx\le h\).
Each working-set subproblem is solved consistently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A dual active-set iteration preserves stationarity and nonnegativity of retained inequality multipliers. Termination with primal feasibility gives the KKT conditions and therefore a global minimizer.

notation.meaning: Working set of inequalities with potentially positive multipliers.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invariant characterization shared by dual-feasible active-set QP schemes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A dual active-set method maintains
\[
Qx+c+A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}z=0,
\qquad z\ge0,
\qquad z_i=0\ \text{for}\ i\notin W,
\]
while primal feasibility may initially fail. A violated inequality is selected and introduced into \(W\); the primal variables and working multipliers are moved along a direction preserving stationarity. The step ends either when the new constraint becomes satisfied or when an existing multiplier reaches zero, in which case its constraint leaves \(W\). If the process reaches \(Ax=b\), \(Gx\le h\), and complementary slackness, the maintained invariants constitute the convex-QP KKT conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual active-set methods preserve stationarity and nonnegative multipliers while adding violated constraints and dropping constraints whose multipliers reach zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Active-Set Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Dual active-set invariants and constraint transitions depend on the precise algorithmic variant. The generic description cannot be validated without a cited formulation and locator.

children.title: Infeasible-Start Active-Set Methods
children.top_down_role: Active-set organizations that do not require a primal-feasible initial point.

assumptions_latex: \(Q\succeq0\), and the original linear constraints are consistent when Phase I attains zero violation.
The Phase-I subproblem is solved to its KKT termination criterion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the optimal Phase-I violation is zero, the resulting point initializes a primal-feasible active-set phase; if it is positive, the original QP is infeasible under an exact Phase-I formulation.

notation.meaning: Nonnegative elastic variables measuring constraint violation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-phase active-set organization using an exact linear feasibility phase.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given an arbitrary \(x^0\), introduce nonnegative elastic variables and solve the Phase-I linear program
\[
\min_{x,v^+,v^-,w}\ \mathbf1^{\mathsf T}(v^++v^-+w)
\]
subject to
\[
Ax-b=v^+-v^-,\qquad Gx-h\le w,\qquad v^+,v^-,w\ge0,
\]
using working-set changes. If its optimum is positive, report primal infeasibility. If its optimum is zero, retain the resulting active constraints and use the feasible \(x\) to initialize an ordinary primal-feasible active-set method for the original convex QP. Thus the original method requires no feasible supplied starting point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An elastic Phase I either constructs a feasible point and working set for the QP or certifies infeasibility through positive minimum violation.
knowledge_statements.title: Infeasible-Start Active-Set Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The elastic Phase-I formulation is mathematically plausible and fits the terminal container, but its infeasibility-certificate interpretation and working-set organization require an authoritative source.

children.title: Working-Set Factorization Maintenance
children.top_down_role: Basis and factorization reuse across working-set modifications.

assumptions_latex: The active rows in \(A_W\) are linearly independent and the current equality-QP KKT matrix is nonsingular.
A working-set change adds or removes one constraint at a time.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each face change can be represented as a bordered update or downdate of the current KKT factorization; a fresh factorization is required when independence, inertia, or numerical-stability tests fail.

notation.meaning: Matrix containing equality and working-set constraint rows.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-constraint maintenance of equality-QP KKT factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a working set \(W\), store a stable factorization of
\[
K_W=\begin{bmatrix}Q&A_W^{\mathsf T}\\A_W&0\end{bmatrix}.
\]
When a constraint row \(a^{\mathsf T}\) enters, form the bordered matrix
\[
K_{W+}=\begin{bmatrix}K_W&d\\d^{\mathsf T}&0\end{bmatrix},
\qquad d=\begin{bmatrix}a\\0\end{bmatrix},
\]
and extend the factors by a bordered symmetric-indefinite update. When a row leaves, delete its multiplier row and column and downdate the factors. After either operation, test rank, pivot quality, residual, and inertia; recompute a factorization of \(K_W\) whenever a test fails. Solve subsequent working-set systems with the maintained factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reuse the KKT factors after each single constraint addition or deletion, but refactor whenever rank, pivots, residuals, or inertia become unreliable.
knowledge_statements.title: Working-Set Factorization Maintenance

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bordered KKT update representation fits the node, but the update/downdate procedure and rank, inertia, residual, and pivot tests are implementation-specific and unsupported by a citation.

children.title: Active-Set Degeneracy Controls
children.top_down_role: Anti-cycling, dependence handling, and weak-activity mechanisms.

assumptions_latex: The convex QP uses a finite indexed family of linear inequalities.
Working-set choices are ordered by a fixed index order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dependence rejection keeps the working-set equations well posed, while lexicographic selection makes every ambiguous add/drop decision deterministic and prevents repetition of an identical degenerate working-set state.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lexicographic and rank-revealing controls for degenerate active-set iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Before adding inequality \(i\), accept its row only if a rank-revealing factorization gives
\[
\operatorname{dist}(G_i^{\mathsf T},\operatorname{range}(A_W^{\mathsf T}))>\tau_{\mathrm{rank}};
\]
otherwise retain it as weakly active without enlarging the independent basis. When several constraints block at the same step, add the smallest indexed admissible one. When a zero direction has several multipliers below \(-\tau_\lambda\), remove the smallest indexed minimizer. Multipliers with magnitude at most \(\tau_\lambda\) are treated as weakly active. Record visited degenerate working sets and forbid a zero-length transition that recreates the same ordered state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank tests reject dependent rows, tolerances classify weak activity, and fixed lexicographic choices resolve ties and suppress degenerate cycling.
knowledge_statements.title: Active-Set Degeneracy Controls

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The listed controls fit the topic, but the claim that these particular lexicographic, tolerance, and visited-state rules prevent repeated degenerate states needs a precise anti-cycling theorem and finite-precision model.

children.title: Primal Barrier QP Methods
children.top_down_role: Interior methods centered on primal barrier subproblems.

assumptions_latex: \(Q\succeq0\), and the set \(\{x:Ax=b,\ Gx<h\}\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any minimizer of the barrier subproblem satisfies equality feasibility and the perturbed KKT equations with strictly positive slacks and multipliers; decreasing \(\mu\) traces the primal barrier path.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logarithmic primal barrier method for linearly constrained convex QPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a decreasing sequence \(\mu_j\downarrow0\), approximately solve
\[
\min_{Ax=b,\,Gx<h}\ \tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x-\mu_j\sum_{i=1}^m\log(h_i-G_i x).
\]
Initialize each subproblem from the preceding strictly feasible solution and apply damped Newton steps that preserve \(Gx<h\). With \(s=h-Gx\) and \(z_i=\mu_j/s_i\), a stationary point obeys
\[
Qx+c+A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}z=0,\quad Ax=b,\quad Gx+s=h,\quad Sz=\mu_j\mathbf1,
\]
with \(s,z>0\). Stop the outer iteration when the chosen primal, dual, and complementarity tolerances hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve logarithmic-barrier QPs for decreasing positive parameters, using damped Newton steps that keep every inequality strictly feasible.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal Barrier QP Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The barrier equations are consistent with the stated inequality convention, but no authoritative source supports the algorithm. Strict feasibility and positive semidefiniteness alone also do not guarantee existence of a barrier-subproblem minimizer, although the conditional stationarity claim remains plausible.

children.title: Primal–Dual Path-Following QP Methods
children.top_down_role: Coupled primal-dual trajectory methods for convex QPs.

assumptions_latex: \(Q\succeq0\), and strictly feasible primal and dual points exist.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Maintaining the perturbed KKT residuals near zero while \(\mu\downarrow0\) drives complementarity to zero; every accumulation point satisfying zero residuals is a primal-dual QP solution.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Short-step-style perturbed-KKT path following without a complexity claim.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Apply Newton's method to the perturbed KKT system
\[
Qx+c+A^{\mathsf T}y+G^{\mathsf T}z=0,\quad Ax=b,\quad Gx+s=h,
\]
\[
s>0,
\quad z>0,
\quad Sz=\mu\mathbf1.
\]
At each iteration choose a smaller target \(\mu^+\in(0,\mu)\), compute the Newton direction for the residual equations with complementarity target \(\mu^+\mathbf1\), and take a fraction-to-boundary step preserving \(s,z>0\) and the prescribed central-path neighborhood. Terminate when primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and \(s^{\mathsf T}z/m\) meet their tolerances; return \(x\) and the multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Newton steps track the perturbed primal-dual KKT system while positivity is preserved and the complementarity parameter decreases to zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Path-Following QP Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The perturbed-KKT path-following description fits the node, but the prescribed central-path neighborhood and supported convergence variant are unspecified and uncited.

children.title: Predictor–Corrector QP Methods
children.top_down_role: Primal-dual variants combining affine prediction and centrality correction.

assumptions_latex: \(Q\succeq0\), with current primal-dual variables satisfying \(s>0\) and \(z>0\).
The Newton systems used for the affine and corrected directions are solvable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The combined direction incorporates both the affine estimate of progress toward complementarity zero and a correction toward the central path while retaining one common KKT coefficient matrix.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mehrotra-type affine predictor and second-order centering correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
First solve the primal-dual Newton equations with complementarity target zero to obtain the affine direction. Compute its maximal positivity-preserving step and the predicted complementarity \(\mu_{\mathrm{aff}}\); choose, for example,
\[
\sigma=(\mu_{\mathrm{aff}}/\mu)^3.
\]
Using the same KKT coefficient matrix, solve a corrected system whose complementarity right-hand side is
\[
\sigma\mu\mathbf1-Sz-\Delta s^{\mathrm{aff}}\circ\Delta z^{\mathrm{aff}}.
\]
Combine the predictor and correction directions, take a fraction-to-boundary step maintaining \(s,z>0\), and repeat until primal residual, dual residual, and complementarity meet their stopping tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine Newton prediction estimates achievable complementarity, then a second-order correction restores centrality before a positivity-preserving step.
knowledge_statements.title: Predictor–Corrector QP Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The formula resembles a Mehrotra predictor-corrector step, but its centering rule and complementarity right-hand-side convention are variant-dependent and require a specific authoritative citation.

children.title: Interior-Point KKT Reductions
children.top_down_role: Normal-equation, augmented-system, and saddle-point realizations.

assumptions_latex: The equality rows have the rank needed for the selected reduced system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Eliminating slack and inequality-multiplier directions yields an augmented equality-constrained system with Hessian \(Q+G^{\mathsf T}S^{-1}ZG\); further elimination gives normal equations when their Schur complement is nonsingular.

notation.meaning: Dual, equality, inequality, and complementarity residuals.
Positive diagonal slack and multiplier matrices.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic reduction of a primal-dual Newton system for linear inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The Newton equations are
\[
Q\Delta x+A^{\mathsf T}\Delta y+G^{\mathsf T}\Delta z=-r_d,
\quad A\Delta x=-r_e,
\]
\[
G\Delta x+\Delta s=-r_g,
\quad Z\Delta s+S\Delta z=-r_c.
\]
Eliminating \(\Delta s\) and \(\Delta z\) gives
\[
\begin{bmatrix}H&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix}\Delta x\\\Delta y\end{bmatrix}
=
\begin{bmatrix}-r_d+G^{\mathsf T}S^{-1}r_c-G^{\mathsf T}S^{-1}Zr_g\\-r_e\end{bmatrix},
\quad H=Q+G^{\mathsf T}S^{-1}ZG.
\]
When \(H\) is invertible, eliminating \(\Delta x\) produces normal equations in \(\Delta y\); back-substitution recovers all remaining directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Slack and inequality-multiplier elimination converts the full Newton equations into an augmented KKT system, with optional further reduction to normal equations.
knowledge_statements.title: Interior-Point KKT Reductions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed elimination and reduced augmented system are internally consistent, but no source with an inspectable locator supports this representation.

children.title: Homogeneous-Embedding QP Methods
children.top_down_role: Unified architectures for solutions and infeasibility certificates.

assumptions_latex: The convex QP is represented in a specified conic primal-dual form.
The chosen homogeneous self-dual embedding preserves the conic dual pairing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A nonzero embedding solution with positive scaling recovers primal-dual QP solutions; an embedding solution with zero scaling and positive certificate variable yields a verifiable primal- or dual-infeasibility certificate according to its nonzero ray.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convention-independent certificate split for homogeneous self-dual QP embeddings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A homogeneous self-dual embedding augments the conic primal-dual QP equations with \(\tau\ge0\) and \(\kappa\ge0\), producing a homogeneous feasibility system \(\mathcal E(u,\tau,\kappa)=0\) whose complementarity relation includes
\[
\tau\kappa=0.
\]
For any nonzero solution, the outcome is interpreted as follows: if \(\tau>0\), divide the embedded primal and dual variables by \(\tau\) to recover variables satisfying the original KKT system. If \(\tau=0\) and \(\kappa>0\), the nonzero primal or dual ray encoded in \(u\) must satisfy the corresponding Farkas inequalities and strict separating inequality, thereby certifying dual or primal infeasibility. The precise ray equations depend on the selected conic QP convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A homogeneous embedding returns either scaled primal-dual solutions or, when its solution scale vanishes, a Farkas-type infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Homogeneous-Embedding QP Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A convention-independent description is insufficient to verify recovery and infeasibility-certificate claims. The exact embedding, conic form, ray inequalities, and outcome conditions must be fixed and cited; the method-family container may also call for an algorithm record rather than a standalone certificate.

children.title: Gradient-Projection QP Methods
children.top_down_role: Projection and face-restricted methods for bound and simple-polyhedral QPs.

children.title: Projected-Gradient Face Identification
children.top_down_role: Projection-based identification of a candidate active face.

assumptions_latex: \(C=\{x:Ax=b,\ Gx\le h\}\) is nonempty and polyhedral.
The projected-gradient iterates converge to \(x^*\), and \(-\nabla f(x^*)\in\operatorname{ri}N_C(x^*)\).
The stepsizes remain in a compact subset of \((0,2/L)\), where \(\nabla f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists \(K\) such that every \(x^k\) with \(k\ge K\) lies in the minimal face of \(C\) containing \(x^*\); equivalently, the locally active face is identified in finitely many projected-gradient iterations.

notation.meaning: Euclidean projection onto the feasible polyhedron.
Normal cone of the feasible set at the limit point.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite minimal-face identification under polyhedral nondegeneracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
x^{k+1}=P_C\bigl(x^k-\alpha_k\nabla f(x^k)\bigr)
\]
for a convex differentiable function \(f\) with \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient on a neighborhood of the polyhedron \(C\). Suppose \(x^k\to x^*\), the stepsizes satisfy \(0<\underline\alpha\le\alpha_k\le\overline\alpha<2/L\), and the nondegeneracy condition
\[
-\nabla f(x^*)\in\operatorname{ri}N_C(x^*)
\]
holds. Then the projected-gradient mapping identifies the minimal face \(F_*\) containing \(x^*\): there exists \(K\) such that \(x^k\in F_*\) for every \(k\ge K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under polyhedral nondegeneracy and convergence, projected-gradient iterates enter the solution's minimal face after finitely many iterations and remain there.
knowledge_statements.title: Projected-Gradient Face Identification

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited section supports only face terminology, not the finite-identification result. The claim is theorem-shaped rather than a generic property and requires an authoritative theorem citation establishing these precise hypotheses and conclusion.

children.title: Cauchy-Point Family
children.top_down_role: First-stage projected-search constructions for bound-constrained QPs.

knowledge_statements.title: Cauchy-Point Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact projected-ray Cauchy point for a convex bound-constrained quadratic program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(Q\succeq0\), \(q\in\mathbb R^n\), finite or infinite componentwise bounds \(\ell<u\), and a feasible point \(x\), set \(g=Qx+q\) and define \(x(t)=\Pi_{[\ell,u]}(x-tg)\) for \(t\ge0\). Choose the smallest global minimizer \(t_C\) of \(\phi(t)=\tfrac12x(t)^\top Qx(t)+q^\top x(t)\), and return \(x_C=x(t_C)\). The one-dimensional function \(\phi\) is continuous and piecewise quadratic, with breakpoints where components of the projected ray encounter bounds; thus \(t_C\) can be found by traversing these breakpoints and minimizing each quadratic piece.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Project the negative-gradient ray onto the box, minimize the quadratic along this piecewise-linear path, and return the earliest minimizing point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_C\in[\ell,u]\) and \(f(x_C)=\min_{t\ge0}f(\Pi_{[\ell,u]}(x-t\nabla f(x)))\).

notation.meaning: Euclidean projection onto the bound box
Gradient of the quadratic at the current point

children.title: Face-Restricted Subspace Minimization
children.top_down_role: Higher-accuracy minimization over the free-variable subspace of a candidate face.

knowledge_statements.title: Face-Restricted Subspace Minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact or approximate convex-QP minimization on a face selected by fixed bound variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+q^\top x\) on \([\ell,u]\), let disjoint sets \(L,U\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) specify a candidate face and let \(F\) be their complement. Fix \(x_L=\ell_L\) and \(x_U=u_U\), and compute a minimizer \(x_F^+\) of the reduced convex quadratic over \(\ell_F\le x_F\le u_F\). Equivalently, its Hessian is \(Q_{FF}\) and its linear coefficient is \(q_F+Q_{FL}\ell_L+Q_{FU}u_U\). Return \(x^+=(\ell_L,x_F^+,u_U)\), or an approximate reduced solution satisfying a prescribed projected-gradient tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fix variables defining the candidate face and minimize the remaining convex quadratic over its free coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^+\in\operatorname*{argmin}\{f(x):x_L=\ell_L,\ x_U=u_U,\ \ell_F\le x_F\le u_F\}\) in the exact variant.

notation.meaning: Indices fixed at lower and upper bounds
Coordinates free on the candidate face

children.title: Projected-Newton QP Methods
children.top_down_role: Projection combined with curvature-informed free-variable models.

knowledge_statements.title: Projected-Newton QP Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularized Newton steps on free variables followed by projection and globalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a feasible iterate \(x^k\) for \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+q^\top x\), choose a free set \(F_k\) and a regularization \(\delta_k>0\). Set \(p_{F_k}=-(Q_{F_kF_k}+\delta_k I)^{-1}(Qx^k+q)_{F_k}\) and \(p_i=0\) otherwise. Select \(\alpha_k>0\) by a line search requiring sufficient decrease of \(f\) along \(x(\alpha)=\Pi_{[\ell,u]}(x^k+\alpha p)\), then set \(x^{k+1}=x(\alpha_k)\). Stop when the projected-gradient residual \(\|x^k-\Pi_{[\ell,u]}(x^k-(Qx^k+q))\|\) is below the prescribed tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve a regularized Newton model on selected free coordinates, project the trial point onto the box, and globalize by line search.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{k+1}\in[\ell,u]\), with termination based on a computable first-order stationarity residual.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard projected reduced-Newton template for bound-constrained convex QPs
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Bound-Form ADMM QP
children.top_down_role: Operator splitting aligned with the OSQP two-sided affine-bound representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Form ADMM QP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-block ADMM for the OSQP-style affine-bound formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_x\tfrac12x^\top Px+q^\top x\) subject to \(\ell\le Ax\le u\), introduce \(z=Ax\). Given \(x^0,z^0,y^0\), \(\sigma>0\), and \(\rho>0\), compute \(x^{k+1}\) as the minimizer of \(\tfrac12x^\top Px+q^\top x+\tfrac\sigma2\|x-x^k\|_2^2+\tfrac\rho2\|Ax-z^k+\rho^{-1}y^k\|_2^2\). Then set \(z^{k+1}=\Pi_{[\ell,u]}(Ax^{k+1}+\rho^{-1}y^k)\) and \(y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho(Ax^{k+1}-z^{k+1})\). Stop when primal and dual residuals meet specified absolute-relative tolerances, and output \(x^{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Split the affine image from its bounds, alternate a regularized quadratic solve with box projection, and update the constraint multiplier.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each \(z\)-update satisfies \(z^{k+1}\in[\ell,u]\), and the residuals provide the stated stopping test.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard proximal ADMM splitting of a convex QP in two-sided affine-bound form
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proximal ADMM iteration fits the OSQP-style affine-bound container and is algebraically coherent, but no OSQP or ADMM source is cited and the referenced absolute-relative residual tests are not defined.

children.title: Direct Linear-System Mode
children.top_down_role: Factorization-based realization of splitting subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Direct Linear-System Mode
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quasi-definite saddle-point realization of the bound-form ADMM quadratic update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the bound-form ADMM iteration, the quadratic update is equivalently obtained from the linear system \[\begin{pmatrix}P+\sigma I&A^\top\\A&-\rho^{-1}I\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}x^{k+1}\\\nu^{k+1}\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}\sigma x^k-q\\z^k-\rho^{-1}y^k\end{pmatrix}.\] With \(\sigma>0\) and \(\rho>0\), the leading block is positive definite and the lower diagonal block is negative definite, so the coefficient matrix is nonsingular. Direct mode forms and factorizes this matrix, reusing the factorization while \(P,A,\sigma,\rho\) remain fixed; the resulting \(x^{k+1}\) is the unique minimizer of the ADMM quadratic subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Represent the ADMM quadratic update by a nonsingular quasi-definite saddle-point system and solve it using a reusable direct factorization.

children.title: Indirect Linear-System Mode
children.top_down_role: Iterative realization of splitting subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Indirect Linear-System Mode
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterative positive-definite normal-equation realization of the ADMM quadratic update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), form the operator \(H=P+\sigma I+\rho A^\top A\) and right-hand side \(b^k=\sigma x^k-q+A^\top(\rho z^k-y^k)\). Starting from a chosen initial guess, apply a symmetric positive-definite iterative linear solver, such as preconditioned conjugate gradients, to \(Hx=b^k\) until \(\|Hx-b^k\|\le\eta_k\). Use the resulting vector as the inexact \(x^{k+1}\), then perform the usual projection and multiplier updates. Exact solution gives the same \(x^{k+1}\) as direct mode; an inexact implementation must prescribe the tolerance sequence \((\eta_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply an iterative positive-definite solver to the ADMM normal equations, with an explicit inner residual tolerance, instead of factorizing a saddle-point matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H\succ0\); when \(\eta_k=0\), the computed update equals the exact bound-form ADMM quadratic minimizer.

knowledge_statements.title: QP Data Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive diagonal variable, constraint, and objective scaling of affine-bound QP data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min_x\tfrac12x^\top Px+q^\top x\) subject to \(\ell\le Ax\le u\). Let \(D\succ0\) and \(E\succ0\) be diagonal and let \(c>0\). Under \(x=D\bar x\), an equivalent scaled problem has \(\bar P=cD^\top PD\), \(\bar q=cD^\top q\), \(\bar A=EAD\), \(\bar\ell=E\ell\), and \(\bar u=Eu\). Its objective equals \(c\) times the original objective and its feasible points correspond bijectively through \(x=D\bar x\); hence positive scaling preserves primal minimizers after mapping back.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive diagonal changes of variables and constraints, plus positive objective scaling, produce an equivalent affine-bound QP with transformed data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x^*\) solves the scaled QP if and only if \(x^*=D\bar x^*\) solves the original QP.

children.title: Residual-Based Penalty Selection

knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Based Penalty Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safeguarded ADMM penalty selection by balancing normalized primal and dual residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a penalty-update checkpoint, compute primal and dual residual measures \(R_p=\|r_p^k\|_\infty/s_p^k\) and \(R_d=\|r_d^k\|_\infty/s_d^k\), where \(s_p^k,s_d^k>0\) are declared scaling factors. For safeguards \(0<\rho_{\min}\le\rho_{\max}\), define \(\widehat\rho=\rho_k\sqrt{R_p/R_d}\) when \(R_pR_d>0\), with specified conventions when either residual vanishes. Set \(\rho_{k+1}=\min\{\rho_{\max},\max\{\rho_{\min},\widehat\rho\}\}\), and retain \(\rho_k\) when the proposed multiplicative change lies inside a prescribed no-update band.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compare normalized primal and dual residuals, propose a square-root penalty correction, and apply bounds and a no-update safeguard.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_{k+1}\in[\rho_{\min},\rho_{\max}]\), with increases favored when \(R_p>R_d\) and decreases when \(R_p<R_d\).

notation.meaning: Normalized primal and dual residual measures

children.title: Adaptive Penalty Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Penalty Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Checkpointed, safeguarded piecewise-constant penalty adaptation for bound-form ADMM.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose checkpoints \(0=k_0<k_1<\cdots\), bounds \(0<\rho_{\min}\le\rho_{\max}\), and a residual-based proposal rule. Keep \(\rho_k\) fixed for \(k_j\le k<k_{j+1}\). At checkpoint \(k_{j+1}\), accept a safeguarded proposal \(\rho^+\) only if it differs from the current value by more than a prescribed multiplicative threshold; otherwise retain \(\rho_k\). If an unscaled multiplier \(y^k\) is stored, it is unchanged when \(\rho\) changes; if the scaled multiplier \(w^k=y^k/\rho_k\) is stored, reset \(w^k\leftarrow y^k/\rho^+\). Rebuild penalty-dependent linear-system data before continuing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hold the penalty fixed between checkpoints, accept only material safeguarded changes, preserve the unscaled multiplier, and refresh penalty-dependent solver data.
assumptions_latex: Penalty proposals lie in a positive safeguard interval
The multiplier storage convention is declared

children.title: Scaling–Penalty Interaction

knowledge_statements.title: Scaling–Penalty Interaction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transformation of ADMM residuals under diagonal QP scaling and its effect on penalty balance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the scaling \(x=D\bar x\), \(\bar z=Ez\), and objective multiplier \(c>0\), consistent dual variables satisfy \(y=E\bar y/c\). Consequently the scaled feasibility residual is \(\bar r_p=E(Ax-z)=Er_p\), while the scaled stationarity residual is \(\bar r_d=cD(Px+q+A^\top y)=cDr_d\). Thus nonuniform \(D\) and \(E\) generally change residual norms and their ratio. A scalar ADMM penalty selected by residual balancing is therefore coordinate-system dependent; scaling and penalty adaptation must be interpreted together rather than as independent numerical choices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Diagonal scaling changes primal and dual residual norms differently, so a scalar penalty chosen by residual balancing depends on the scaled coordinates.
assumptions_latex: Primal and dual variables use the stated scaling convention
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: In general, \(\|\bar r_p\|/\|\bar r_d\|\neq\|r_p\|/\|r_d\|\); hence scalar residual-balanced penalty updates are not invariant under nonuniform data scaling.

children.title: Active-Set Polishing

knowledge_statements.title: Active-Set Polishing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained refinement using an active pattern inferred from an approximate affine-bound QP solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an approximate solution of \(\min_x\tfrac12x^\top Px+q^\top x\) subject to \(\ell\le Ax\le u\), infer disjoint candidate sets \(L\) and \(U\) of constraints active at lower and upper bounds. Form \(A_W\) from their rows and \(b_W=(\ell_L,u_U)\), then solve the regularized equality-constrained KKT system for \(Px+q+A_W^\top\lambda_W\approx0\) and \(A_Wx=b_W\). Accept the polished point only if all affine bounds hold, lower-active multipliers have the lower-bound sign, upper-active multipliers have the upper-bound sign, and the chosen KKT residual is smaller; otherwise retain the original iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Guess active affine bounds, solve the resulting equality-constrained QP, and accept refinement only after feasibility, multiplier-sign, and residual checks.

children.title: Coordinate-Descent QP Methods

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate-Descent QP Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact scalar minimization for box-constrained convex quadratics with positive coordinate curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Qx+q^\top x\) on \([\ell,u]\), choose coordinates \(i_k\) cyclically or by a declared selection rule. Assuming \(Q_{i_ki_k}>0\), update only that coordinate by \[x_{i_k}^{k+1}=\Pi_{[\ell_{i_k},u_{i_k}]}\!\left(x_{i_k}^k-\frac{(Qx^k+q)_{i_k}}{Q_{i_ki_k}}\right),\qquad x_j^{k+1}=x_j^k\quad(j\ne i_k).\] This is the exact minimizer of \(f\) with all other coordinates fixed. Stop after a sweep when a prescribed norm of the coordinatewise projected-gradient residual is below tolerance, and output the current feasible iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly minimize the quadratic exactly along one bounded coordinate while holding all other coordinates fixed, then stop using projected stationarity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every update remains feasible and satisfies \(f(x^{k+1})\le f(x^k)\).

notation.meaning: Projection onto the scalar coordinate interval

assumptions_latex: \(Q\succeq 0\) and \(C=C_1\times\cdots\times C_p\), where every \(C_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n_i}\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact cyclic or essentially cyclic minimization over Cartesian block constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x^0\in C\), choose a cyclic or essentially cyclic sequence \((i_k)_{k\geq0}\subseteq\{1,\ldots,p\}\). At iteration \(k\), compute
\[
x_{i_k}^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\in C_{i_k}} f(x_{-i_k}^k,u),
\]
and set \(x_j^{k+1}=x_j^k\) for every \(j\neq i_k\). Stop when a prescribed block-stationarity residual, objective decrease, or iteration limit meets its tolerance; otherwise continue. Return the final feasible iterate. Exact minimization gives \(f(x^{k+1})\leq f(x^k)\).

children.title: Dual-Decomposition QP Methods

assumptions_latex: \(Q_i\succeq0\), each \(X_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n_i}\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and every local infimum is attained.
A dual optimal multiplier exists; convergence additionally requires a valid subgradient stepsize rule.
