knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-coupled separable convex QPs with subgradient coordination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For
\[
\min_{x_i\in X_i}\ \sum_{i=1}^p f_i(x_i)\quad\text{subject to}\quad\sum_{i=1}^p A_ix_i=b,
\]
initialize \(\lambda^0\). At iteration \(k\), solve in parallel
\[
x_i^k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x_i\in X_i}\bigl(f_i(x_i)+(\lambda^k)^{\mathsf T}A_ix_i\bigr),
\]
then update \(\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+\alpha_k(\sum_iA_ix_i^k-b)\), where \(\alpha_k>0\). Stop at prescribed primal-residual and dual-progress tolerances or an iteration limit. Return the final multiplier and a stated primal recovery, such as an ergodic average.

children.title: Ellipsoid Complexity Route
children.top_down_role: Oracle-based polynomial solvability for convex quadratic models.

knowledge_statements.title: Ellipsoid Complexity Route
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak bit-complexity statement under explicit separation and radius promises.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\leq b,\ Ex=d\}\) and \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\). Apply the ellipsoid method to feasibility subproblems for the epigraph sections
\[
K_t=\{x\in F:f(x)\leq t\},
\]
using separating hyperplanes obtained from violated linear constraints or the convex gradient inequality. With polynomially encoded initial bounds for the objective search, binary search on \(t\) returns \(x_\varepsilon\in F\) satisfying
\[
f(x_\varepsilon)\leq\min_{x\in F}f(x)+\varepsilon
\]
after \(\operatorname{poly}(n,L,\log(1/\varepsilon))\) bit operations and oracle calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With rational data, polynomial-time separation access, encoded geometric and objective bounds, and a bounded feasible region, the ellipsoid method finds an additive-epsilon solution in weakly polynomial time.
assumptions_latex: The convex QP has rational data of total encoding length \(L\), a nonempty bounded feasible region, and \(Q\succeq0\).
A polynomial-time strong separation oracle, polynomially encoded inner and outer radius bounds, and polynomially encoded initial objective-search bounds are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An ellipsoid reduction computes an \(\varepsilon\)-optimal feasible solution using a number of bit operations and oracle calls polynomial in \(n\), \(L\), and \(\log(1/\varepsilon)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: separation-based ellipsoid optimization gives weakly polynomial approximate solvability
authoritative support is required for the oracle and bit-complexity bound

children.title: Interior-Point Complexity Route
children.top_down_role: Barrier and path-following polynomial solvability for convex QPs.

assumptions_latex: \(Q\succeq0\), the inequality-feasible region has a strictly feasible point, and the optimal value is finite.
Newton systems are solved to the accuracy required by a short-step path-following method.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A short-step logarithmic-barrier method reaches duality gap at most \(\varepsilon\) in \(O(\sqrt{m}\log(\mu_0/\varepsilon))\) Newton steps.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: logarithmic barriers have parameter proportional to the number of inequalities
exact bound requires source confirmation for the selected primal-dual QP formulation
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Short-step path following for strictly feasible linearly constrained convex QPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the convex QP with affine inequalities \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x<b_i\), follow the minimizers of
\[
\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x-\mu\sum_{i=1}^m\log(b_i-a_i^{\mathsf T}x)
\]
subject to any affine equalities, decreasing \(\mu\) by the standard short-step factor and restoring the prescribed central-neighborhood condition with Newton steps. Starting at central parameter \(\mu_0\), the method obtains a primal-dual point with duality gap at most \(\varepsilon\) in
\[
O\!\left(\sqrt m\log\frac{\mu_0}{\varepsilon}\right)
\]
Newton steps; each step requires forming and solving the associated linear system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A short-step logarithmic-barrier method solves a strictly feasible convex QP to epsilon duality gap in order square-root-m times a logarithmic factor.
knowledge_statements.title: Interior-Point Complexity Route

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind fits the interior-point route, but the exact short-step bound depends on whether the initial scale denotes the barrier parameter or the duality gap and on the chosen primal-dual formulation. A specific source is required.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical binary representation of rational convex-QP coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Represent every rational coefficient \(r\) uniquely as \(r=p/q\), where \(p\in\mathbb{Z}\), \(q\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}\), and \(\gcd(|p|,q)=1\). Encode the sign of \(p\) and the unsigned binary expansions of \(|p|\) and \(q\), using a self-delimiting convention. One admissible coefficient-length measure is
\[
\ell(r)=1+\lceil\log_2(|p|+1)\rceil+\lceil\log_2(q+1)\rceil,
\]
up to fixed delimiter overhead. A rational QP is encoded by its dimensions, matrix sparsity or dense layout, and the ordered encodings of all entries of \(Q,c,A,b,E,d\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bit complexity for explicitly requested approximate QP solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T(\mathcal I,\varepsilon)\) be the number of bit operations used to produce \(x_\varepsilon\) satisfying the stated feasibility tolerance and
\[
f(x_\varepsilon)\leq f^\star+\varepsilon.
\]
A precision-dependent polynomial bound has the form
\[
T(\mathcal I,\varepsilon)\leq \operatorname{poly}\bigl(n,m,L,\log(1/\varepsilon)\bigr).
\]
The dependence on \(\log(1/\varepsilon)\) counts requested binary digits of accuracy. A bound polynomial in \(1/\varepsilon\) is polynomial in the reciprocal tolerance but is not, by that fact alone, polynomial in the binary length of the accuracy request.

existence for general convex QP classes is not asserted
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complexity-class definition, not an existence claim for unrestricted convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A rational-QP algorithm is strongly polynomial if there is a polynomial \(P\) such that it performs at most \(P(n,m)\) arithmetic operations and comparisons, independently of coefficient magnitudes and the input length \(L\), and if every intermediate rational has encoding length bounded by a polynomial in \(L,n,m\). These two requirements imply polynomial Turing running time while keeping the combinatorial operation count independent of numerical values. Merely obtaining a bound polynomial in \(L\), or counting unit-cost operations on arbitrarily large numbers, does not establish strong polynomiality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong polynomiality requires dimension-polynomial arithmetic work independent of coefficient sizes, plus polynomial bounds on all intermediate number lengths.
knowledge_statements.title: Strongly Polynomial Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the Strongly Polynomial Regime and does not assert existence for general convex QP. The two-part definition requires an authoritative, specifically located complexity source.

children.title: Arithmetic Complexity Regime
children.top_down_role: Operation-count guarantees abstracting away finite-precision bit costs.

assumptions_latex: Each exact real-arithmetic operation and comparison is assigned unit cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An arithmetic complexity bound counts operations over the chosen exact-arithmetic model and does not alone imply polynomial bit complexity.

notation.meaning: Number of unit-cost arithmetic operations and comparisons.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: arithmetic and Turing models differ by treatment of operand size
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unit-cost exact-arithmetic model for QP algorithm analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the arithmetic complexity regime, an algorithm's cost \(N_{\mathrm{arith}}\) is the number of additions, subtractions, multiplications, divisions, and comparisons performed over the specified exact field, each charged unit cost. A bound such as \(N_{\mathrm{arith}}\leq P(n,m)\) controls the number of algebraic steps but ignores the bit lengths of operands and results. Therefore it yields a Turing-model polynomial bound only when coefficient access, rounding conventions if any, and polynomial bounds on all intermediate encodings are supplied separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Arithmetic complexity counts exact algebraic operations at unit cost; without operand-size bounds, it does not establish polynomial bit complexity.
knowledge_statements.title: Arithmetic Complexity Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the arithmetic-complexity terminal and correctly warns that unit-cost arithmetic does not alone imply bit complexity. No citation identifies the exact computational model.

children.title: Polynomiality Classification Boundary
children.top_down_role: Distinctions separating arithmetic, bit, weakly polynomial, and strongly polynomial claims.

assumptions_latex: The same rational convex-QP family is assessed under explicitly stated arithmetic, bit, exact-output, and approximate-output conventions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Polynomiality classifications are comparable only after the computational model, input encoding, output criterion, and precision parameter are fixed.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: polynomiality changes when encoding, operand cost, or precision is omitted
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between arithmetic, weak bit-polynomial, and strong polynomial claims.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The classification boundary is determined by what the running-time polynomial may depend on. A bound \(N_{\mathrm{arith}}\leq\operatorname{poly}(n,m)\) is only an arithmetic-model claim unless intermediate bit lengths are controlled. A bound \(\operatorname{poly}(n,m,L,\log(1/\varepsilon))\) is weakly polynomial for approximate rational input. Strong polynomiality additionally removes \(L\) from the arithmetic-operation count while retaining polynomial intermediate encoding lengths. Thus omitting the encoding, treating arbitrary-precision arithmetic as unit cost, or replacing \(\log(1/\varepsilon)\) by an unstated real tolerance crosses the boundary and invalidates the corresponding bit-polynomial classification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Arithmetic, weakly polynomial, and strongly polynomial claims differ by operand costs, encoding length, precision dependence, and intermediate-size control.
knowledge_statements.title: Polynomiality Classification Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind appropriately captures invalid transitions among arithmetic, weakly polynomial, and strongly polynomial claims. The distinctions are plausible and internally consistent but lack a specifically located source.

children.title: QP Algorithm Completion Guarantees
children.top_down_role: Qualitatively different guarantees associated with major QP solver families.

children.title: Active-Set Finite-Termination Regimes
children.top_down_role: Finite working-set termination under appropriate convexity and degeneracy regimes.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Section 16.5: Finite Termination of Active-Set Algorithm on Strictly Convex QPs

assumptions_latex: The feasible polyhedron is nonempty and the convex quadratic objective is bounded below on it.
Each working-set subproblem is solved exactly, and the method either strictly decreases the objective or changes the working set.
An anti-cycling rule is used; at the solution, LICQ and strict complementarity hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method reaches a primal-dual KKT point after finitely many working-set changes.

notation.meaning: Finite set of active constraint indices used by an iterate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applies to exact convex-QP active-set methods with explicit anti-cycling and nondegeneracy assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a convex quadratic program over a polyhedron with \(m\) inequalities. Suppose an active-set method associates each iterate with a working set \(W_k\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\), solves every equality-constrained working-set subproblem exactly, and accepts only a strict objective decrease or a nonrepeating working-set change. If an anti-cycling rule prevents repeated zero-length transitions, then only finitely many working sets can be visited. Under LICQ and strict complementarity at the limiting solution, the final working set identifies the active constraints and the final primal-dual iterate satisfies the KKT conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact working-set solves, strict progress, anti-cycling, LICQ, and strict complementarity make a convex-QP active-set method terminate at a KKT point after finitely many set changes.
knowledge_statements.title: Active-Set Finite-Termination Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is cited, and the stated progress rule does not by itself establish finite termination: infinitely many strict-decrease iterations are not excluded merely by finiteness of the set of working sets. A specific active-set algorithm and an authoritative finite-termination result with matching anti-cycling and degeneracy hypotheses are required.

children.title: Interior-Point Iteration Complexity
children.top_down_role: Barrier-theoretic iteration regimes for affine-constrained convex QPs.

assumptions_latex: The convex QP has affine equalities and \(m\) affine inequalities and admits a strictly feasible primal-dual point.
A short-step path-following method uses the logarithmic barrier and sufficiently accurate Newton steps.
The initial average complementarity is \(\mu_0>0\), and the requested duality gap is \(\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At most \(O\!\left(\sqrt m\log\!\left(m\mu_0/\varepsilon\right)\right)\) Newton iterations are required.

notation.meaning: Number of affine inequality constraints and logarithmic-barrier parameter

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Short-step logarithmic-barrier complexity; affine equalities do not increase the barrier parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an affine-constrained convex quadratic program with \(m\) inequalities, use the standard logarithmic barrier, whose self-concordance parameter is \(m\). Assume strict primal-dual feasibility and initialize within a fixed short-step neighborhood of the central path at average complementarity \(\mu_0\). A short-step path-following method that reduces the barrier parameter by a factor \(1-\Theta(m^{-1/2})\) and computes sufficiently accurate Newton directions produces a feasible primal-dual point with gap at most \(\varepsilon\) in \(O\!\left(\sqrt m\log\!\left(m\mu_0/\varepsilon\right)\right)\) Newton iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strictly feasible short-step logarithmic-barrier method needs order square-root-of-m times a logarithmic accuracy factor to reduce the primal-dual gap below the target.
knowledge_statements.title: Interior-Point Iteration Complexity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind fits the terminal container and the stated order is plausible for a short-step logarithmic-barrier method, but no source verifies the precise neighborhood, Newton-step accuracy, or the normalization producing the factor m mu_0 inside the logarithm.

children.title: Projection-Method Accuracy Complexity
children.top_down_role: Accuracy-dependent regimes shaped by smoothness, curvature, and domain geometry.

assumptions_latex: The feasible set \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and a minimizer \(x^*\) exists.
The objective is \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^TQx+c^Tx\) with \(0\preceq Q\preceq LI\).
For the linear regime, additionally \(Q\succeq\mu I\) with \(\mu>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The convex regime has \(O(1/k)\) objective error, while positive curvature gives geometric distance contraction.

notation.meaning: Euclidean projection onto the feasible set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean projected gradient with fixed step \(1/L\) for a convex quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_{k+1}=P_C\!\left(x_k-L^{-1}(Qx_k+c)\right)\). If \(0\preceq Q\preceq LI\), then for every minimizer \(x^*\in C\) and every \(k\ge1\), \[f(x_k)-f(x^*)\le \frac{L\lVert x_0-x^*\rVert^2}{2k}.\] Consequently, objective accuracy \(f(x_k)-f(x^*)\le\varepsilon\) requires at most \(O(L\lVert x_0-x^*\rVert^2/\varepsilon)\) projections. If also \(Q\succeq\mu I\), then \[\lVert x_k-x^*\rVert^2\le(1-\mu/L)^k\lVert x_0-x^*\rVert^2,\] giving logarithmic dependence on the requested distance accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projected gradient has inverse-accuracy complexity for a smooth convex QP and geometric convergence when the quadratic has uniformly positive curvature.
knowledge_statements.title: Projection-Method Accuracy Complexity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind and the separation between semidefinite and positive-definite curvature regimes fit the container. The formulas are mathematically plausible, but the record supplies no inspectable source for the exact projected-gradient objective and distance estimates.

children.title: Operator-Splitting Convergence Regimes
children.top_down_role: Asymptotic and conditioning-sensitive regimes for splitting-based QP solvers.

assumptions_latex: The convex QP is represented by a maximal-monotone KKT inclusion \(0\in\mathcal A(u)+\mathcal B(u)\).
The chosen splitting induces an averaged fixed-point map \(T\), and \(\operatorname{Fix}T\ne\varnothing\).
For the linear regime, \(T\) is contractive on the relevant invariant set with modulus \(q<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iterates converge asymptotically; under contraction they satisfy \(\lVert u_k-u^*\rVert\le q^k\lVert u_0-u^*\rVert\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-point formulation covering proximal, Douglas-Rachford, and related exact splitting schemes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent the convex-QP KKT system as \(0\in\mathcal A(u)+\mathcal B(u)\), where the induced exact splitting update is \(u_{k+1}=T(u_k)\). If \(T\) is averaged and has a fixed point, finite-dimensional fixed-point theory gives convergence of \(u_k\) to some \(u^*\in\operatorname{Fix}T\), and the fixed-point residual \(\lVert u_k-T(u_k)\rVert\) tends to zero. If metric regularity or an equivalent QP error bound makes \(T\) contractive with modulus \(q<1\) on the invariant set containing the iterates, then \(\lVert u_k-u^*\rVert\le q^k\lVert u_0-u^*\rVert\). The factor \(q\) depends on scaling, penalty parameters, and KKT conditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Averaged splitting maps converge asymptotically to QP KKT fixed points; an error bound that yields contraction upgrades convergence to a conditioning-dependent linear rate.
knowledge_statements.title: Operator-Splitting Convergence Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No splitting method or source is fixed. Averagedness supports finite-dimensional fixed-point convergence under appropriate assumptions, but metric regularity or a QP error bound does not generically make the update map contractive in the displayed norm. A method-specific theorem must identify the actual linear-convergence condition and rate.

children.title: Inexact Linear-Algebra Regimes
children.top_down_role: Outer-solver behavior under approximate linear-system solutions.

assumptions_latex: The exact outer iteration \(u_{k+1}=T(u_k)\) has an averaged map \(T\) with a nonempty fixed-point set.
The perturbations are absolutely summable: \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\lVert e_k\rVert<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Summable linear-solve errors preserve convergence to a fixed point; nonsummable errors need not do so.

notation.meaning: Error induced by the inexact linear solve at iteration k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic summable-error regime for averaged fixed-point QP solvers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an exact QP solver can be written as \(u_{k+1}=T(u_k)\), where \(T\) is averaged and \(\operatorname{Fix}T\ne\varnothing\). Model each approximate linear-system solution by \(u_{k+1}=T(u_k)+e_k\). The sufficient forcing condition \[\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\lVert e_k\rVert<\infty\] preserves convergence of the perturbed iterates to a point in \(\operatorname{Fix}T\). If the exact map is contractive with modulus \(q<1\) and \(\lVert e_k\rVert\le C\rho^k\) for some \(\rho<1\), then the convergence is geometric with asymptotic factor no worse than \(\max\{q,\rho\}\), up to the equal-factor polynomial prefactor.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Outer convergence survives approximate linear solves when their induced errors are summable; geometrically decaying errors preserve a geometric rate for a contractive outer map.
knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Linear-Algebra Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the inexact-linear-algebra terminal container, and summable perturbations are a standard sufficient regime for appropriate averaged iterations. An authoritative source is still required to verify the precise perturbation theorem and geometric-rate statement for the intended outer solver.

children.title: Approximate Solution Quality
children.top_down_role: Solver-independent and solver-facing measures of approximate completion.

children.title: Primal–Dual Residual Quality
children.top_down_role: Residual-based assessment of approximate feasibility and stationarity.

assumptions_latex: The QP is \(\min_x \tfrac12x^TQx+c^Tx\) subject to \(Ax=b\) and \(Gx\le h\), with \(Q\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Zero primal, dual, and complementarity residuals constitute a sufficient certificate of global optimality.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute Euclidean KKT residuals for an equality-and-inequality convex QP.

source_refs.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a candidate \((x,y,z)\) with \(z\ge0\), define \(s=h-Gx\), \(r_{\mathrm d}=Qx+c+A^Ty+G^Tz\), and \[r_{\mathrm p}=\bigl(Ax-b,\,(Gx-h)_+\bigr).\] Its absolute KKT residual quality may be measured by \[R(x,y,z)=\max\{\lVert r_{\mathrm p}\rVert_2,\lVert r_{\mathrm d}\rVert_2,\lVert z\odot s\rVert_2\}.\] The tuple is an \(\varepsilon\)-residual solution when \(R(x,y,z)\le\varepsilon\). If \(R(x,y,z)=0\), primal feasibility, dual feasibility, stationarity, and complementarity all hold; because \(Q\succeq0\), these KKT conditions certify that \(x\) is globally optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The maximum of feasibility, stationarity, and complementarity residuals measures approximate KKT quality; a zero residual certifies global optimality for the convex QP.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Residual Quality

source_witnesses.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

children.title: Duality-Gap Quality
children.top_down_role: Objective-quality assessment using primal and dual bounds.

assumptions_latex: The point \(x\) is primal feasible, and \((y,z)\) is dual feasible with \(z\ge0\).
The dual value \(d(y,z)=\inf_u L(u,y,z)\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The computable gap \(g=f(x)-d(y,z)\) is nonnegative and bounds primal objective suboptimality from above.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite dual-function gap for a primal-feasible and dual-feasible convex-QP tuple.

source_refs.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

source_refs.locator: 5.6.1 An Estimate of the Duality Gap p. 371
source_refs.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For constraints \(Ax=b\) and \(Gx\le h\), define \(L(u,y,z)=f(u)+y^T(Au-b)+z^T(Gu-h)\) with \(z\ge0\), and define \(d(y,z)=\inf_u L(u,y,z)\). For every primal-feasible \(x\) and every dual-feasible pair \((y,z)\) having finite dual value, weak duality yields \[d(y,z)\le p^*\le f(x).\] Hence the gap \(g(x,y,z)=f(x)-d(y,z)\) satisfies \(g(x,y,z)\ge0\) and \[0\le f(x)-p^*\le g(x,y,z).\] Thus \(g(x,y,z)\le\varepsilon\) certifies objective suboptimality at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible primal objective minus a feasible dual value is nonnegative and gives a computable upper bound on primal objective suboptimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Duality-Gap Quality

children.title: Nearby-QP Backward-Error Certificates
children.top_down_role: Interpretation of computed solutions as exact solutions to nearby QPs.

children.title: Backward-Error Interpretation
children.top_down_role: Interpretation of a computed point through proximity to an exactly solved nearby QP.

assumptions_latex: A norm is fixed on the QP data space.
The candidate includes primal variables and any multipliers required by the chosen exact optimality system.
Only perturbations preserving the designated QP class are admissible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Backward error is the smallest admissible data perturbation that makes the candidate an exact solution of a nearby QP.

notation.meaning: Admissible perturbation of the QP data
Backward error of a candidate tuple

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normwise backward error relative to a declared admissible class of convex-QP data perturbations.

source_refs.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(Q,c,A,b,G,h)\) denote convex-QP data and let \(w=(x,y,z)\) be a computed primal-dual tuple. For a specified admissible perturbation set \(\mathcal P\) that preserves symmetry and positive semidefiniteness of the perturbed Hessian, define the absolute backward error by \[\eta_D(w)=\inf\{\lVert\Delta D\rVert:\Delta D\in\mathcal P,\ w\text{ satisfies the exact KKT conditions for }D+\Delta D\}.\] A small value means that the computed tuple is exact for a nearby admissible QP. It does not, without conditioning assumptions, imply proximity to a solution of the original QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Backward error is the least admissible change to QP data that turns a computed primal-dual tuple into an exact KKT solution of the perturbed problem.
knowledge_statements.title: Backward-Error Interpretation

source_witnesses.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is precise and fits the terminal container, but the only citation is a general convex-programming and duality section. It does not specifically evidence the normwise backward-error definition, admissible data class, or conditioning caveat. A backward-error source with a section or theorem locator is required.

children.title: Objective-Data Perturbations
children.top_down_role: Nearby-model changes affecting linear or quadratic objective data.

assumptions_latex: The candidate \((x,y,z)\) is primal feasible, \(z\ge0\), and satisfies complementarity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Changing only \(c\) by \(\Delta c=-r_{\mathrm d}\) makes the candidate an exact KKT tuple for a convex nearby QP.

notation.meaning: Perturbation of the linear objective coefficient

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-objective perturbation certificate with all constraints and the Hessian held fixed.

source_refs.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the convex QP with data \((Q,c,A,b,G,h)\), let a candidate \((x,y,z)\) be primal feasible, satisfy \(z\ge0\), and satisfy \(z\odot(h-Gx)=0\). Define its stationarity residual by \[r_{\mathrm d}=Qx+c+A^Ty+G^Tz.\] Set \(\Delta c=-r_{\mathrm d}\) and leave \(Q,A,b,G,h\) unchanged. Then \[Qx+(c+\Delta c)+A^Ty+G^Tz=0,\] while feasibility, dual feasibility, and complementarity remain unchanged. Thus \((x,y,z)\) is an exact KKT tuple, and hence \(x\) is globally optimal, for the nearby convex QP whose linear objective coefficient is \(c+\Delta c\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a feasible complementary tuple, negating the stationarity residual as a perturbation of the linear objective coefficient makes the tuple exactly optimal for a nearby convex QP.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Data Perturbations

source_witnesses.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

children.title: Constraint-Data Perturbations
children.top_down_role: Nearby-model changes affecting affine constraints or bounds.

assumptions_latex: The candidate satisfies stationarity \(Qx+c+A^Ty+G^Tz=0\) and dual feasibility \(z\ge0\).
The matrices \(Q,A,G\) and objective vector \(c\) are held fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Explicit perturbations of \(b\) and \(h\) make the candidate primal feasible and complementary without changing stationarity.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Right-hand-side perturbation certificate with objective and constraint matrices fixed.

source_refs.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \((x,y,z)\) satisfies stationarity and \(z\ge0\). Define \(b'=Ax\). For each inequality index \(i\), define \[h'_i=\begin{cases}(Gx)_i,&z_i>0,\\ \max\{h_i,(Gx)_i\},&z_i=0.\end{cases}\] Then \(Ax=b'\), \(Gx\le h'\), and \(z_i(h'_i-(Gx)_i)=0\) for every \(i\). Because \(Q,c,A,G\) are unchanged, stationarity also remains valid. Therefore \((x,y,z)\) is an exact KKT tuple for the QP with right-hand sides \((b',h')\); the perturbations are \(\Delta b=b'-b\) and \(\Delta h=h'-h\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Changing equality and inequality right-hand sides by explicit residual-based amounts can make a stationary, dual-feasible tuple exactly feasible and complementary for a nearby QP.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Data Perturbations

source_witnesses.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

children.title: Nearby-QP Quality
children.top_down_role: Assessment of the size and interpretation of model perturbations.

assumptions_latex: Forward quality is measured by distance from the candidate to the original QP solution.
Backward quality permits perturbations of the linear objective coefficient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Arbitrarily small backward error can coexist with arbitrarily large forward solution error when curvature approaches zero.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional example separating small backward error from forward accuracy under vanishing curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\delta>0\) and \(\eta>0\), consider the unconstrained convex QP \[f_{\delta,\eta}(x)=\tfrac12\delta x^2-\eta x.\] At the computed point \(\widehat x=0\), the stationarity residual and the linear-objective backward error both equal \(\eta\): changing the linear coefficient by \(\Delta c=\eta\) makes \(\widehat x\) exact for the nearby QP \(\tfrac12\delta x^2\). However, the original minimizer is \(x^*=\eta/\delta\), so \(\lvert\widehat x-x^*\rvert=\eta/\delta\). Choosing \(\eta\to0\) and \(\delta=\eta^2\) makes backward error vanish while forward error diverges. Thus nearby-QP quality requires conditioning information for a forward interpretation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point may exactly solve an arbitrarily nearby QP yet remain arbitrarily far from the original solution when quadratic curvature becomes small.
knowledge_statements.title: Nearby-QP Quality

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind is appropriate and the one-dimensional construction internally demonstrates vanishing objective-data backward error with diverging forward error. However, the record provides neither a source nor an explicit standard-field rationale, so the nontrivial conditioning interpretation lacks required evidence.

children.title: Solver Status Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Solved, approximate, infeasible, unbounded, interrupted, and numerical-failure outcomes.

assumptions_latex: The status refers to the convex QP with constraints \(Ax=b\) and \(Gx\le h\).
Numerical tolerances and resource limits are declared before interpreting approximate or operational statuses.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Statuses separate verified solution or recession certificates from tolerance-based and operational outcomes.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mathematical core and operational boundary of common convex-QP termination statuses.

source_refs.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Use solved when an exact KKT tuple is available, and approximate when declared residual or gap tests hold only within \(\varepsilon>0\). Use primal infeasible when a Farkas certificate satisfies \(A^Ty+G^Tz=0\), \(z\ge0\), and \(b^Ty+h^Tz<0\). Use unbounded when a feasible base point and a direction \(d\) satisfy \(Ad=0\), \(Gd\le0\), \(Qd=0\), and \(c^Td<0\). Interrupted means termination by an external resource or user limit without a stronger certificate. Numerical failure means arithmetic or linear-algebra breakdown prevents any declared certificate. Operational statuses alone make no mathematical claim about feasibility or optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: QP statuses should distinguish exact or tolerance-based solutions, certificate-backed infeasibility or unboundedness, external interruption, and uncertified numerical failure.
knowledge_statements.title: Solver Status Taxonomy

children.title: QP Degeneracy-Pathology-Repair Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Mathematical and numerical regimes that make QP representations, certificates, or solver systems singular or unstable.

children.title: Constraint-Multiplier Degeneracy Coupling
children.top_down_role: Dependent active normals, redundancy, weak activity, and ambiguous multipliers.

children.title: Rank-Deficient Active Constraints
children.top_down_role: Dependent working sets and singular active-set systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Deficient Active Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex QP; rank is tested on the combined equality and active-inequality Jacobian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the convex quadratic program \(\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\tfrac12x^\top Hx+c^\top x\) subject to \(Ax\le b\) and \(Ex=d\), where \(H\in\mathbb{S}_+^n\), \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m_i\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^{m_i}\), \(E\in\mathbb{R}^{m_e\times n}\), and \(d\in\mathbb{R}^{m_e}\). At a feasible point \(x\), let \(I(x)=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,m_i\}:A_i x=b_i\}\) and \(G_I=[E^\top\ A_I^\top]^\top\). The active constraints are rank deficient at \(x\) precisely when \[\operatorname{rank}(G_I)<m_e+|I(x)|.\] Equivalently, there exist \(u\in\mathbb{R}^{m_e}\) and \(v\in\mathbb{R}^{|I(x)|}\), not both zero, such that \(E^\top u+A_I^\top v=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Active constraints are rank deficient when the equality normals and active inequality normals are linearly dependent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}(G_I)<m_e+|I(x)|\).

notation.meaning: active inequality index set at the feasible point
matrix formed from the equality rows and active inequality rows

children.title: Redundant QP Constraints
children.top_down_role: Duplicated or implied constraints affecting representation and numerics.

knowledge_statements.title: Redundant QP Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global redundancy of a represented linear constraint, independent of the quadratic objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m_i\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^{m_i}\), \(E\in\mathbb{R}^{m_e\times n}\), and \(d\in\mathbb{R}^{m_e}\), and define \(F=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\le b,\ Ex=d\}\). For \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m_i\}\), the inequality \(A_i x\le b_i\) is redundant when deleting it leaves the feasible set unchanged: \[F=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:A_{-i}x\le b_{-i},\ Ex=d\}.\] Equivalently, every point satisfying the remaining constraints also satisfies \(A_i x\le b_i\). An equality row \(E_jx=d_j\) is redundant under the analogous deletion criterion. Duplicate constraints are a special case; redundancy also includes constraints implied by nonidentical remaining constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A represented QP constraint is redundant when deleting it does not change the feasible set; duplicate constraints are one special case.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:A_{-i}x\le b_{-i},\ Ex=d\}\).

notation.meaning: feasible set of the represented QP
inequality system with row i removed

children.title: Multiplier Nonuniqueness
children.top_down_role: Dual ambiguity induced by constraint geometry.

assumptions_latex: \(x^*\) satisfies the KKT conditions of a convex QP

notation.meaning: set of KKT multiplier pairs at the fixed primal solution

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonuniqueness is defined at a fixed primal KKT solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min_x \tfrac12x^\top Hx+c^\top x\) subject to \(Ax\le b\) and \(Ex=d\), fix a KKT solution \(x^*\). Define \(\mathcal{M}(x^*)\) as the set of pairs \((\lambda,\nu)\) satisfying \[Hx^*+c+A^\top\lambda+E^\top\nu=0,\qquad \lambda\ge0,\qquad \lambda_i(A_i x^*-b_i)=0.\] Multiplier nonuniqueness occurs exactly when \(|\mathcal{M}(x^*)|>1\). Thus two distinct dual pairs certify the condition even though the primal solution is fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multipliers are nonunique when one primal KKT solution admits at least two distinct equality-and-inequality multiplier pairs.
knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier Nonuniqueness

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-primal multiplier-set condition is mathematically coherent and fits the leaf, but no inspectable source is supplied for its QP-specific formulation.

children.title: Strict-Complementarity Failure
children.top_down_role: Weakly active constraints and ambiguous dual support.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists i\in I(x^*):\lambda_i^*=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure is relative to a specified KKT multiplier vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a KKT point \((x^*,\lambda^*,\nu^*)\) of a convex QP with inequalities \(Ax\le b\), strict complementarity holds when \[A_i x^*=b_i\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\lambda_i^*>0\] for every inequality index \(i\). Strict-complementarity failure occurs when at least one active constraint is weakly active: \[\exists i\in I(x^*)\quad A_i x^*=b_i\quad\text{and}\quad\lambda_i^*=0.\] This condition concerns inequality constraints; equality multipliers have no complementary-sign requirement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict complementarity fails when an active inequality has zero multiplier at the specified KKT point.
knowledge_statements.title: Strict-Complementarity Failure

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition is valid relative to the specified KKT multiplier vector, but an authoritative source is needed to confirm that this local meaning—not failure of every possible strictly complementary multiplier—is intended.

children.title: Curvature-System Degeneracy Regimes
children.top_down_role: Singular or nearly singular curvature and KKT systems.

children.title: Singular-Hessian Regime
children.top_down_role: Flat ambient directions and nonunique unconstrained responses.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex quadratic objectives in finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the convex quadratic objective \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^\top Hx+c^\top x\) with \(H\succeq0\), the singular-Hessian regime is \[\ker(H)\neq\{0\},\] equivalently \(\operatorname{rank}(H)<n\). Every nonzero \(p\in\ker(H)\) is a zero-curvature direction because \(p^\top Hp=0\). If the unconstrained stationarity equation \(Hx=-c\) is solvable, then every solution \(x_0\) generates the affine family \(x_0+\ker(H)\) of unconstrained minimizers; otherwise singularity alone does not imply existence of a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The singular-Hessian regime occurs when the positive-semidefinite Hessian has a nonzero null direction; solvable unconstrained stationarity then yields nonunique minimizers.
knowledge_statements.title: Singular-Hessian Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The singular-Hessian condition and qualified statement about unconstrained minimizers are standard and consistent, but the record has no citation.

children.title: Singular Reduced-Hessian Regime
children.top_down_role: Flat feasible directions and singular equality subproblems.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ker(Z^\top HZ)\neq\{0\}\).

notation.meaning: independent equality or working-set constraint matrix

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained or fixed-working-set convex QP subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an equality-constrained convex QP with constraint matrix \(G\), let the columns of \(Z\) form a basis of \(\ker(G)\). The reduced Hessian is \(R=Z^\top HZ\). The singular reduced-Hessian regime occurs precisely when \[\ker(R)\neq\{0\}.\] Equivalently, there exists a nonzero feasible tangent direction \(p=Zz\) such that \(Gp=0\) and \(p^\top Hp=0\). When \(G\) has full row rank, this condition is equivalent to singularity of the saddle-point matrix \(\begin{bmatrix}H&G^\top\\G&0\end{bmatrix}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The reduced Hessian is singular when a nonzero direction tangent to the working constraints has zero quadratic curvature.
knowledge_statements.title: Singular Reduced-Hessian Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The reduced-Hessian condition, tangent-direction equivalence, and KKT singularity claim are coherent under the stated positive-semidefinite and full-row-rank assumptions, but no supporting source is supplied.

children.title: Ill-Conditioned KKT Regime
children.top_down_role: Instability caused by weak curvature and constraint coupling.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa_2(K)\ge\tau\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative spectral definition for a nonsingular equality or active-set KKT system.

source_refs.locator: 3.3 Approximation Procedures for Nondifferentiable and Ill-Conditioned Optimization Problems p. 167
source_refs.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the equality-constrained or active-set system with \(K=\begin{bmatrix}H&G^\top\\G&0\end{bmatrix}\), fix a threshold \(\tau>1\). If \(K\) is nonsingular, the system is in the ill-conditioned KKT regime when \[\kappa_2(K)=\frac{\sigma_{\max}(K)}{\sigma_{\min}(K)}\ge\tau.\] Consequently, normwise relative perturbations in the KKT right-hand side can be amplified by a factor on the order of \(\kappa_2(K)\). Rank loss of \(G\), weak reduced curvature, or their coupling can make \(\sigma_{\min}(K)\) small.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonsingular KKT system is ill conditioned when its spectral condition number exceeds a chosen threshold, permitting strong amplification of data errors.
knowledge_statements.title: Ill-Conditioned KKT Regime

source_witnesses.locator: 3.3 Approximation Procedures for Nondifferentiable and Ill-Conditioned Optimization Problems p. 167
source_witnesses.source_title: Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

children.title: Active-Set Progress Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Repeated working sets or negligible progress near degenerate faces.

children.title: Active-Set Cycling
children.top_down_role: Return to previously encountered active-set configurations.

assumptions_latex: \((x_k,W_k)\) is the deterministic state sequence of an active-set QP method
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists k,p\ge1:\ (x_{k+p},W_{k+p})=(x_k,W_k)\) and no intervening state is terminal.

notation.meaning: primal iterate and working set at iteration k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic active-set methods whose complete state is determined by iterate and working set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((x_k,W_k)\) denote the complete deterministic state of an active-set QP method. Active-set cycling occurs if there exist integers \(k\ge0\) and \(p\ge1\) such that \[(x_{k+p},W_{k+p})=(x_k,W_k),\] no state from iteration \(k\) through \(k+p-1\) satisfies the method's termination test, and the deterministic update rule therefore repeats the same subsequent states. Repetition of a working set alone is not sufficient unless the remaining algorithmic state also repeats.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cycling occurs when a deterministic active-set method returns to the same nonterminal complete state and therefore repeats indefinitely.
knowledge_statements.title: Active-Set Cycling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role is appropriate and the complete-state recurrence criterion is coherent, but its validity depends on the method's state convention and no algorithm-specific source is supplied.

children.title: Working-Set Repetition
children.top_down_role: Repeated working-set patterns without meaningful structural change.

assumptions_latex: \(W_k\) is the working-set sequence of an active-set QP method
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists 0\le j<k:\ W_j=W_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A combinatorial event, weaker than cycling of the complete algorithmic state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an active-set QP method with working sets \(W_0,W_1,\ldots\), working-set repetition has occurred by iteration \(k\) when \[\exists j<k\quad W_j=W_k.\] The event records recurrence of the same constraint index set only. It does not by itself imply cycling, because the primal iterate, multiplier estimate, search direction, tie-breaking state, or regularization parameters may differ between iterations \(j\) and \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Working-set repetition means that the same constraint index set appears at two different iterations; other algorithmic state may still differ.
knowledge_statements.title: Working-Set Repetition

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition correctly distinguishes working-set recurrence from full-state cycling, but it lacks an inspectable active-set-method source.

children.title: Degenerate-Face Stalling
children.top_down_role: Loss of progress near faces with redundant or weakly active constraints.

assumptions_latex: \(F_0\) is a face of the QP feasible polyhedron
\(x_k\in F_0\) on an infinite index set \(K\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lim_{k\to\infty,\ k\in K}\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|=0\) while no \(x_k\) with \(k\in K\) is terminal.

notation.meaning: degenerate feasible face visited infinitely often

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic stalling on a face with dependent active normals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_0\) be a feasible face on which the active-constraint matrix is rank deficient. An active-set sequence exhibits degenerate-face stalling on an infinite index set \(K\) when \[x_k\in F_0\ \text{for all }k\in K,\qquad \lim_{k\to\infty,\ k\in K}\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|=0,\] while no \(x_k\) with \(k\in K\) satisfies the algorithm's termination test. Thus working-set changes or multiplier exchanges occur without departure from the degenerate face or a step bounded away from zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Degenerate-face stalling means nonterminal iterates remain on a rank-degenerate face while their step lengths tend to zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate-Face Stalling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source establishes this proposed stalling definition. Moreover, membership of x_k in the face only for k in K does not justify the broader statement that the method does not depart from the face, since x_{k+1} need not lie in the face.

children.title: Negligible-Progress Regimes
children.top_down_role: Solver states exhibiting changes too small to produce effective progress.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|\le\varepsilon_x\) and \(|f(x_{k+1})-f(x_k)|\le\varepsilon_f\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational per-iteration condition relative to specified step and objective tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a norm and tolerances \(\varepsilon_x>0\) and \(\varepsilon_f>0\). An iteration of a QP method is in a negligible-progress regime when \[\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|\le\varepsilon_x\qquad\text{and}\qquad |f(x_{k+1})-f(x_k)|\le\varepsilon_f,\] yet the termination conditions are not satisfied at \(x_{k+1}\). Persistent negligible progress means these inequalities hold for every iteration in a prescribed consecutive window or along an infinite subsequence, according to the monitoring convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Progress is negligible when both the step and objective change fall below chosen tolerances even though the method has not met its termination conditions.
knowledge_statements.title: Negligible-Progress Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The inequalities define an operational event, but the leaf denotes a failure regime and may require a failure_boundary record with a fixed persistence window or subsequence convention. No source resolves that choice.

children.title: QP Data Pathologies
children.top_down_role: Scaling and finite-precision problems affecting otherwise valid convex QPs.

children.title: QP Scale-Imbalance Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Large disparities among variable, constraint, and objective scales.

children.title: Variable-Scale Imbalance
children.top_down_role: Large scale disparities across decision-variable coordinates.

assumptions_latex: \(s_i>0\) are declared characteristic magnitudes of the variables
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max_i s_i/\min_i s_i\ge\tau_s\).

notation.meaning: characteristic magnitude assigned to variable i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale imbalance relative to declared characteristic variable magnitudes and a chosen threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assign each QP variable \(x_i\) a positive characteristic magnitude \(s_i\), and fix \(\tau_s>1\). Variable-scale imbalance is present when \[\frac{\max_i s_i}{\min_i s_i}\ge\tau_s.\] Under the normalization \(x=Dy\), where \(D=\operatorname{diag}(s_1,\ldots,s_n)\), the QP data transform as \(H_y=D^\top HD\), \(c_y=D^\top c\), and \(A_y=AD\). The condition is representation-dependent and must therefore be stated relative to the selected units or characteristic scales.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Variables are scale-imbalanced when their declared characteristic magnitudes span more than a chosen ratio; diagonal normalization correspondingly transforms all QP data.
knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Scale Imbalance

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation-dependent ratio condition and diagonal transformation are coherent, but neither the characteristic-scale convention nor the threshold is supported by a cited QP scaling source.

children.title: Constraint-Scale Imbalance
children.top_down_role: Large magnitude disparities across affine constraint rows.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Scale Imbalance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerical imbalance among rows of a linearly constrained convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider constraints \(l\le Ax\le u\), with row vectors \(a_i^{\mathsf T}\). For a chosen row scale \(s_i=\max\{\lVert a_i\rVert_2,|l_i|,|u_i|\}\), omitting infinite bounds, define \(s_{\min}=\min_{i:s_i>0}s_i\) and \(s_{\max}=\max_i s_i\). Constraint-scale imbalance at threshold \(\kappa_c>1\) is the condition \[s_{\max}/s_{\min}>\kappa_c.\] The ratio depends on the representation: multiplying any constraint row and its finite bounds by the same positive number preserves its feasible set but changes this diagnostic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraint-scale imbalance occurs when representative magnitudes of nonzero constraint rows and their bounds span more than a prescribed ratio, although equivalent row rescaling can change the diagnostic.
assumptions_latex: At least one row scale \(s_i\) is positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_{\max}/s_{\min}>\kappa_c\) diagnoses constraint-scale imbalance in the chosen representation.

notation.meaning: representative magnitude of constraint row i and its finite bounds

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: row-scale spread is a conventional representation-dependent numerical diagnostic
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the leaf and is internally coherent, but the particular row-scale formula and threshold diagnostic are representation conventions requiring an authoritative numerical-scaling source.

children.title: Objective-Scale Imbalance
children.top_down_role: Mismatch between objective curvature, linear costs, and feasibility scales.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Scale Imbalance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relative scaling of quadratic and linear objective data in a convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x+\gamma\) and a reference variable scale \(d\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\), set \(H=DQD\), \(g=Dc\), and \(D=\operatorname{diag}(d)\). With \(h=\max\{\lVert H\rVert_2,\lVert g\rVert_2,|\gamma|\}\) and \(h_+=\min\{z>0:z\in\{\lVert H\rVert_2,\lVert g\rVert_2,|\gamma|\}\}\), objective-scale imbalance at threshold \(\kappa_o>1\) is \[h/h_+>\kappa_o.\] This is a representation-dependent diagnostic, not a change in convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After fixing variable units, objective-scale imbalance means that the nonzero quadratic, linear, and constant objective magnitudes span more than a chosen factor.
assumptions_latex: At least one of \(H\), \(g\), or \(\gamma\) is nonzero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(h/h_+>\kappa_o\) diagnoses objective-scale imbalance relative to \(d\).

notation.meaning: largest and smallest nonzero objective-component magnitudes

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: scaled coefficient spread is a conventional numerical diagnostic
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the leaf, but the proposed comparison of Hessian, gradient, and constant-term norms is not a canonical objective-scaling definition. A source is needed to establish this exact diagnostic, especially because the arbitrary constant does not affect the optimizer.

children.title: Physical-Unit Mismatch
children.top_down_role: Numerical imbalance arising from incompatible or poorly normalized measurement units.

knowledge_statements.title: Physical-Unit Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimensional-consistency boundary for algebraic QP data and scaling transformations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assign each variable \(x_j\) a physical unit \(U_j\) and the objective a unit \(U_f\). A physically meaningful QP requires \([Q_{jk}]=U_f/(U_jU_k)\), \([c_j]=U_f/U_j\), and, for each constraint row, \([A_{ij}]U_j=U_i\) whenever \(A_{ij}\ne0\), with \([l_i]=[u_i]=U_i\). If any displayed equality fails, algebraic addition combines unlike units. Moreover, a diagonal substitution \(x=D\hat x\) is dimensionally valid only when each \(D_{jj}\hat x_j\) has unit \(U_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: QP terms must combine quantities with matching physical dimensions. Violating the displayed unit identities makes the model dimensionally inconsistent, and arbitrary numerical scaling cannot repair its semantics.
assumptions_latex: Every variable, constraint row, and objective value has an assigned physical unit.
The QP is \(\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\) subject to \(l\le Ax\le u\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Failure of any unit identity is a physical-unit mismatch; dimensionally valid scaling must preserve the assigned units.

notation.meaning: units of variable j, constraint row i, and objective
diagonal variable conversion or scaling matrix

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: dimensional homogeneity requires addends in every equation to share units
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role and dimensional identities are plausible and consistent, but no inspectable source supports the precise unit assignments or the stated scaling restriction.

children.title: Extreme Coefficient Magnitudes
children.top_down_role: Finite-precision difficulties caused by very large or small data values.

knowledge_statements.title: Extreme Coefficient Magnitudes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-precision boundary for representable and reliably manipulable QP coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathbb F\) be a floating-point system with largest finite number \(M\), smallest positive normal number \(m\), and unit roundoff \(u\). QP data are outside the safe coefficient range whenever a required stored or intermediate value has magnitude greater than \(M\), or a required nonzero value has magnitude below \(m\). Even within range, if an update \(a+b\) satisfies \(|b|\le u|a|\), its smaller contribution may be lost to rounding. Thus extreme coefficient magnitudes can cause overflow, underflow, or absorption independently of mathematical feasibility and convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coefficients or intermediates beyond floating-point range overflow or underflow; sufficiently disparate in-range terms can also lose smaller contributions through rounding.
assumptions_latex: QP data and solver intermediates are represented in floating-point arithmetic \(\mathbb F\).
Arithmetic uses rounding with unit roundoff \(u\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stated magnitude conditions permit overflow, underflow, or absorption and therefore delimit numerically reliable QP representation.

notation.meaning: largest finite and smallest positive normal floating-point numbers

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard floating-point overflow, underflow, and absorption model
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits, but the exact absorption threshold depends on the floating-point model and rounding convention, while values below the smallest normal number may remain representable as subnormals. An authoritative numerical-analysis locator is required.

children.title: Convexity-Detection Tolerance
children.top_down_role: Classification ambiguity near the positive-semidefinite boundary.

knowledge_statements.title: Convexity-Detection Tolerance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tolerance-based classification of a symmetric QP Hessian near the PSD boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a computed symmetric Hessian \(\widehat Q\) and tolerance \(\tau\ge0\), define the numerical classifications \(\tau\)-convex if \(\lambda_{\min}(\widehat Q)\ge-\tau\), definitely nonconvex if \(\lambda_{\min}(\widehat Q)<-\tau\), and borderline if \(|\lambda_{\min}(\widehat Q)|\le\tau\). If the exact Hessian is \(Q=\widehat Q+E\), Weyl's bound gives \(|\lambda_{\min}(Q)-\lambda_{\min}(\widehat Q)|\le\lVert E\rVert_2\). Hence exact convexity is uncertified whenever the computed minimum eigenvalue lies within the error radius of zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tolerance classifies small negative computed eigenvalues as numerically convex, but exact convexity remains ambiguous when eigenvalue error can cross zero.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) and \(\widehat Q\) are real symmetric matrices.
\(Q=\widehat Q+E\) and an upper bound on \(\lVert E\rVert_2\) is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact positive semidefiniteness is ambiguous if \(|\lambda_{\min}(\widehat Q)|\le\lVert E\rVert_2\); the \(\tau\)-classification is only numerical.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Weyl eigenvalue perturbation bound determines ambiguity near zero
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Weyl-based ambiguity claim is plausible, but the labels overlap: values in the stated borderline interval can also be tau-convex. A matrix-perturbation source and clarification of whether these are overlapping labels or exclusive classifications are required before fixing the mathematical version.

children.title: Bound-Constraint Consistency Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Modeling inconsistencies exposed by presolve and feasibility checks.

children.title: Contradictory Variable Bounds
children.top_down_role: Lower and upper bound data that cannot describe a common variable value.

knowledge_statements.title: Contradictory Variable Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct infeasibility certificate from one inconsistent variable interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider componentwise bounds \(\ell\le x\le u\), where infinite endpoints are allowed. If there exists an index \(j\) such that \(\ell_j>u_j\), then no \(x_j\in\mathbb R\) can satisfy both \(x_j\ge\ell_j\) and \(x_j\le u_j\). The index \(j\), together with the two finite values \((\ell_j,u_j)\), is therefore a directly verifiable certificate that the bound set, and hence any QP containing these bounds, is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variable whose lower bound exceeds its upper bound provides an immediate, locally checkable certificate that the QP is infeasible.
assumptions_latex: The QP imposes componentwise bounds \(\ell\le x\le u\).
For some \(j\), both \(\ell_j\) and \(u_j\) are finite and \(\ell_j>u_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pair \((j,\ell_j,u_j)\) certifies that the QP feasible set is empty.

notation.meaning: componentwise lower and upper variable bounds
index of the contradictory bound pair

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: incompatible interval endpoints imply an empty interval
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind fits the exact leaf, and the interval contradiction is mathematically correct, but the record supplies no inspectable source locator.

children.title: Bound–Constraint Conflicts
children.top_down_role: Incompatibility between variable bounds and affine constraint data.

assumptions_latex: Every bound needed to evaluate \(L(a)\) is finite.
The QP contains the row \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L(a)>b\) certifies that the bound box and the linear constraint have empty intersection.

notation.meaning: minimum of the row activity over the variable-bound box

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: separable linear minimization over a box gives the row-activity bound
latex_repaired: removed unmatched right delimiter command
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interval-arithmetic infeasibility certificate linking variable bounds to one linear constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\ell\le x\le u\) and consider one row \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\), with finite bounds for every \(j\) such that \(a_j\ne0\). Its minimum over the box is \[L(a)=\sum_{a_j\ge0}a_j\ell_j+\sum_{a_j<0}a_ju_j.\] If \(L(a)>b\), every box-feasible point violates the row. Thus the row index, its coefficients and right-hand side, and the participating variable bounds form a verifiable infeasibility certificate. The analogous test for \(a^{\mathsf T}x\ge b\) uses the box maximum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the smallest possible value of a linear row over the variable-bound box already exceeds its upper limit, that row and the bounds certify infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Bound–Constraint Conflicts

children.title: Mutually Inconsistent Constraints
children.top_down_role: Affine constraint groups lacking a common feasible point.

knowledge_statements.title: Mutually Inconsistent Constraints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Farkas certificate for infeasibility of a finite system of linear inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the inequality system \(Ax\le b\), mutual inconsistency is certified by a vector \(y\in\mathbb R_+^m\) satisfying \[A^{\mathsf T}y=0,\qquad b^{\mathsf T}y<0.\] Indeed, the certificate is checked solely by matrix-vector multiplication, sign tests, and a scalar product. By Farkas' alternative, exactly one of the following systems is feasible: \(Ax\le b\), or the displayed certificate system. Consequently, existence of such \(y\) is equivalent to emptiness of the intersection of all constraint halfspaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative combination of constraint normals that cancels while producing a negative combined right-hand side certifies that the constraints are mutually inconsistent.
assumptions_latex: Constraints are represented exactly as \(Ax\le b\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ax\le b\) is infeasible if and only if there exists \(y\ge0\) with \(A^{\mathsf T}y=0\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}y<0\).
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate statement has the correct sign convention for the system Ax <= b and fits the leaf, but the nontrivial equivalence invokes Farkas' alternative without an inspectable theorem or section locator.

children.title: Presolve Inconsistency Signals
children.top_down_role: Structural inconsistency indicators exposed during model preprocessing.

knowledge_statements.title: Presolve Inconsistency Signals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound presolve deductions that certify infeasibility before QP iterations begin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A presolve inconsistency signal is certifying when it derives either an empty bound \(\ell'_j>u'_j\), an impossible row interval \(L_i>u_i\) or \(U_i<l_i\), or a nonnegative Farkas multiplier \(y\) with \(A^{\mathsf T}y=0\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}y<0\). Here \([L_i,U_i]\) is a rigorously valid enclosure of \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\) over the current variable box. Such a signal certifies infeasibility only when every bound propagation, enclosure, and comparison is valid for the original constraints; a tolerance-triggered warning alone is not a certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Presolve certifies infeasibility through an empty propagated bound, an impossible row interval, or a Farkas vector, provided all deductions remain valid for the original model.
assumptions_latex: The QP has linear constraints and componentwise variable bounds.
Presolve transformations preserve feasibility and retain a reconstruction record.
Row-activity enclosures are outward-valid under the arithmetic used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any listed exact or rigorously enclosed inconsistency is a verifiable infeasibility certificate; a heuristic tolerance flag is not.

notation.meaning: valid enclosure of row i activity over the current box

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: sound bound propagation and Farkas multipliers yield checkable infeasibility deductions
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: QP Numerical Stabilization System

children.title: Primal Curvature Regularization
children.top_down_role: Curvature modification for stability or uniqueness.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Curvature Regularization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive diagonal curvature added to a convex QP Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a convex QP objective \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\), primal curvature regularization with parameter \(\rho>0\) replaces \(Q\) by \(Q_\rho=Q+\rho I\), equivalently replacing the objective by \[f_\rho(x)=f(x)+\tfrac\rho2\lVert x\rVert_2^2.\] Since \(Q\succeq0\), one has \(Q_\rho\succeq\rho I\), so the regularized objective is \(\rho\)-strongly convex and has at most one minimizer on every convex feasible set. Unless the added term is centered or removed through a limiting procedure, the minimizer may differ from that of the original QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding a positive multiple of the identity to the Hessian makes the objective strongly convex and its minimizer unique, but generally biases the solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q_\rho\succeq\rho I\), hence \(f_\rho\) is strongly convex and has at most one feasible minimizer.

children.title: Dual-Constraint Block Regularization

children.title: Dual-Block Regularization
children.top_down_role: Stabilizing modifications applied to multiplier-related system blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Block Regularization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quasi-definite regularization of the multiplier block in a saddle-point system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the equality-constrained QP KKT system \[\begin{pmatrix}Q&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}x\\y\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}-c\\b\end{pmatrix},\] dual-block regularization with \(\delta>0\) replaces the zero multiplier block by \(-\delta I\). The second block equation becomes \(Ax-\delta y=b\). If additionally \(Q\succ0\), then the regularized saddle-point matrix is nonsingular: its Schur complement in the dual variables is \(-\delta I-AQ^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}\prec0\). The computed pair solves a perturbed primal-dual system rather than the unregularized KKT equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replacing the zero multiplier block by a negative diagonal term can make the KKT matrix nonsingular, while perturbing primal feasibility by an amount tied to the multiplier.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regularized KKT matrix is nonsingular and imposes \(Ax-b=\delta y\).

children.title: Constraint-Block Regularization
children.top_down_role: Stabilizing modifications associated with affine-constraint blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Block Regularization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive regularization of the primal block induced by constraint geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an equality-constrained QP with Hessian \(Q\) and constraint matrix \(A\), constraint-block regularization with \(\sigma>0\) replaces the primal curvature by \[Q_\sigma=Q+\sigma A^{\mathsf T}A.\] Equivalently, it adds \(\tfrac\sigma2\lVert Ax-b\rVert_2^2\) to the objective, up to the accompanying linear and constant terms. For every \(v\in\mathbb R^n\), \(v^{\mathsf T}Q_\sigma v=v^{\mathsf T}Qv+\sigma\lVert Av\rVert_2^2\). Thus directions detected by \(A\) gain curvature, while directions in \(\ker Q\cap\ker A\) remain unregularized.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding a weighted constraint Gram matrix supplies curvature in directions visible to the constraints, but cannot stabilize directions lying in both Hessian and constraint nullspaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q_\sigma\succeq0\), and \(Q_\sigma\succ0\) exactly when \(\ker Q\cap\ker A=\{0\}\).

children.title: Multiplier Stabilization
children.top_down_role: Effects of regularization on multiplier behavior and dual-system conditioning.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier Stabilization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proximal dual-block stabilization for an equality-constrained convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the QP \(\min_x \tfrac12 x^TQx+q^Tx\) subject to \(Ax=b\), choose \(\delta>0\) and compute \((x_\delta,y_\delta)\) from
\[
\begin{pmatrix}Q&A^T\\A&-\delta I\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}x_\delta\\y_\delta\end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{pmatrix}-q\\b\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The negative dual diagonal removes null directions confined to the multiplier block. The output satisfies \(Qx_\delta+q+A^Ty_\delta=0\) and \(Ax_\delta-b=\delta y_\delta\); hence it solves a stabilized, generally perturbed KKT system rather than the original constraints exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add a negative proximal term to the multiplier block, solve the regularized KKT system, and report its explicitly biased primal residual.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(q\in\mathbb R^n\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\).
The displayed stabilized matrix is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Qx_\delta+q+A^Ty_\delta=0\) and \(Ax_\delta-b=\delta y_\delta\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct block regularization of the equality-constrained QP KKT equations
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the Multiplier Stabilization leaf and its displayed residual identities are internally consistent, but no inspectable source is cited for the stabilized KKT formulation or the stated null-direction effect.

children.title: Regularization Bias Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Balance between numerical stabilization and perturbation of the original QP.

knowledge_statements.title: Regularization Bias Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact residual bias induced by equality-multiplier block regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
In the stabilized KKT equations with dual block \(-\delta I\), the constraint equation is \(Ax_\delta-b=\delta y_\delta\). Consequently,
\[
\|Ax_\delta-b\|=\delta\|y_\delta\|
\]
for any common vector norm. Thus a larger \(\delta\) strengthens the dual-block diagonal but permits larger constraint bias for a multiplier of fixed magnitude. If \(y_\delta\) remains bounded as \(\delta\downarrow0\), then the feasibility residual converges to zero; this conclusion need not hold when the regularized multipliers diverge.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual regularization improves the block diagonal while creating an exact feasibility bias equal to the parameter times the stabilized multiplier.
assumptions_latex: \((x_\delta,y_\delta)\) satisfies the stabilized KKT system with dual block \(-\delta I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|Ax_\delta-b\|=\delta\|y_\delta\|\), and bounded \(y_\delta\) implies feasibility as \(\delta\downarrow0\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact consequence of the stabilized constraint equation
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: QP Equilibration Calculus
children.top_down_role: Data transformations improving numerical balance.

children.title: Row Equilibration
children.top_down_role: Balancing affine constraint rows with disparate coefficient magnitudes.

knowledge_statements.title: Row Equilibration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive diagonal scaling of QP constraint rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given constraints \(l\le Ax\le u\), let \(D_r=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_m)\) with \(d_i>0\). Row equilibration replaces them by
\[
D_rl\le (D_rA)x\le D_ru.
\]
The scaled and original feasible sets are identical because multiplication by each positive \(d_i\) preserves inequality direction and equality. A typical equilibration choice makes a selected row norm of \(D_rA\) near one. For equality constraints, if \(\widetilde y\) is the multiplier of \(D_r(Ax-b)=0\), the original multiplier is \(y=D_r\widetilde y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scale every constraint row and its bounds by the same positive factor; feasibility is unchanged and equality multipliers transform diagonally.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and bounds are interpreted componentwise.
Every diagonal entry of \(D_r\) is finite and strictly positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x:l\le Ax\le u\}=\{x:D_rl\le D_rAx\le D_ru\}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: positive diagonal scaling gives an algebraically equivalent componentwise constraint system
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation matches Row Equilibration, including consistent bound scaling and the equality-multiplier transformation, but it has no inspectable citation.

children.title: Column Equilibration
children.top_down_role: Balancing variable columns across quadratic and affine model data.

knowledge_statements.title: Column Equilibration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invertible diagonal change of primal variables for a convex QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x=D_cz\), where \(D_c=\operatorname{diag}(s_1,\ldots,s_n)\) and \(s_j>0\), the QP
\[
\min_x\ \tfrac12x^TQx+q^Tx\quad\text{subject to}\quad l\le Ax\le u
\]
is represented in \(z\) by \(\widetilde Q=D_cQD_c\), \(\widetilde q=D_cq\), and \(\widetilde A=AD_c\). The transformation is bijective, preserves objective values and feasibility under \(x=D_cz\), and preserves convexity because \(Q\succeq0\) implies \(D_cQD_c\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rescale primal coordinates by an invertible positive diagonal matrix and transform the Hessian, linear term, and constraint columns consistently.
assumptions_latex: Every diagonal entry of \(D_c\) is finite and strictly positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x=D_cz\), \(\widetilde Q=D_cQD_c\), \(\widetilde q=D_cq\), and \(\widetilde A=AD_c\) define an equivalent convex QP.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: invertible diagonal substitution in a quadratic objective and linear constraints
