intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The diagonal variable substitution and transformed QP data correctly fit Column Equilibration, but no source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Objective Prescaling
children.top_down_role: Magnitude adjustment for quadratic and linear objective data.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective Prescaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive scalar normalization of the complete QP objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^TQx+q^Tx+c\) and choose \(\alpha>0\). Objective prescaling replaces \((Q,q,c)\) by \((\alpha Q,\alpha q,\alpha c)\), so the new objective is \(\widetilde f(x)=\alpha f(x)\). For any unchanged feasible set \(C\),
\[
\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}\widetilde f(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x).
\]
If KKT multipliers \(y\) accompany unscaled constraint functions, their consistently scaled counterparts are \(\widetilde y=\alpha y\). Objective prescaling changes numerical magnitudes but not primal minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiply every objective coefficient by one positive scalar; primal minimizers stay unchanged, while consistently normalized multipliers scale by that scalar.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is the unchanged feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}\alpha f(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: multiplication of an objective by a positive scalar preserves its ordering
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation correctly describes positive scalar objective prescaling and its effect on primal minimizers and consistently normalized multipliers, but it lacks an inspectable source.

children.title: Constraint Prescaling
children.top_down_role: Magnitude adjustment for constraint coefficients and associated bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Prescaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent positive diagonal normalization of constraint functions and bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the componentwise constraint system \(l\le Ax\le u\), choose finite factors \(d_i>0\) and set \(D=\operatorname{diag}(d_i)\). Constraint prescaling produces \(\widetilde A=DA\), \(\widetilde l=Dl\), and \(\widetilde u=Du\), with infinite bound endpoints left infinite with the same sign. Then
\[
l\le Ax\le u\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \widetilde l\le\widetilde Ax\le\widetilde u.
\]
Any implementation must apply the same factor to a row and both associated finite endpoints; otherwise it changes the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiply each constraint row and both finite endpoints by the same positive factor, preserving the represented feasible set exactly.
assumptions_latex: Bounds are componentwise elements of \(\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty,+\infty\}\).
Every \(d_i\) is finite and strictly positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(l\le Ax\le u\) if and only if \(Dl\le DAx\le Du\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: componentwise multiplication by positive scalars preserves inequalities
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits Constraint Prescaling and correctly requires consistent positive scaling of each row and its endpoints, including preservation of extended-real endpoint signs. No source is cited.

children.title: Scaling Safeguards
children.top_down_role: Limits, clipping policies, and reversibility concerns for numerical scaling.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaling Safeguards
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clipped diagonal equilibration with protection for zero and nonfinite norms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given nonnegative row or column measures \(n_i\), a target \(\tau>0\), a floor \(\eta>0\), and limits \(0<d_{\min}\le d_{\max}<\infty\), define
\[
d_i=\min\!\left\{d_{\max},\max\!\left\{d_{\min},\frac{\tau}{\max\{n_i,\eta\}}\right\}\right\}.
\]
If \(n_i\) is nonfinite, set \(d_i=1\) and flag the datum. Apply only the finite positive diagonal \(D=\operatorname{diag}(d_i)\), transform all coupled coefficients and bounds consistently, and retain \(D\) for recovery of primal or dual variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Floor small norms, clip scaling factors, reject nonfinite measures, transform coupled data consistently, and retain the scaling for solution recovery.
assumptions_latex: \(\tau,\eta,d_{\min},d_{\max}\) satisfy the displayed positivity and ordering conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_i\in[d_{\min},d_{\max}]\) and every applied scaling factor is finite and positive.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: clipping and norm flooring are standard finite-scaling safeguards
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and clipped-scaling algorithm fit Scaling Safeguards, but the chosen flooring, clipping, nonfinite-data response, and recovery requirements need a numerical optimization or solver implementation source.

children.title: Iterative Refinement
children.top_down_role: Linear-system correction for improved numerical accuracy.

knowledge_statements.title: Iterative Refinement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-correction refinement of a computed QP KKT-system solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonsingular linear system \(Kz=h\), start from a computed solution \(z_0\). At iteration \(k\), evaluate the residual \(r_k=h-Kz_k\), preferably in precision higher than that used for the stored factorization; solve \(K\Delta z_k=r_k\) using that factorization; and set \(z_{k+1}=z_k+\Delta z_k\). Stop when a prescribed backward-error test holds, the correction stagnates, or an iteration limit is reached. Return the last iterate together with its residual and stopping status. For a QP, \(K\) may be the current KKT matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly compute a linear-system residual, solve for its correction with the existing factorization, update the solution, and test backward error.
assumptions_latex: Correction solves and residual evaluations are sufficiently accurate to produce meaningful updates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_{k+1}=z_k+K^{-1}(h-Kz_k)\) in exact arithmetic for an exact correction solve.

notation.meaning: linear-system residual at refinement step k

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The residual-correction procedure is a correctly scoped iterative-refinement algorithm for a QP KKT system, but no authoritative source with a specific locator is provided.

children.title: Active-Face Polishing
children.top_down_role: Post-solve refinement using a candidate optimal face.

knowledge_statements.title: Active-Face Polishing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained post-solve refinement on an inferred active polyhedral face.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a convex QP with inequalities \(Ax\le b\), infer a candidate active set \(I\) from an approximate primal-dual solution. Compute a polished pair by solving
\[
\begin{pmatrix}Q&A_I^T\\A_I&0\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}x^+\\y_I^+\end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{pmatrix}-q\\b_I\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Set inactive multipliers to zero. Accept \(x^+\) only if its inactive slacks satisfy \(A_jx^+\le b_j\) within tolerance, its active multipliers have the sign required by the chosen Lagrangian convention, and its KKT residual improves; otherwise reject the polished candidate or revise \(I\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Infer an active face, solve its equality-constrained KKT system, and accept the polished point only after feasibility, sign, and residual checks.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\) and the candidate-face KKT matrix is nonsingular.
The inequality convention is \(Ax\le b\) with nonnegative multipliers in the Lagrangian \(f(x)+y^T(Ax-b)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An accepted \((x^+,y^+)\) satisfies the candidate-face equations and the stated numerical validation tests.

notation.meaning: constraint submatrix indexed by the candidate face

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits Active-Face Polishing and its sign convention is internally consistent. The cited face-geometry section does not support the complete active-set inference, KKT solve, acceptance tests, or revision procedure, so a solver-algorithm source is required.

children.title: Sparse Matrix-Data Interfaces

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse Matrix-Data Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical sparse-array representation of QP Hessian and constraint matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sparse QP interface represents \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\) and \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) by a declared sparse format such as compressed sparse column storage. For a matrix \(M\), arrays \(p\), \(i\), and \(v\) encode column \(j\) in positions \(p_j,\ldots,p_{j+1}-1\), with row indices \(i_k\) and values \(v_k\). The interface must declare dimensions, index base, duplicate-entry policy, and whether \(Q\) stores both triangles or one designated triangle. After duplicate aggregation, the decoded matrices must equal the intended \(Q\) and \(A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Encode QP matrices in a declared sparse format with explicit dimensions, indexing, duplicate handling, and a fixed Hessian-triangle convention.
assumptions_latex: Sparse index and pointer arrays satisfy the selected format's validity conditions.
The Hessian symmetry-storage convention is declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{decode}(p_Q,i_Q,v_Q)=Q\) and \(\operatorname{decode}(p_A,i_A,v_A)=A\) after the declared duplicate aggregation.

notation.meaning: sparse pointer, row-index, and value arrays

children.title: QP Bound-Encoding Conventions
children.top_down_role: Encoding absent, one-sided, finite, and equality bounds.

children.title: Finite Bound Encoding
children.top_down_role: Solver-facing representation of finite lower and upper limits.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Bound Encoding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-sided finite interval encoding for a scalar affine constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For row \(a_i^Tx\), finite bound encoding assigns real numbers \(l_i,u_i\in\mathbb R\) satisfying \(l_i\le u_i\) and interprets the row as
\[
l_i\le a_i^Tx\le u_i.
\]
Both endpoints are present and neither is an infinity sentinel. The encoding is infeasible for every \(x\) if the interface instead receives finite endpoints with \(l_i>u_i\); a canonicalizer should detect that inconsistency before invoking the QP solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-bound row stores two real endpoints and represents membership of its affine value in their closed interval.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) satisfies row \(i\) exactly when \(a_i^Tx\in[l_i,u_i]\).

notation.meaning: finite closed interval for the row value

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: interval encoding is the canonical componentwise representation of two-sided affine bounds
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition precisely fits Finite Bound Encoding and correctly identifies reversed finite endpoints as inconsistent, but it has no inspectable citation.

children.title: One-Sided Bound Encoding
children.top_down_role: Representation choices for lower-only or upper-only restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: One-Sided Bound Encoding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extended-real encoding of a single lower or upper affine bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A one-sided bound on \(a_i^Tx\) is encoded with exactly one finite endpoint. A lower bound uses
\[
l_i\le a_i^Tx,
\]
represented by \((l_i,u_i)=(l_i,+\infty)\); an upper bound uses
\[
a_i^Tx\le u_i,
\]
represented by \((l_i,u_i)=(-\infty,u_i)\). The infinite endpoint denotes absence of that side and is not a finite coefficient to be used in arithmetic. The interface must use its documented infinity representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Represent a lower-only or upper-only affine bound by one finite endpoint and one documented absent-bound marker.
assumptions_latex: The present endpoint is real and the absent endpoint uses the interface's documented infinity convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((l_i,+\infty)\) encodes \(l_i\le a_i^Tx\), while \(( -\infty,u_i)\) encodes \(a_i^Tx\le u_i\).

children.title: Equality Bound Encoding
children.top_down_role: Representation of coincident lower and upper limits.

knowledge_statements.title: Equality Bound Encoding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality rows in a two-sided bound interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a canonical constraint row \(i\) represented by \(\ell_i\le a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le u_i\), an equality is encoded by finite coincident bounds: \(\ell_i=u_i=b_i\in\mathbb R\). Its feasible set is therefore \(\{x:a_i^{\mathsf T}x=b_i\}\). Equality classification requires exact equality in the interface's stored scalar representation unless the interface explicitly declares a separate comparison tolerance; numerical feasibility tolerances used by a solver do not alter the encoded mathematical constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A two-sided row encodes an equality when its finite lower and upper bounds coincide; solver feasibility tolerances do not change that mathematical encoding.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ell_i=u_i=b_i\Longleftrightarrow (\ell_i\le a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le u_i)=(a_i^{\mathsf T}x=b_i)\).

notation.meaning: Stored lower and upper row bounds.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The equality encoding is mathematically sound and the definition fits the leaf, but the exact stored-scalar comparison and tolerance-policy claims require a specific solver-interface source.

children.title: Absent-Bound Sentinels
children.top_down_role: Accepted markers for omitted lower or upper restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: Absent-Bound Sentinels
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extended-real sentinels for omitted constraint sides.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In an extended-real bound interface, the sentinel \(\ell_i=-\infty\) means that row \(i\) has no lower restriction, and \(u_i=+\infty\) means that it has no upper restriction. Thus \(-\infty\le a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le u_i\) denotes only \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le u_i\), while \(\ell_i\le a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le+\infty\) denotes only \(\ell_i\le a_i^{\mathsf T}x\). If both sentinels occur, the row imposes no restriction and may be removed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negative and positive infinity respectively omit the lower and upper sides of a row; two absent sides make the row vacuous.
assumptions_latex: Finite bounds belong to \(\mathbb R\), while absent sides belong to \(\{-\infty,+\infty\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ell_i=-\infty\) removes the lower side, \(u_i=+\infty\) removes the upper side, and \((\ell_i,u_i)=(-\infty,+\infty)\) yields \(\mathbb R^n\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The extended-real interpretation is correct and fits a definition, but no inspectable source supports the asserted interface convention or removal policy.

children.title: Infinity Threshold Handling
children.top_down_role: Interpretation of large finite values used as practical infinity markers.

knowledge_statements.title: Infinity Threshold Handling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Threshold conversion of large finite bound sentinels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a declared threshold \(\tau>0\), process each submitted row bound before solver dispatch. Replace a lower bound \(\ell_i\le-\tau\) by \(-\infty\), replace an upper bound \(u_i\ge\tau\) by \(+\infty\), and retain bounds strictly inside \((-\tau,\tau)\). Reject nonnumeric values and any retained pair satisfying \(\ell_i>u_i\). After all rows are processed, output the resulting extended-real bound vectors. The value of \(\tau\) and the inclusive comparisons are part of the interface contract and must not depend silently on solver feasibility tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A declared threshold maps sufficiently extreme bounds to absent sides, validates the resulting intervals, and remains distinct from feasibility tolerances.
assumptions_latex: Submitted bounds are numeric scalars or explicitly supported infinity values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ell_i\le-\tau\Rightarrow\ell_i'=-\infty\), \(u_i\ge\tau\Rightarrow u_i'=+\infty\), and every retained row satisfies \(\ell_i'\le u_i'\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the appropriate kind, but threshold values, inclusive comparisons, supported inputs, and rejection behavior are interface-specific and have no cited source.

children.title: Automatic QP Convexity Checks
children.top_down_role: Validation of quadratic curvature before solver dispatch.

knowledge_statements.title: Automatic QP Convexity Checks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact curvature validation for continuous minimization QPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given the quadratic objective \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\), form \(Q_s=(Q+Q^{\mathsf T})/2\). Apply a symmetric positive-semidefiniteness test to \(Q_s\), such as an exact \(LDL^{\mathsf T}\) factorization with nonnegative pivot blocks. Dispatch the model as a convex QP exactly when the test certifies \(Q_s\succeq0\); otherwise return a negative-curvature direction \(d\) with \(d^{\mathsf T}Q_sd<0\), when available, and reject convex-QP dispatch. A floating-point implementation must report its acceptance tolerance separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Symmetrize the quadratic matrix and dispatch as convex only after certifying positive semidefiniteness; otherwise report or detect negative curvature.
assumptions_latex: The problem minimizes the displayed quadratic objective over a convex feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) is convex on \(\mathbb R^n\) if and only if \(Q_s\succeq0\).

notation.meaning: Symmetric part of the quadratic matrix.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited convex-functions section plausibly supports convexity iff the symmetric Hessian is positive semidefinite, but it does not establish the stated LDL test, dispatch procedure, or negative-curvature output contract.

children.title: QP Presolve Simplification System
children.top_down_role: Structural simplification of bounds, fixed variables, and redundant affine constraints.

children.title: Fixed-Variable Elimination
children.top_down_role: Structural removal of variables fixed by coincident bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Variable Elimination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact substitution of variables fixed by coincident bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\) with symmetric \(Q\), and partition \(x=(x_R,x_F)\) where \(x_F=d\) is fixed. Substitution produces the reduced objective \(\tfrac12x_R^{\mathsf T}Q_{RR}x_R+(c_R+Q_{RF}d)^{\mathsf T}x_R+\kappa\), where \(\kappa=\tfrac12d^{\mathsf T}Q_{FF}d+c_F^{\mathsf T}d\). Every row \(\ell\le A_Rx_R+A_Fd\le u\) becomes \(\ell-A_Fd\le A_Rx_R\le u-A_Fd\). Reconstructing \(x_F=d\) gives a feasibility- and objective-preserving correspondence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Substitute fixed variables, shift linear objective and row bounds, solve the reduced QP, then restore the fixed values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The original and reduced feasible points correspond bijectively under \(x=(x_R,d)\), and their objectives differ only by \(\kappa\).

notation.meaning: Remaining and fixed variable index sets.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The substitution formulas are correct, but this presolve operation is an algorithm rather than merely a representation. A presolve source is also required before a replacement can be reviewed.

children.title: Bound Tightening
children.top_down_role: Propagation of stronger variable limits from model structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound Tightening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Row-wise interval propagation over variable bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each row \(\ell_i\le\sum_k a_{ik}x_k\le u_i\) and variable \(j\) with \(a_{ij}\ne0\), compute the exact interval \([L_{ij},U_{ij}]\) of \(\sum_{k\ne j}a_{ik}x_k\) over the current box. If \(a_{ij}>0\), intersect the bound of \(x_j\) with \([(\ell_i-U_{ij})/a_{ij},(u_i-L_{ij})/a_{ij}]\); if \(a_{ij}<0\), intersect it with \([(u_i-L_{ij})/a_{ij},(\ell_i-U_{ij})/a_{ij}]\). Repeat until no bound changes, and declare infeasibility if any interval becomes empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Interval propagation derives implied variable bounds from each linear row, iterating to stability and detecting empty bound intervals.
assumptions_latex: Each variable has an extended-real interval bound.
Interval endpoints are computed with validity-preserving arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted update preserves all feasible points and weakly shrinks the current variable box.

notation.meaning: Residual activity interval excluding variable j.
Coefficient of variable j in row i.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The row-wise update formulas are correct, but exact interval propagation need not reach an unchanged state after finitely many iterations without additional assumptions or a stopping rule. A source is needed to fix the intended algorithm.

children.title: Redundant Constraint Detection
children.top_down_role: Identification of affine restrictions that do not alter the feasible region.

knowledge_statements.title: Redundant Constraint Detection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Box-implied redundancy certificate for a linear row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the current variable domain be the box \(B=\{x:p_j\le x_j\le q_j\}\), and let \([L_i,U_i]\) be the exact range of \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\) over \(B\). If \(\ell_i\le L_i\) and \(U_i\le u_i\), then the row \(\ell_i\le a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le u_i\) is redundant relative to \(B\) and may be deleted. The endpoint calculations constitute a checkable certificate because each is obtained by selecting the appropriate variable endpoint according to the sign of each coefficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A row is redundant over the current box when its entire attainable activity interval lies inside the row bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(B\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is the current box relaxation.
The activity extrema are finite or handled in extended-real arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \([L_i,U_i]\subseteq[\ell_i,u_i]\Rightarrow B\subseteq\{x:\ell_i\le a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le u_i\}\).

notation.meaning: Exact row-activity range over the box.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The box-containment certificate is mathematically correct and certificate is an appropriate kind, but no inspectable presolve source is supplied.

children.title: Duplicate Constraint Consolidation
children.top_down_role: Treatment of repeated or proportional affine restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: Duplicate Constraint Consolidation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consolidation of proportional two-sided linear rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose two rows satisfy \(a_j=\alpha a_i\) for some \(\alpha\ne0\). Writing \(t=a_i^{\mathsf T}x\), row \(j\) is equivalent to \(\underline b_j\le t\le\overline b_j\), where \(\underline b_j=\min\{\ell_j/\alpha,u_j/\alpha\}\) and \(\overline b_j=\max\{\ell_j/\alpha,u_j/\alpha\}\). The two rows may be replaced by the single interval \(\max\{\ell_i,\underline b_j\}\le a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le\min\{u_i,\overline b_j\}\). If its lower endpoint exceeds its upper endpoint, the model is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proportional rows are converted to one common activity scale and replaced by the intersection of their bound intervals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The consolidated row has exactly the feasible set of the conjunction of the two original rows.

notation.meaning: Activity on the retained row scale.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proportional-row intersection formula is correct, but the leaf describes a consolidation algorithm rather than a representation, and the domains and ordering of the row bounds are not stated. No presolve source is supplied.

children.title: Empty Constraint Processing
children.top_down_role: Handling of zero-coefficient rows under their associated bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Empty Constraint Processing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Presolve classification of zero-coefficient rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an empty row \(a_i=0\), the activity is \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x=0\) for every \(x\). If \(\ell_i\le0\le u_i\), the row is redundant and can be deleted. If \(0<\ell_i\) or \(u_i<0\), the row is inconsistent and certifies primal infeasibility independently of all other constraints. The same test applies after substitutions or coefficient elimination create a zero row.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero row is removable when zero satisfies its bounds and is an immediate infeasibility certificate otherwise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\in[\ell_i,u_i]\) implies redundancy; \(0\notin[\ell_i,u_i]\) implies infeasibility.

notation.meaning: Coefficient vector of the processed row.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The zero-row redundancy and infeasibility classification is correct, and certificate fits the terminal container, but it lacks an inspectable presolve citation.

children.title: QP-to-Conic Canonicalization
children.top_down_role: Automatic conversion of convex quadratic models into cone-based forms.

knowledge_statements.title: QP-to-Conic Canonicalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rotated-second-order-cone epigraph of a convex quadratic objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the convex QP \(\min_x\ \tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\) subject to \(Ax=b\) and \(Gx\le h\), where \(Q\succeq0\). Choose \(B\) satisfying \(Q=B^{\mathsf T}B\), and define \(\mathcal Q_r=\{(s,v,w):s\ge0,\ v\ge0,\ 2sv\ge\lVert w\rVert_2^2\}\). An equivalent conic problem is \(\min_{x,t}\ c^{\mathsf T}x+t\) subject to \(Ax=b\), \(Gx\le h\), and \((t,1,Bx)\in\mathcal Q_r\). At every optimum, \(t=\tfrac12\lVert Bx\rVert_2^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Factor the positive-semidefinite quadratic and represent its epigraph with a rotated second-order cone, preserving feasible optimizers and objective values.
assumptions_latex: The original QP has a finite attained optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The QP and its rotated-cone formulation have the same optimal \(x\) and the same optimal value.

notation.meaning: Factor satisfying Q equal to transpose(B) times B.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The rotated-cone formulation has the correct factor of one half under the declared cone convention, and representation fits the leaf, but no conic-canonicalization source is supplied.

children.title: Repeated-QP Deployment Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Deployment structures for fixed sparsity, changing data, and constrained computing environments.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Warm starts, matrix updates, code generation, and linear-system solvers

children.title: Warm-Start Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Transfer of primal, dual, and active-set information between related solves.

knowledge_statements.title: Warm-Start Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Initialization contract for a sequence of related QPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A warm-start interface for a QP accepts, in the current model's coordinates, any supported subset of a primal estimate \(x^0\), constraint-multiplier estimate \(y^0\), bound multipliers, and active-set labels. Each supplied vector must match current dimensions and the solver's sign and scaling conventions. The solver may project, repair, or ignore an inadmissible estimate, but must distinguish warm-start rejection from model infeasibility. Termination and correctness tests remain those of the target QP; a warm start changes initialization, not the mathematical problem or required solution certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A warm start transfers compatible primal, dual, or active-set estimates while leaving the target QP and its correctness criteria unchanged.
assumptions_latex: The new QP uses a declared mapping from prior to current variables and constraints.
All accepted estimates are finite where the solver requires finite initialization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Accepted warm-start data determine only the solver's initial state; the returned solution must satisfy the current QP's termination criteria.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition matches the warm-start leaf, but supported data, repair or rejection behavior, scaling, and sign conventions are solver-specific and unsupported by a cited interface source.

children.title: Two-Stage Factorization Reuse
children.top_down_role: Caching of sparse linear algebra across fixed-pattern QP sequences.

children.title: Symbolic Factorization Caching
children.top_down_role: Reuse of sparsity analysis and elimination structure across QP instances.

knowledge_statements.title: Symbolic Factorization Caching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reuse of sparse elimination structure across fixed-pattern systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a sequence of sparse matrices \(K_k\) with identical dimensions and structural nonzero pattern, choose a fixed permutation \(P\) and perform symbolic factorization once to determine the elimination tree and storage pattern for factors of \(PK_kP^{\mathsf T}\). Cache that symbolic data. For each new \(K_k\), insert its numerical values and perform only numerical factorization in the cached structure. Before reuse, compare the declared dimensions, pattern, matrix type, and permutation with the cache key; on any mismatch, invalidate the cache and repeat symbolic analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cache ordering and elimination structure for fixed-pattern systems, refactor only numerical values, and invalidate the cache whenever structural metadata changes.
assumptions_latex: All matrices accepted by one cache entry share an identical declared sparsity pattern.
The numerical factorization method is compatible with the cached matrix type and permutation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every valid cache hit, symbolic analysis is reused while the numerical factors are recomputed for the current \(K_k\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the leaf, but identical input sparsity alone does not guarantee an unchanged numerical factor structure when dynamic pivoting is permitted. A sparse-factorization source and an explicit pivoting-compatible reuse condition are needed.

children.title: Numeric Refactorization Reuse
children.top_down_role: Reuse opportunities for numerical factorization work under changing coefficient values.

assumptions_latex: The repeated convex QPs have KKT matrices \(K_k\in\mathbb{S}^N\) with a common sparsity pattern.
A symbolic elimination ordering and symbolic factorization for that pattern have already been computed.
Each numerical factorization is performed only when \(K_k\) satisfies the solver's regularity and pivoting requirements.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The symbolic data may be retained while the numerical factors are recomputed from the current coefficients of \(K_k\).

notation.meaning: KKT matrix for the QP at repetition index k

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard two-stage sparse direct-factorization procedure
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sparse direct solution of repeated convex-QP KKT systems with unchanged structural pattern.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a sequence \((K_k)_{k\geq 0}\) whose matrices share the structural nonzero set \(\mathcal S\), first compute an ordering and symbolic elimination structure from \(\mathcal S\). For each \(k\), insert the current numerical entries into that structure and compute fresh numerical factors, such as \(P K_k P^{\mathsf T}=L_kD_kL_k^{\mathsf T}\), without repeating symbolic analysis. Solve the current KKT equations with \(L_k\) and \(D_k\). Numerical factors from an earlier index are not reused as exact factors unless the relevant coefficients are unchanged; only their symbolic storage and ordering are reused.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reuse ordering and symbolic storage across fixed-pattern KKT systems, but recompute numerical factors whenever matrix coefficients change.
knowledge_statements.title: Numeric Refactorization Reuse

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm and content kind fit numeric refactorization reuse, but no inspectable source supports the stated symbolic-reuse, pivoting, and cache-validity conditions.

children.title: Fixed-Pattern Sequence Eligibility
children.top_down_role: QP sequence structures compatible with persistent sparse-factorization resources.

assumptions_latex: Every QP in the sequence uses fixed variable and constraint dimensions \(n\) and \(m\).
The solver represents matrices using declared structural nonzero sets, including any stored zeros required by its interface.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sequence is fixed-pattern eligible exactly when its declared matrix structures are independent of the repetition index.

notation.meaning: quadratic and constraint matrices at repetition index k

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: fixed sparse-pattern eligibility is defined by invariant dimensions and declared sparsity
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eligibility criterion for symbolic-factorization reuse across a sequence of solver-facing QPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For QPs \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}P_kx+q_k^{\mathsf T}x\) subject to \(l_k\leq A_kx\leq u_k\), the sequence is fixed-pattern eligible when \(n\) and \(m\) are constant and there exist fixed sets \(\mathcal S_P\) and \(\mathcal S_A\) such that \(\operatorname{pat}(P_k)=\mathcal S_P\) and \(\operatorname{pat}(A_k)=\mathcal S_A\) for every \(k\). Values in those positions may change, including becoming numerically zero, provided the declared storage pattern remains unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A QP sequence is eligible when dimensions and declared matrix sparsity remain fixed, although stored coefficient values may vary.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Pattern Sequence Eligibility

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the leaf, but eligibility based on declared patterns, stored zeros, and exact pattern equality is solver-interface-specific and has no cited support.

children.title: Factorization Cache Invalidation
children.top_down_role: Structural or numerical changes that require cached factorization resources to be rebuilt.

assumptions_latex: A cache contains symbolic or numerical factorization state derived from a matrix \(K\).
The solver can identify which dimensions, structural indices, coefficients, ordering rules, and numerical settings generated that state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Cached state must be discarded whenever a changed dependency makes that state inconsistent with the current KKT system.

notation.meaning: matrix from which cached factorization state was derived
declared structural nonzero pattern of a matrix

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: cache validity follows from equality of all structural and numerical dependencies
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity boundary for symbolic and numerical caches used by repeated sparse KKT solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A symbolic-factorization cache for \(K\) is invalid if the matrix dimension, \(\operatorname{pat}(K)\), ordering policy, or symbolic-analysis settings change. A numerical-factor cache is additionally invalid if any coefficient affecting \(K\), any regularization or scaling entering \(K\), or any pivoting condition requiring a different factorization changes. Changes confined to right-hand sides preserve both caches, while coefficient changes with fixed structure may preserve only the symbolic cache. Reuse is valid only for cache components whose complete generating dependencies remain unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Invalidate symbolic caches after structural changes and numerical caches after coefficient-dependent changes; right-hand-side changes alone preserve both.
knowledge_statements.title: Factorization Cache Invalidation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits cache invalidation, but the asserted effects of coefficient, scaling, regularization, pivoting, and right-hand-side changes require an authoritative sparse-solver reference.

children.title: Incremental QP Data-Update Interface
children.top_down_role: Incremental replacement of QP data without complete solver reconstruction.

children.title: Matrix Coefficient Updates
children.top_down_role: Replacement of quadratic or affine matrix values between related QP solves.

assumptions_latex: The QP has the form \(\min_x\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Px+q^{\mathsf T}x\) subject to \(l\leq Ax\leq u\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A matrix update replaces \((P,A)\) by \((P^+,A^+)\) and thereby defines a new convex QP with unchanged dimensions.

notation.meaning: cone of symmetric positive semidefinite n by n matrices

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct data replacement in a parametrized convex QP
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full matrix-value replacement in a dimension-preserving incremental convex-QP interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed \(n\) and \(m\), a matrix coefficient update supplies \(P^+\in\mathbb S_+^n\) and \(A^+\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), replacing \(P\) and \(A\) while retaining \(q\), \(l\), and \(u\) unless those data are separately updated. The resulting problem is \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}P^+x+q^{\mathsf T}x\) subject to \(l\leq A^+x\leq u\). Preservation of cached symbolic state requires the declared patterns of the updated matrices to remain compatible with the original patterns.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matrix update replaces Hessian or constraint coefficients without changing QP dimensions; positive semidefiniteness preserves convexity.
knowledge_statements.title: Matrix Coefficient Updates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition matches full matrix coefficient replacement, but the update and symbolic-cache compatibility semantics are uncited and depend on the solver interface.

children.title: Vector Data Updates
children.top_down_role: Replacement of objective vectors, right-hand sides, or bound vectors.

assumptions_latex: The matrices \(P\in\mathbb S_+^n\) and \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) remain fixed.
Each component of the new bounds satisfies \(l_i^+\leq u_i^+\), allowing infinite endpoints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A vector update replaces any selected members of \((q,l,u)\) without changing the QP matrices or dimensions.

notation.meaning: linear objective and lower and upper bound vectors
extended real line used for unbounded constraint sides

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct vector-data replacement in a fixed-matrix convex QP
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-linear-term and bound updates with fixed QP matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A vector data update replaces one or more of \(q\in\mathbb R^n\), \(l\in\overline{\mathbb R}^m\), and \(u\in\overline{\mathbb R}^m\) by \(q^+\), \(l^+\), and \(u^+\), respectively, while leaving \(P\) and \(A\) unchanged. The updated QP is \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Px+(q^+)^{\mathsf T}x\) subject to \(l^+\leq Ax\leq u^+\), with every unchanged vector interpreted as retaining its previous value. Such an update changes KKT right-hand-side data but not the matrix sparsity structure.

children.title: Partial Sparse Updates
children.top_down_role: Indexed modification of selected entries within solver-held sparse data.

assumptions_latex: A matrix or vector datum is stored with a fixed indexing convention.
The supplied update indices are valid and each replacement value has the scalar type required by the QP data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only entries selected by the update index set change; all other entries retain their prior values.

Matrix indices are interpreted in the solver's declared sparse-storage ordering, including its symmetry convention for \(P\). After the scatter operation, validate convexity and bound consistency where applicable, invalidate every numerical state depending on changed values, and output the updated QP data object.

children.title: Fixed-Pattern Update Regimes
children.top_down_role: Incremental interfaces restricted to unchanged matrix sparsity patterns.

assumptions_latex: QP dimensions \(n\) and \(m\) remain constant throughout the update sequence.
Sparse matrices use declared patterns that distinguish structural positions from numerical nonzeros.

notation.meaning: matrix data at update index k
fixed declared patterns of the Hessian and constraint matrix

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural restriction governing incremental sparse-matrix updates and symbolic reuse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An incremental QP update sequence is in a fixed-pattern regime if fixed sets \(\mathcal S_P\) and \(\mathcal S_A\) satisfy \(\operatorname{pat}(P_k)=\mathcal S_P\) and \(\operatorname{pat}(A_k)=\mathcal S_A\) for every update index \(k\). Coefficients stored at those positions may take arbitrary admissible values, including zero. Inserting a coefficient at an undeclared position, deleting a declared position from the storage structure, or changing either matrix dimension leaves the fixed-pattern regime and requires structural reanalysis.

children.title: Solver-State Invalidation
children.top_down_role: Update classes that invalidate cached analysis, factors, scaling, or warm-start state.

assumptions_latex: Solver state is partitioned into components with identifiable dependencies on QP data and algorithmic settings.
An accepted update changes a known subset of matrix entries, vector entries, dimensions, patterns, scaling, or settings.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every state component depending on changed data is invalid; a component independent of all changed data may remain valid.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependency rule for retaining or discarding internal state after incremental QP updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D(s)\) be the complete set of QP data and settings from which a solver-state component \(s\) was constructed, and let \(U\) be the set changed by an update. The component is invalid whenever \(D(s)\cap U\neq\varnothing\), unless the solver establishes an update formula that transforms \(s\) consistently to the new data. Thus matrix changes ordinarily invalidate numerical factors and residual products; structural changes also invalidate symbolic analysis; and vector-only changes may preserve matrix factorizations. A retained iterate is a warm-start candidate, not a certificate of feasibility or optimality for the updated QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Discard each internal state component whose dependencies changed, unless a validated update formula brings that component into consistency.
knowledge_statements.title: Solver-State Invalidation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits solver-state invalidation, but its universal dependency rule and examples concerning factors, residual products, symbolic analysis, and warm starts need authoritative support.

children.title: Embedded QP Code Generation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operator-based access to large convex QPs for iterative, non-direct solution methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A matrix-free interface for \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Px+q^{\mathsf T}x\) subject to \(l\leq Ax\leq u\) supplies callbacks \(\mathcal P(v)=Pv\), \(\mathcal A(v)=Av\), and, when required, \(\mathcal A^*(w)=A^{\mathsf T}w\), together with \(q\), \(l\), and \(u\). It need not expose the entries or sparse storage of \(P\) and \(A\). Preconditioner actions may be supplied separately, but they must state the operator they approximate and must not silently alter the represented QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matrix-free QP interface provides Hessian, constraint, and adjoint products to an iterative solver without storing explicit matrices.
knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Free Large-Scale QP Interfaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and content kind fit the matrix-free interface leaf, but the required callbacks, adjoint access, and preconditioner obligations need an authoritative large-scale QP or solver-interface reference.
